Being bullied by a foster mother was nothing. The real disaster would come after she married into the Prince Anjing’s residence, when Prince Anjing himself turned against her.

As she pondered, she looked up and saw Xie Jingyu enter Shengju Hall.

Dressed in a light moon-white robe, his scholarly demeanor was evident. His long strides showed that he was in a very good mood.

---

chapters.title: Xie Jingyu Drinks Medicine
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu strode in.

The maidservants all bowed and served him clear tea.

"You seem to be in a good mood, husband," Yun Chu said, looking at him. "Has something good happened?"

Xie Jingyu drank half a cup of tea, a smile appearing on his face: "Ping sister’s dowry is almost ready."

Yun Chu smiled as well: "I knew there would be no problem leaving this task to you. I’ll tell Ping sister the good news later."

"There’s another piece of good news," Xie Jingyu’s smile deepened. "The Emperor has ordered a re-investigation into the Crown Prince’s serious illness. Prince Anjing has been cleared of the charges and will be able to return to the capital tomorrow."

Although not many people knew about Prince Anjing being punished and sent to Qing’an Temple, it was still not a good thing.

Previously, he had been worried that the Emperor might revoke Prince Anjing’s title. Now, it seemed he had worried too much.

Three months after Ping sister’s marriage to Prince Anjing, the Xie family would officially become royal in-laws.

The Marquis of Xuanwu would no longer be able to make things difficult for him.

His face was filled with joy, but he noticed Yun Chu’s brows slowly furrowing.

He knew Yun Chu was the most beautiful woman in the capital, but he had never realized how beautiful she looked when worried.

But now was not the time to admire her beauty. He asked, "Wife, is there a problem?"

Yun Chu shook her head: "Prince Anjing being cleared of the charges may be a good thing for him, but for our Xie family..."

She didn’t continue, but Xie Jingyu was a clever man and understood her implication.

The reason the Xie family had been able to secure the position of princess consort was because Prince Anjing had made a mistake and was punished. He hadn’t dared to make a fuss, allowing the Xie family to exploit the situation.

"If it’s come to this, so be it," Xie Jingyu said, a hint of hidden worry appearing between his brows. "Moreover, it was the Emperor’s personal decree to bestow the marriage. Can Consort De still go back on her word?"

Yun Chu spoke: "The Emperor’s decree is absolute. Consort De naturally won’t go back on her word. It’s just that... Ping sister is likely..."

Xie Jingyu’s expression was indifferent: "This is the path she chose herself. Even if she has to crawl, she must walk it to the end."

As expected, the next morning, Tang Mama from Consort De’s palace came to the Xie family to request Xie Pin’s presence in the palace.

Once again, Xie Jingyu was convinced by Yun Chu’s foresight. His wife seemed to have calculated every step. With Yun Chu in the Xie family, what was there to worry about in rising to prominence...

Xie Pin followed Tang Mama and Foster Mother Fu into the palace.

She carefully remembered Foster Mother Fu’s teachings, keeping her head slightly lowered and walking carefully, trying to ensure her skirt did not sway in the slightest...

After nearly half an hour, they finally arrived at Changqing Palace, where Consort De resided.

She ascended the steps and entered the palace hall, performing a standard palace greeting: "This humble subject greets Consort De."

Not hearing Consort De’s command to rise, she maintained the posture. After about the time it took to drink a cup of tea, she saw a pair of feet walking toward her. Soon, they stopped in front of her. Then, her chin was lifted by fingers adorned with golden nails.

The sharp golden nails poked into her flesh, causing her to frown in pain.

She was forced to lift her head and met a beautiful face. Even though she had never entered the palace before, she knew this was Consort De.

"Miss Xie, you have such audacity! You’ve even schemed against me!" Consort De abruptly pushed her away.

Caught off guard, Xie Pin was thrown to the ground.

She didn’t dare to get up, shifting from lying prostrate to kneeling on the ground. She spoke, "Your Highness, this humble subject knows her mistake. I and the Prince are mutually in love, unable to control our feelings, so..."

Hearing the words "unable to control our feelings," Consort De was so enraged she almost exploded. She lifted her foot and kicked Xie Pin hard.

The Xie family was truly cunning. They hadn’t acted too early or too late but had chosen this exact moment when Lao Si was punished and sent to Qing’an Temple, forcing her to agree to this marriage.

If she had hesitated for a few more days, Lao Si would have been cleared of the charges. How could the Xie family have manipulated the situation to this extent?

Xie Pin was kicked over.

A thirteen-year-old girl couldn’t withstand such a kick and immediately struggled to breathe.

Consort De coldly said, "Miss Xie of the Xie family has offended me. Foster Mother Fu, slap her for me."

Foster Mother Fu stepped forward and delivered a series of slaps with both hands. After more than twenty slaps, Xie Pin’s face swelled.

The pain was so intense she nearly fainted, and tears streamed down her face.

"What bad luck," Consort De said with a look of disgust. "Crying like this; do you think I’ve wronged you? Go stand outside. You may come back in when you’ve figured it out."

Xie Pin couldn’t even stand steadily. She was supported by palace maids and pushed to the entrance of Changqing Palace’s main hall.

There was not a single tree here, only white jade stone under the blazing sun, which was so hot it made her dizzy.

She had arrived in the morning, and now it was almost noon. Her stomach was empty, and the scorching sun seemed to melt her.

She didn’t know how long she stood there before her vision blurred, and she collapsed.

The palace maid standing nearby coldly pulled her up: "Miss Xie, stand properly. If you anger Consort De, it won’t be as simple as just standing as punishment."

Xie Pin felt the maid’s nails digging into her flesh. The pain had numbed her.

She wanted to cry.

She didn’t understand why, as the future princess consort, she had to endure such torment and humiliation.

Why could a mere palace maid treat her like this?

If she had agreed earlier to become Prince Anjing’s concubine, as a concubine, she might have suffered even crueler treatment.

Just as she was in despair, she saw a tall figure entering the gates of Changqing Palace.

She looked up and saw Prince Anjing.

Her eyes instantly sparkled with hope, and she stared intently at the approaching man.

Prince Anjing’s gaze lingered on her for only a brief moment before he continued walking without stopping, ascending the steps and entering Consort De’s palace hall.

He admitted he had some interest in Miss Xie, but it was merely physical. His willingness to take responsibility meant he could accept her as a concubine.

But she, ungrateful, had refused even the position of a concubine and instead forced his mother to agree to marry her as the principal consort.

Marrying the illegitimate daughter of a fifth-rank official as his principal consort would make him the biggest joke in the entire capital.

Watching Prince Anjing’s cold back as he entered the main hall, despair slowly spread across Xie Pin’s face...

Once again, she felt relieved that she was the future princess consort. Even if the prince didn’t favor her, he would still have to take her to palace banquets and produce a legitimate heir with her...

Xie Pin was allowed to leave the palace in the evening.

The people of the Xie family, seeing that she had not returned for a long time, were all worried sick. They had sent someone to wait at the gate. As soon as she entered, she was taken to Anshou Hall.

"Heavens, what happened to your face..." He Shi was the first to exclaim. "Who, who hit you? You are the future Princess Consort Anjing. This is disrespectful to Prince Anjing!"

Xie Pin’s nose twinged, and she buried her face in He Shi’s arms, sobbing loudly.

The old madam anxiously asked, "Ping sister, who laid a hand on you?"

"Who else could it be?" Yun Chu’s voice was extremely calm. "Naturally, it was Consort De."

chapters.title: Tingshuang's Marriage
chapters.content:
Xie Pin nodded through her tears.

For a moment, An Shou Hall fell silent.

Although everyone knew that Eldest Sister Pin’s future days would not be easy, no one had expected that, before even entering the marital home, she would be beaten to this state by her future mother-in-law.

They say you should never strike someone’s face, but the Virtuous Consort had deliberately ordered someone to slap Eldest Sister Pin, this was a message to the Xie family: their schemes against Prince Anjing would not be left unpunished.

"Zhou Mama, bring the swelling-relief ointment for Eldest Sister Pin." The Old Madam sighed. "When you were scheming against Prince Anjing, you should have anticipated this day would come."

Xie Jingyu’s voice was low: "The Virtuous Consort is better than those who use underhanded tactics in secret. If we deserve this, then we must endure it."

Xie Shian lifted his gaze: "No matter how the Virtuous Consort treats you, you are still the future Princess Consort of Anjing. No one can change that."

Xie Pin cried even harder.

Even her own family couldn’t stand up for her; what was she supposed to do?

"Eldest Sister Pin." Yun Chu spoke softly. "If our Xie family finds a proper reason to call off the marriage, the Virtuous Consort will surely agree. Then you won’t have to suffer like this anymore."

"Call off the marriage?" Xie Pin lifted her tear-blurred eyes. "I, I don’t want to call it off."

This was something she had schemed so hard to obtain. She had endured so much suffering, yet she hadn’t even tasted the glory of being a princess consort. How could she bear to give it up?

"Chu’er, what nonsense are you spouting?" The Old Madam’s face darkened. "Eldest Sister Pin’s marriage to Prince Anjing was decreed by His Majesty. Calling it off would be defying the imperial decree, a crime our Xie family cannot afford."

Xie Jingyu nodded: "We cannot call it off."

Yun Chu pulled Xie Pin closer, speaking slowly and clearly: "Before the wedding, you still have the chance to back out. No matter which path you choose, your mother will support you. Remember, as long as I am here, you will always have a way out."

Xie Pin’s nose twinged, and tears welled up again.

Everyone in the Xie family placed the clan’s honor above all else. Only her mother truly considered her, her daughter.

What great virtue had she accumulated in her past life to be blessed with such a mother in this one?

After leaving An Shou Hall, Xie Jingyu caught up to Yun Chu and couldn’t help but ask: "Madam, do you truly want to call off Eldest Sister Pin’s marriage?"

"Of course not." Yun Chu replied. "Eldest Sister Pin is enduring the Virtuous Consort’s harassment for the sake of the Xie family. If everyone in the Xie family believes this is the suffering she deserves and treats her with cold indifference, then after she marries into Prince Anjing’s estate, would she still scheme for the Xie family?"

Xie Jingyu had an epiphany: "Madam is indeed wise."

Yun Chu’s expression remained impassive as she continued toward Shengju Courtyard.

Xie Jingyu followed her into Shengju. He pressed his lips together and asked: "I only just learned that last time, my mother-in-law took you to see the divine physician. What did the divine physician say?"

"The divine physician said I need to regulate my body. He prescribed a few remedies for me to take." Yun Chu turned her gaze to the side. "A consultation with the divine physician costs five thousand taels of silver. Husband, in your opinion, who should pay for this?"

"Any child you bear in the future will be a legitimate heir of the Xie family. Naturally, the Xie family should cover the cost." Xie Jingyu took over the conversation. "I’ll have someone deliver the consultation fee to my mother-in-law later."

Five thousand taels was no small sum for him, but fortunately, as the future father-in-law of Prince Anjing, he had plenty of ways to obtain that much silver.

He took a slow step toward Yun Chu, placing his hand on her shoulder: "Madam, I’ll stay in Shengju tonight."

Yun Chu felt a wave of nausea.

She took a step back, evading Xie Jingyu’s touch, and moved to the side table: "The divine physician said that both husband and wife must regulate their bodies. During this period, we must not share a bed."

She handed the packet of medicine on the table to Xie Jingyu.

Xie Jingyu felt a weight in his hand: "I have to drink this too?"

Yun Chu nodded: "Of course. If my lord does not wish to have more children, he may refuse."

At this point, Xie Jingyu knew that if he refused to regulate his body, his marital relationship with Yun Chu would truly come to an end.

Once their bodies were regulated, he and Yun Chu should be able to have a child truly their own.

He looked deeply at Yun Chu, took the medicine, and left for his own courtyard.

Tingshuang stood to the side, confused: "Madam, what is this about?"

She knew that Physician Si had not prescribed any medicine for the master. In fact, even the medicine prescribed for Madam had been torn up and thrown away by Madam herself.

She was well aware that Madam had no intention of regulating her body, nor did she plan to have another child with the master.

But why had she given the master so much medicine?

She truly did not understand what Madam was trying to do.

Yun Chu’s expression remained blank: "The Xie family has enough children. This medicine can solve many troubles."

Currently, the Xie family had five children: Eldest Young Lady Xie Pin, Second Young Lady Xie Xian, Eldest Young Master Xie Shian, Second Young Master Xie Shiwei, and Third Young Master Xie Shiyun. Concubine Tao was also carrying another young master in her belly... In the future, there would be even more concubines in the Xie mansion, each giving birth to sons, Fourth Young Master, Fifth Young Master, Sixth Young Master...

Thinking of the terrible things these children would do in the future, Yun Chu’s chest filled with hatred.

Rather than waiting for those children to bring her ruin, it was better to address the problem at its source.

As long as Xie Jingyu could not father any more children, it would save her countless troubles.

Tingshuang was utterly shocked.

She didn’t know how to describe her feelings.

However, she soon had no time to dwell on this shock.

Because Yun Chu’s next words left her no room to think of anything else.

"Tingshuang, I’ve asked my mother to find someone for you." Yun Chu said. "Tomorrow morning, we’ll return home. See if you approve of him."

"Husband... Madam..." Tingshuang’s face paled. "This servant does not wish to marry. I want to stay by Madam’s side and serve you for the rest of my life..."

"If I let you remain unmarried and childless for your entire life, one day you will come to resent me." Yun Chu said gently. "Tingshuang, you and I are the same age. I have already been married for five years. I cannot delay your life any longer."

Tingshuang bit her lower lip.

Madam had already secretly distanced herself from the Xie family. She didn’t dare to imagine what would become of Madam in the future.

If she left Madam’s side, who would be left to assist Madam?

Chen Bo was in the outer courtyard, Tingxue was too honest, and Tingfeng was too impulsive. In the future, when Madam needed to handle private matters, who would do it for her?

But Tingshuang said nothing more. When they returned to the Yun family the next day and she met that person, she would simply say she disapproved.

No matter what, she would not leave Madam.

Later that evening, Tingxue came to report: "The master ordered the maids to decoct the medicine, and he drank all of it."

Yun Chu nodded: "There’s no need to keep watch anymore."

One dose would be enough.

She had someone clean up the dregs. Any medicine decocted afterward would be the genuine remedy for regulating a man’s body.

The next morning, Yun Chu took Tingshuang and Tingfeng to the Yun family.

Along the way, Tingshuang nervously twisted her fingers, while Tingfeng, carefree as ever, looked out the carriage window and said: "Madam, look! There’s such a long line outside the ice shop."

Yun Chu glanced over and saw that the ice shops under different West family brands all had long queues of servants from wealthy families waiting to purchase ice.

---

chapters.title: I Don’t Like Her
chapters.content:
Because the ice shops were so popular, and there were still several months of heat ahead, she and Manager Chen had decided to set a daily sales limit.

By noon, the ice shops would usually be sold out.

As a result, the wealthy families had no choice but to send their people to line up early.

On the streets, many people were discussing the Summer Retreat Courtyard.

"I used to be puzzled, ice is just made from water, so why is it so expensive? But after visiting Madam Yun’s Summer Retreat Courtyard, I finally understood why ice is worth its weight in gold during this scorching summer."

"Don’t even mention it. In all my years, this is the first time I’ve experienced the joy of using ice in the summer. I truly have to thank Madam Yun."

"Huh? What is this Summer Retreat Courtyard you’re talking about?"

"How can you not know about something so big? It’s in Guihua Alley in the west of the city. At the end of the alley, there’s a courtyard that opens for a couple of hours every afternoon. Anyone can enter to escape the heat. I don’t know how much ice they’ve put in there, but the moment you step inside, it feels like winter. It’s so refreshing!"

"Heavens, an entire courtyard filled with ice blocks? That must cost a fortune. Is the Yun family that rich?"

"The Yun family has produced three great generals. They are a true aristocratic family. Of course they can afford the silver for ice. Speaking of which, there are countless wealthy families in the capital, but only the Yun family uses their silver to do good for the common people. Madam Yun is truly a living Bodhisattva."

"General Yun is at the front lines defending our nation, and Madam Yun is spending silver to help the common people stay cool. The Yun family loves the people and pities all things; they should be a model for all officials."

"I heard General Yun is about to return to the capital in triumph! Our great general is coming home!"

"How wonderful! How wonderful!"

...

The common people cheered.

Yun Chu felt a pang of emotion.

She had only placed some crushed ice in the courtyard for people to rest in for free. The cost wasn’t actually that high, yet it had earned such high praise from the common people.

The simple and honest common folk were like this; if you gave them even the slightest bit, they would remember it in their hearts.

They would risk everything for you in your darkest hour.

However, the power of the common people was too insignificant. In her past life, even when tens of thousands of commoners had pleaded for mercy, it had not been enough to sway the Emperor’s decision against the Yun family.

The carriage soon stopped in front of the Yun mansion.

The moment she stepped out, Tingshuang grew tense.

As she walked in, she immediately noticed a young man standing in Madam Lin’s courtyard.

When he saw her enter, the young man slightly tilted his head, stealing a quick glance before quickly looking away.

"Regarding the matter I just instructed you on, handle it as discussed. You may leave for now." Madam Lin told the young man to withdraw, then turned to Yun Chu. "That was Mama Yu’s youngest son. He’s currently gaining experience under a deputy general who serves under your father. What do you think?"

Yun Chu looked at Tingshuang.

Tingshuang lowered her head, thinking of how to refuse.

Then Madam Lin said: "Tingshuang, you and Chu’er grew up together. I treat your marriage as seriously as I would Chu’er’s. If you’re not satisfied, just shake your head. There’s no need to force yourself out of any pressure. If you don’t like this one, I’ll find you another. There are many fine young men in the Yun family army. We can take our time."

Tingshuang: "..."

In other words, if she rejected this one, there would be countless others waiting.

She couldn’t possibly reject each and every one, wouldn’t that break Madam Yun’s heart?

"Slave... I..." Tingshuang’s mouth turned bitter. "I don’t know."

"It’s true, deciding after just one glance is too rushed." Madam Lin smiled. "Chu’er, when you return to the Xie family later, take Yu Ke with you. Let him get to know Tingshuang better, and then we’ll make a decision."

Yun Chu nodded: "I am indeed short on help. Having Yu Ke assist me with some matters in the outer courtyard will also lighten Chen Bo’s load."

And so, the matter was settled.

During the meal, Yun Chu brought up the Summer Retreat Courtyard: "...The Yun family’s Summer Retreat Courtyard has benefited many poor commoners. Now, the common people hold the Yun family in too high regard. I don’t know if this is a blessing or a curse. We need to find a way to tone it down."

She truly hadn’t expected such a small Summer Retreat Courtyard to elicit such a strong reaction from the common people. Anything taken to extremes would backfire.

Liu Qianqian set down her chopsticks: "Although the Yun family did this to benefit the people, some may see it as currying favor with the masses. Right now, the Yun family is at its peak. One wrong move and..."

Madam Lin shook her head: "You two are overthinking. The Yun family has been loyal for generations. The Emperor’s trust in our family is as vast as a flowing river. He would never turn against us."

She knew the Emperor harbored some wariness toward the Yun family, which was why the Yun family had married their children to lower statuses, avoiding alliances with other noble families. The eldest son had not pursued a military career, and they had intentionally performed poorly in the imperial examinations. The Emperor’s wariness should have gradually faded.

Yun Chu gave a bitter smile.

She had once believed the same.

But the truth had proven that a martial family that threatened imperial authority was doomed to only one fate.

"This summer is too hot. Without the Summer Retreat Courtyard, who knows how many people would die from the heat." Madam Lin said. "The Emperor’s suspicions are intangible, but the people dying from heat are real. Should we just stand by and watch so many commoners perish because of something that hasn’t even happened yet?"

Yun Chu knew that even if she hadn’t taken the initiative to establish the Summer Retreat Courtyard, her mother would have unconditionally helped those suffering from heatstroke.

"I have an idea." She said. "We can open another shop inside the Summer Retreat Courtyard. With so many people coming and going every afternoon, the shop will naturally do some business. This way, we can let the Emperor believe that the Yun family is using the Summer Retreat Courtyard to make a little money. Mother, Elder Sister-in-law, what do you think?"

Madam Lin’s eyes lit up: "That truly is a good idea."

Liu Qianqian nodded in agreement: "Then I’ll take care of this matter."

If she, a woman, handled these financial matters, the Emperor would be even less likely to say anything.

Yun Chu trusted her elder sister-in-law completely.

Her elder sister-in-law was the legitimate eldest daughter of the distinguished Liu family. The Liu family was a true scholarly clan, and her elder sister-in-law carried the bearing of a literary family. After the Yun family’s downfall, she had torn up the divorce letter her husband had given her, swearing to live and die with the Yun family...

After finishing their meal at the Yun family, Yun Chu prepared to return.

When they had arrived, there had been three of them, mistress and two servants. When they left, they had an additional young man named Yu Ke.

Yun Chu, Tingshuang, and Tingfeng sat inside the carriage, while the coachman sat outside with Yu Ke beside him. Occasionally, they could hear the coachman and Yu Ke talking.

Tingshuang’s expression was calm, but her mind was racing. After about ten days or half a month, she would find Madam and refuse this match. Her unwillingness to marry was her own business; she couldn’t delay someone else’s chance at starting a family.

As the carriage traveled along, Tingfeng suddenly spoke up: "Madam, I think I just saw the young heir of Prince Pingxi’s estate."

Yun Chu immediately looked over.

Sure enough, she saw a small child, surrounded by several servants, walking down the street.

chapters.title: The Young Master Falls into the Water
chapters.content:
The streets were bustling with people.

Chu Hongyu pouted, clearly displeased.

A Mao bent over and whispered, "Your Highness, at least pretend to enjoy the outing. Otherwise, when the Prince asks, you won’t even have an excuse for disliking her, will you?"

Chu Hongyu looked up at the woman standing beside him.

She was the second daughter of the Tan family, a candidate for the future princess consort, chosen by many in the household, including his father. She was to be the mother of both him and Changsheng.

He and Changsheng did want a mother, but not this woman.

This woman was gentle, her words and actions flawless. Everyone in the household, including his father, was very fond of her.

Only after everyone was satisfied did they ask him if he would allow this woman to become his stepmother.

"Yu Ge’er, do you like this sugar figurine?" Miss Tan picked up a cute tiger-shaped sugar figurine from the stall and handed it to Chu Hongyu.

She wore a gentle smile, bending down to close the distance between them.

"I don’t like it! It’s ugly!" Chu Hongyu coldly threw out these words and strode forward.

Miss Tan felt helpless.

She had racked her brains to please the young master, but he had kept a straight face the entire time, clearly disliking her.

Whether her marriage to Prince Pingxi would be settled depended entirely on whether the young master liked her or not.

She was only seventeen and didn’t want to be a stepmother, but her father needed Prince Pingxi’s support to advance his official rank.

For her father, for her family, she had to go through with it.

"Yu Ge’er, then what do you like?" Miss Tan put on her gentle smile again. "I heard you like crickets. How about I take you to watch a cricket fight?"

Chu Hongyu felt a flicker of interest but immediately scolded himself in his mind.

Since he didn’t like this woman, he shouldn’t give her any hope, nor should he let his father think he was willing to accept her as his stepmother.

He coldly stated, "Miss Tan, don’t waste your effort. No matter what you do, I will never agree to let you marry my father!"

Miss Tan’s smile froze. She took a deep breath, crouched down, and took Chu Hongyu’s small hand in hers. "Yu Ge’er, I know you feel some resistance toward me now, but please trust me. I will treat you as my own child. I will love you and Changsheng and let you know how different life is with a mother… Your father will marry a princess consort someday. It might not matter who he marries, but I can promise you this: I will not have any more children with your father. The Prince Pingxi’s residence will only have you and Changsheng as his children…"

Chu Hongyu bit his lower lip.

He found his heart wavering slightly.

If even he was moved by this woman’s words, his father would certainly find it even harder to resist.

If no faults could be found in her, the Emperor would soon bestow the marriage, and this woman would truly become his stepmother.

At this thought, Chu Hongyu felt a surge of resistance.

"Yu Ge’er, can we give it a try?" Miss Tan held the child’s hand, her eyes clear.

At that moment, Chu Hongyu suddenly let out a piercing scream and violently pushed Miss Tan away.

"She pinched me!" The little boy, tears welling in his eyes, hid behind his wet nurse. "She just pinched my hand and threatened me to agree to let her be my stepmother. Waaah!"

He burst into tears.

Miss Tan’s eyes widened. She had only gently held the young master’s hand, not daring to use any force. How could she have pinched a child?

Before she could explain, the wet nurse holding Chu Hongyu angrily declared, "Miss Tan, how dare you! To treat our young master like this, threatening him before even entering our household. Who knows how you’ll torment the children once you become the princess consort. I will definitely report this to the Prince!"

Miss Tan’s face paled. "Wet Nurse, I didn’t! How would I dare lay a hand on the young master? I truly didn’t… Yu Ge’er, quickly tell the wet nurse the truth. I really didn’t touch you!"

Chu Hongyu sobbed, "My hand is all red! It was you who pinched me. You’re a bad person. I hate you!"

The wet nurse took a look and saw that the young master’s fair hand was indeed red.

Miss Tan felt for the first time what it meant to be framed so thoroughly that even jumping into the Yellow River wouldn’t wash her clean. But even if it was hard to explain, she had to make things clear...

Just as she was about to speak, a figure appeared in her line of sight.

She looked up and recognized her, Yun Chu, the legitimate daughter of the General’s mansion, now Madam Xie.

Yun Chu had not intended to get out of the carriage, but while sitting inside, she had seen the entire exchange between Yu Ge’er and Miss Tan clearly.

If it were any other child, no matter how naughty or deceitful, she wouldn’t have interfered.

But the child lying and framing someone was Yu Ge’er.

The child who had sneaked into the Xie residence just to see her. The child who had earnestly carved a wooden sculpture for her. The child whose heart was always filled with thoughts of her... She couldn’t stand by and watch him make a mistake without doing anything.

"Nurse Zheng." Yun Chu greeted Chu Hongyu’s wet nurse, her gaze falling on the child clinging to the nurse. "Young Master, is your hand really red because Miss Tan pinched you?"

At the moment Yun Chu appeared, Chu Hongyu’s eyes lit up with a huge spark. Instinctively, he wanted to pounce into her arms.

But he noticed that Yun Chu’s expression was very serious. Children were perceptive, and he sensed that Yun Chu’s mood was related to him.

He grabbed the wet nurse’s clothes, avoiding Yun Chu’s gaze, and pursed his lips without answering.

"Madam Xie, what do you mean by that?" Nurse Zheng frowned. "Are you suggesting that our young master is framing Miss Tan?"

"Yu Ge’er." Yun Chu fixed her gaze on the child. "Didn’t I tell you before? It’s okay to make mistakes, but the most important thing is to admit them."

Miss Tan let out a huge sigh of relief.

She truly hadn’t expected that Madam Xie would risk offending the young master to stand up for her.

If it were someone else, even if they saw the young master framing her, they definitely wouldn’t choose to side with her...

Chu Hongyu bit his lower lip.

He knew he shouldn’t have framed Miss Tan, but if he didn’t do this, this woman would become his stepmother.

He didn’t want this woman to be his mother.

He looked at Yun Chu, wishing that she could marry his father. But why had she married someone else so early...

Yun Chu softened her voice. "Yu Ge’er, if you know you were wrong, then apologize. I think Miss Tan would be willing to forgive you."

"No, I wasn’t wrong." Chu Hongyu shouted, his eyes red. "She was the one who bullied me. And now you’re bullying me with her. I hate you both!"

He jumped down from the wet nurse and dashed into the crowd.

"Oh dear, my little ancestor, don’t run around! Don’t get lost!" Nurse Zheng was terrified. "What are you all standing around for? Go after him!"

The servants of Prince Pingxi’s residence rushed in the direction where Chu Hongyu had disappeared.

Yun Chu didn’t hesitate for a second. She lifted her skirt and chased after him.

Miss Tan’s head was about to explode. It was she who had suggested taking the young master out for a stroll. If he got lost, her Tan family would be doomed.

---

chapters.title: Her Heart Like Still Water
chapters.content:
Though the child’s legs were short, he ran exceptionally fast.

After darting into the crowd, he ran straight in one direction and soon ran out of the city gate.

Outside the city, though there were fewer people, the area was filled with grass and trees. The servants of Prince Pingxi’s residence split into two groups to search in different directions.

"Madam Xie, what should we do?" Miss Tan was so anxious she was pacing in circles. "If something happens to the young master, my life won’t be enough to make amends."

"Nothing will happen to the young master." Yun Chu said calmly. "Hurry and look for him."

She only appeared calm on the outside. In reality, she was very worried. It was her fault. She shouldn’t have asked Yu Ge’er to apologize in the middle of the street. She should have considered the child’s feelings...

Yun Chu had two maids with her, as well as Yu Ke. Miss Tan also had a maid with her. The group of six didn’t dare to slack off, walking and calling out as they searched.

After about half an hour, they were getting farther and farther from the capital. Gradually, a lake came into view. The sunlight reflected off the water, shimmering.

Yun Chu immediately spotted the child sitting on a large rock by the lake.

Her heart leapt to her throat.

"It’s Yu Ge’er!" Miss Tan’s eyes lit up with joy.

Yun Chu softly said, "Yu Ke, you’re fast on your feet. Quickly go notify Prince Pingxi’s people and have them come here to pick up the young master."

Yu Ke nodded and quickly went to find Nurse Zheng and the others.

Yun Chu and Miss Tan slowly approached the lakeside.

Before they got close, Chu Hongyu, sitting on the rock, heard the footsteps. He turned around, his eyes red as he looked at Yun Chu.

"Don’t come over!" He stood up, stepping onto the large rock.

The lakeside was windy, and as a gust blew, Yun Chu saw his figure sway.

Miss Tan was so scared she tightly grabbed Yun Chu’s hand.

"Yu Ge’er, be good." Yun Chu said as she walked toward the lake. "Whatever you have to say, let’s sit down and talk about it slowly, okay?"

"Yes, Yu Ge’er." Miss Tan spoke up. "I admit I pinched you. I will apologize to your father. Won’t you come over? It’s too dangerous by the lake."

Chu Hongyu didn’t even glance at Miss Tan. His eyes were fixed on Yun Chu. "You saw me frame her with your own eyes. Does that mean you won’t like me anymore?"

"How could that be?" A smile appeared on Yun Chu’s face. "I know you must have had your reasons. Besides, it’s a great virtue to admit and correct one’s mistakes. You will always be the likable young master."

Chu Hongyu tightly pursed his lips. "But you called me ‘young master’."

The title "young master" was too distant. He liked it when she called him Yu Ge’er.

Yun Chu had no choice but to change her address. "Yu Ge’er, you’re the most obedient. How could I possibly not like you? Be good and stand still. I’ll help you down."

Chu Hongyu lowered his gaze, tugging at his own clothes.

He felt that he had let down Yun Chu’s affection for him.

He took a deep breath and looked at Miss Tan. "Miss Tan, I’m sorry. I shouldn’t have framed you for pinching my hand. It was my fault. Can you forgive me?"

Miss Tan was extremely surprised.

She had spent more than an hour with the young master, and no matter what she said, he had always kept a straight face.

But now, with just a few light words from Madam Xie, the young master had admitted his mistake and apologized to her.

She had originally thought the young master was willful and unreasonable, but now she realized, perhaps she simply didn’t know how to coax a child?

"Yu Ge’er, it’s fine." Miss Tan smiled. "It was also my fault for forcing you to accept me. There’s still time. We can take it slow."

Upon hearing this, Chu Hongyu, who had just calmed down, once again tightly pursed his lips.

If his father found out he had framed Miss Tan, being scolded would be the least of his worries. His father would definitely feel sorry for Miss Tan and agree to marry her.

What should he do? What could he do? Why had he messed everything up?

He glanced at Yun Chu, wishing he could openly call her "Mother." But that dream would probably never come true.

He unconsciously took a step back.

Suddenly, Miss Tan let out a scream. Immediately after, there was a splash, Chu Hongyu had fallen into the lake without warning.

"Yu Ge’er!"

Without a second thought, Yun Chu rushed forward. She didn’t even have time to take off her shoes before jumping into the lake.

"Madam!" Ling Shuang was so scared she followed suit and jumped in. Ling Feng, who couldn’t swim, quickly looked for a long branch or bamboo pole.

The lake water in summer wasn’t that cold, but it was deep.

Yun Chu was extremely grateful that when she was young, her mother often took her to the countryside to play. She was mischievous and loved the water, so her mother, fearing she might drown, had someone teach her how to swim.

As soon as she jumped in, she saw Chu Hongyu continuously sinking.

The lakebed was covered with water plants. As soon as the little guy sank, the water plants entangled his ankles, and he struggled with all his might.

Yun Chu quickly swam over.

She first untangled the water plants, then wrapped her arms around his shoulders from behind and swam upward with him.

Finally, they surfaced. Once the little guy could breathe, he suddenly regained his strength and wrapped his arms and legs around Yun Chu’s waist.

Yun Chu hadn’t been in the water for many years. With him clinging to her like this, she forgot how to use her limbs. Her body sank a little, and she unexpectedly swallowed a mouthful of water.

Chu Hongyu had no idea how much trouble his actions were causing Yun Chu.

All he knew was that he had to hold tightly onto the person in front of him, or he would sink again. That suffocating and stifling feeling was unbearable.

Yun Chu, thrown off balance by him, swallowed three more mouthfuls of lake water.

She heard Ling Shuang’s voice in the distance. Since Ling Shuang had learned to swim with her since childhood, having Ling Shuang’s help would make things much easier.

Just then, she felt a shadow loom over her.

Before she could see what it was, her waist was suddenly grabbed. Immediately after, she and Chu Hongyu were both lifted out of the water.

Instinctively, she tightened her hold on the child clinging to her. At the same time, she found herself pressed against a broad chest.

She looked up and saw the side of a man’s face, Prince Pingxi.

Instinctively, she tried to struggle.

"Don’t move." Chu Yi’s voice was extremely cold. "Be careful not to fall back into the lake."

She looked down and saw that Chu Yi was lightly skimming the lake’s surface with his feet. In almost the blink of an eye, they were at the shore.

A crowd of people surrounded them. Chu Yi turned, blocking the view of his guards.

He lowered his gaze and saw the woman was completely soaked, her thin summer dress outlining her graceful figure... He quickly averted his eyes, took off his outer robe, and draped it over Yun Chu.

Ling Feng, who had been holding a long branch and was about to help, was completely stunned. From the moment Prince Pingxi appeared holding Yun Chu to when they landed on the shore, she finally snapped out of her daze.

She threw away the branch in her hand, quickly unbuttoned her outer garment, and rushed toward Yun Chu. She squeezed between Chu Yi and Yun Chu.

She snatched the man’s robe off Yun Chu and, with the fastest speed possible, draped her own outer garment over Yun Chu’s head.

Only when Yun Chu was completely covered did she let out a sigh of relief. Then, she used the man’s robe to wrap up the equally drenched Chu Hongyu.

On the other side, Ling Shuang, with Miss Tan’s help, climbed out of the lake, also completely soaked.

Miss Tan was helping Ling Shuang, so naturally, she didn’t see how Yun Chu had suddenly emerged from the water...

Yu Ke, who had brought Nurse Zheng and the others, happened to see the drenched Ling Shuang. Without a word, he took off his own clothes and walked toward Ling Shuang.

chapters.title: But He Was Crying
chapters.content:
"Prince, it is all this concubine's fault. I failed to look after the young master properly. Please punish me, Prince."

Miss Tan the Second's face was ashen, clearly terrified.

The moment she saw Prince Pingxi arrive, she hurried over, knelt, and bowed her head, her heart pounding with unease.

On his way here, Chu Yi had already been briefed on the entire incident. Though the servants did not dare explicitly state that the young master had framed Miss Tan the Second, as the boy's father, how could he not understand how mischievous his son was?

To achieve his goals, the boy was capable of such things; it was not surprising.

Chu Yi spoke, "It should be I who apologize on behalf of my unruly son."

Miss Tan the Second was taken aback.

Prince Pingxi had earned great merit on the battlefield at the age of fifteen. People in the capital said he had a peculiar temper, yet she found him rather reasonable.

She had made such a grave mistake, yet Prince Pingxi not only did not blame her but even apologized to her?

"Miss Tan, these past few days have wasted your time. I will compensate Lord Tan for it." Chu Yi turned to the servants beside him. "You lot, escort Miss Tan safely back to her residence."

"Yes!"

Two guards and two wet nurses stepped forward, each making a gesture of invitation.

Miss Tan the Second was no fool. Hearing Chu Yi’s words, she understood: these past few days, she had been summoned repeatedly by the imperial family, but it had all been in vain. No matter how satisfied the royal family was with her, the young master was not. Moreover, she had caused the young master to fall into the water... Just for that alone, Prince Pingxi would never take her as his wife.

The only silver lining was that Prince Pingxi had said he would compensate her for the wasted time. She hoped it would benefit her father’s official career.

"Then this concubine will take her leave."

Miss Tan the Second curtsied and turned to board the carriage.

As Chu Yi and Miss Tan the Second spoke, Yun Chu had already stood up, wrapped in Ling Feng’s outer garment.

She glanced at the little one carried away by Nurse Zheng. Since he still had the strength to speak, he was probably fine.

She approached Chu Yi, maintaining a distance of five or six steps, and curtsied. "Thank you for your rescue, Prince. This concubine will take her leave now."

"It should be I who thanks Lady Xie." Chu Yi looked at her, but all he could see was her dripping hair. "If not for Lady Xie risking her life to save my son, he would likely have... Since it’s a half-hour’s journey back to the capital, Lady Xie might catch a chill along the way. Coincidentally, I have a manor nearby. Would Lady Xie consider changing into dry clothes before departing?"

Yun Chu lowered her head, pondering how to refuse.

Earlier, she had been soaked and held in this man’s arms. As a married woman, she should not be so close to another man.

In her past life, she would have been tormented by guilt over this, even feeling as if she had wronged Xie Jingyu.

But now, her heart was as still as water. She no longer cared about such things.

Of course, not caring did not mean she was willing to go to Prince Pingxi’s manor.

Yun Chu was about to speak when she felt her skirt being tugged.

Looking down, she saw Chu Hongyu.

The little one had somehow slipped out of Nurse Zheng’s arms at some point. He tilted his head up and said, "Mother, Changsheng drew a dress for you. He had the servants work through the night to make it and said that next time he sees you, he would give it to you as a gift. I’ve already sent someone to fetch it from the prince’s residence for you to wear. It must be very beautiful."

Before Yun Chu could respond, he ordered Ah Mao to go quickly.

Ah Mao mounted a sweat-blooded horse and disappeared down the path in a flash.

Hearing the young master call Yun Chu "Mother," Nurse Zheng and the others were all stunned.

But when they saw that Prince Pingxi did not seem bothered at all, they were even more shocked...

Nurse Zheng’s heart suddenly trembled. Could it be that their prince... liked married women like Lady Xie?

Heavens, no wonder Prince Pingxi had never married. So that was the reason...

She turned and warned the surrounding maids and servants with a glance, signaling them not to spread such a huge secret...

Yun Chu’s resolve to refuse softened instantly at the mention of Changsheng’s name.

Changsheng couldn’t speak, but he was good at painting. She found herself genuinely looking forward to seeing what kind of dress he had drawn. She had never anticipated a gift so eagerly before.

With so many servants around, it wouldn’t be improper.

Chu Yi had a carriage brought over. Yun Chu and her two maids boarded it, while Yu Ke drove from the front.

The manor was indeed close. Yun Chu felt as if she had just sat down when they arrived. Lifting the curtain, she saw a modestly sized manor.

The attending servants had already been notified. They stood at the entrance to welcome them, then led Yun Chu and her group to the nearest courtyard. Hot water and everything else had already been prepared.

Ling Shuang was also soaked. She went to the adjacent side room to bathe.

Ling Feng attended to Yun Chu.

Being on someone else’s property, it wasn’t as relaxed as at home. After quickly washing off the dirt from her body and hair, she got up immediately.

At this moment, the servant sent to fetch the dress from the prince’s residence had also returned. A maid knocked and entered, stopping outside the screen. She respectfully said, "Lady Xie, the dress has been placed here for you."

The maid set down the tray and quietly exited.

Ling Feng unfolded the dress and gasped, "Heavens, this dress is too beautiful! How is the young princess so talented?"

Yun Chu looked over. It was a long dress made of watered cloud brocade, embroidered with tea flowers of various colors. Though many colors were used, they were all subtle, giving the dress an elegant and graceful appearance rather than a chaotic one.

On the sleeve of the dress, she saw two characters: Yun Chu.

It must have been drawn by the young princess, and the embroiderer had followed the design. One could tell the characters were written by a child.

In addition to the dress, there was also an outer robe on the tray, the same color as the one she had worn before. Unless one looked closely, no one would notice she had changed clothes.

Ling Feng helped her into the dress, styled her hair, and finally draped the outer robe over her.

Chu Hongyu had been waiting impatiently at the door. When he saw Yun Chu come out wearing the outer robe, he pouted and said, "Mother, let me see if the dress is beautiful or not. When I go home, I can tell Changsheng about it."

Yun Chu lifted the outer robe slightly, revealing only the hem of the dress.

Chu Yi was sitting in a pavilion outside the side room. He couldn’t help but look over.

He saw a woman in a multicolored dress standing at the door of the side room. The flowers embroidered with gold and silver threads shimmered in the sunlight. As she stepped forward, the sunlight fell upon her, making the hem of her dress glow as if she herself were glowing.

As she approached, he even caught the scent of her bath.

Realizing what he was doing, Chu Yi quickly averted his gaze and held his breath. He uncomfortably looked into the distance and said, "The carriage is ready. Lady Xie, this way, please."

Yun Chu nodded and followed him out.

Suddenly, it felt as if her skirt had been stepped on. Before she could check, she felt a push at her lower back, and her body lurched forward uncontrollably.

Chu Yi, walking in front of her, instinctively caught her falling body.

---

chapters.title: Weakness and Hypocrisy
chapters.content:
The soft body fell into his arms.

Chu Yi froze entirely.

He had never been this close to a woman, except for that one night...

He quickly helped her stand up.

In that instant, he caught a scent beyond the fragrance of her bath, an unique, distinctly feminine aroma.

It seemed familiar...

"Thank you, Prince."

Yun Chu took two large steps back, putting a considerable distance between herself and the man.

Chu Yi looked at her. Compared to the ripples in his own heart, she seemed far too calm.

No matter what happened, she always wore this composed expression.

Just as this thought crossed his mind, he noticed Yun Chu’s expression darken slightly. She turned her head to look at Chu Hongyu, who was walking beside her.

"Young Master, don’t you have something to say?"

She had just fallen forward because the little one in front of her had pushed her hard.

Chu Hongyu lowered his head, twisting his fingers together. "I’m sorry... I didn’t mean to... I just..."

He just wanted Mother and Father Prince to develop some feelings. He wanted Mother to like Father Prince. He wanted Father Prince to be willing to marry Mother as his princess consort.

Why could Mother marry someone as terrible as Xie Jingyu, but not Father Prince?

Yun Chu knew exactly what he was thinking.

She crouched down and said, "Yu’ge’er, today you did three things wrong. First, you framed Miss Tan the Second. Second, you didn’t admit your mistake and ran away, nearly causing a disaster. Third, you intentionally pushed someone... Although I’ve said that knowing one’s mistake and correcting it makes a good child, repeatedly making mistakes and then apologizing is not ‘the greatest virtue’, it’s... repeated offenses without reform."

If she hadn’t happened to pass by, who knew how much blame Miss Tan the Second would have had to bear.

If she hadn’t known how to swim, the little one in front of her might have drowned in the lake.

If she hadn’t lived an extra decade, after being held by another man, she might have died from shame and anger.

Chu Hongyu’s eyes widened.

This was the first time Mother had spoken to him so sternly, even calling him unrepentant.

"I hope you become a child of upright character." Yun Chu ruffled his hair. "Alright, I should go now."

She stood up and curtsied to Chu Yi. "Prince, it is this concubine who has overstepped."

"You spoke well, Lady Xie." Chu Yi said, "It is I who have failed in raising my son, causing you so much trouble. In the future, I will take more care in disciplining him."

Yun Chu said nothing more.

She walked out of the manor and boarded the carriage. Looking back, she saw the little one staring at her with tear-filled eyes.

She couldn’t help but sigh.

After her rebirth, she had used every means at her disposal against the Xie family. What right did she have to demand that Yu’ge’er be a person of upright character?

But she truly hoped he would be a good child, reading countless books, traveling thousands of miles, growing into a proper young man with the integrity of a green pine and a heart of compassion for the world... While someone as despicable as her should slowly rot away in the long years. How could she ever be worthy of his affection?

But he was crying.

Yun Chu’s heart melted completely.

She could only force a smile.

Chu Hongyu immediately stopped crying and laughed, waving his hands and feet. "Father Prince, Mother smiled at me! She must have forgiven me..."

"If she has forgiven you, then don’t let her down." Chu Yi said, "The most important thing for a person of upright character is to read more. When we return, study hard with your tutor. This autumn, I will send you to the Imperial Academy."

Chu Hongyu sniffled and nodded.

The carriage slowly made its way toward the capital. After entering the city, the crowded streets forced the carriage to slow down considerably.

Suddenly, a voice came from outside.

"Is Lady Xie in the carriage?"

Yu Ke, the driver, called out, "Madam, it’s Lord Xuanwu."

Even before Yu Ke spoke, Yun Chu had recognized Lord Xuanwu’s voice.

That day at the Xuanwu Marquis’s residence, the man’s words to her still seemed to echo in her ears. And she had slapped him in response.

Ling Shuang worriedly grabbed Yun Chu’s hand and whispered, "Madam, let this servant go deal with him."

Yun Chu shook her head. Enough days had passed; Lord Xuanwu’s anger should have subsided.

If she avoided him now, he would surely find a way to force her to visit the marquis’s residence, which would be even more troublesome.

Right now, they were on a busy street. With so many people coming and going, Lord Xuanwu wouldn’t dare do anything.

Moreover, she always felt that Lord Xuanwu seemed to know something she didn’t...

She lifted the carriage curtain and, with Ling Shuang’s support, stepped out. Lowering her gaze, she said, "Greetings, Lord Marquis. Is there something you need?"

Qin Mingheng had been riding a sweat-blooded horse when he unexpectedly spotted the Xie family’s carriage. He had called out tentatively, not expecting to actually encounter her.

His tongue pressed against his cheek. The slap from days ago had kept him from court for a full five days.

He dismounted and took a few steps forward. Immediately, his nose caught a unique fragrance.

He inhaled the scent greedily.

Yun Chu felt a chill run down her spine. This man was even more disgusting than she had imagined.

Ling Feng and Ling Shuang positioned themselves on either side of Yun Chu, shielding her from Qin Mingheng’s unusual gaze.

"Do you remember what I said to you that day, Lady Xie?" Qin Mingheng smiled. "The two corpses you reburied; are they truly your own flesh and blood?"

Yun Chu’s fingers tightened.

Here it was. This was the feeling she had, that Qin Mingheng knew a lot.

She knew she shouldn’t fall into the trap he had deliberately set, but when it came to her children, she couldn’t remain calm.

She gave a signal, and Ling Shuang and Ling Feng stepped aside. She looked up at the man before her. "Lord Marquis, you said this once before. This is the second time. As the saying goes, ‘nothing should be done to excess.’ What do you think?"

"Come a little closer." Qin Mingheng gazed at her obsessively. "Come here, and I’ll tell you what’s really going on."

Yun Chu stared at him coldly.

It seemed she would have to find a way to pry the truth out of him.

"If Lord Marquis has nothing else, I will take my leave."

She turned to leave.

"Wait." Qin Mingheng took two steps forward. "Yun Chu, I’ll only tell you this: the two corpses buried by the Yun family are not your biological children. If you want to know more, come to the Xuanwu Marquis’s residence of your own accord. I will tell you everything."

Yun Chu’s pupils contracted sharply.

She didn’t want to believe this man, but the facts told her that Xie Jingyu was capable of such deception.

Moreover, that day when she had gone to find her children’s remains, she had been so grief-stricken that, looking back now, there had indeed been many oversights.

Yun Chu lowered her gaze to conceal the emotions in her eyes.

When she looked up again, her expression was calm. "I ask that Lord Marquis stop using my deceased children as leverage..."

Before she could finish, a figure suddenly appeared beside her. Then, her wrist was grabbed and pulled behind someone. She didn’t need to look to know; it was Xie Jingyu.

chapters.title: His Deep-Rooted Affection
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu’s face darkened to the extreme.

After having tea with Director Yu, he left the teahouse and spotted the most eye-catching woman in the crowd from afar.

True to her reputation as the most beautiful daughter of the Yun family in the capital, she stood out so brightly on the bustling street that everyone’s gaze was involuntarily drawn to her.

However, when he saw the man standing in front of Yun Chu, his heart instantly sank to the bottom of the valley.

He apologized to Director Yu, then quickly walked over and pulled Yun Chu behind him.

He cupped his hands in greeting: "This official greets Lord Qin."

"Tsk." Qin Mingheng chuckled, "I was merely having a few words with Lady Xie. Does Lord Xie fear I might devour her?"

Xie Jingyu spoke: "The hour is late. This official will take my wife home. Next time, I shall visit Lord Qin properly."

After saying this, he turned to Yun Chu: "Wife, let us go home."

Yun Chu evaded his outstretched hand, steadied herself with Tingshuang, and boarded the carriage first.

Xie Jingyu followed her inside and sat across from her.

As before, Yun Chu couldn’t be bothered to speak to him. She lifted the carriage curtain to gaze at the scenery outside.

Xie Jingyu’s chest swelled with frustration.

Unable to contain himself, he asked: "What were you and Marquis Wu discussing?"

Yun Chu replied coolly: "We happened to meet on the road. Just exchanged greetings."

Xie Jingyu pressed: "Only that?"

"Otherwise, what could it be?" Yun Chu lowered the curtain and met his gaze directly. "My lord’s urgent questioning; does he suspect me of having an affair?"

"Of course not..." Xie Jingyu hadn’t expected her to be so blunt. He was left speechless, even avoiding her clear eyes. He stammered, "Last time, when Wei Ge’er injured the young master of Marquis Wu’s household, Marquis Wu has been making things difficult for me at court. I was worried he might disrespect you, so I..."

Yun Chu stared at him fixedly.

She knew Xie Jingyu was a thoroughly hypocritical man who would resort to any means to achieve his goals.

If what Qin Mingheng said was true, then why had Xie Jingyu used two fake corpses to deceive her?

Those were her children, carrying the blood of the Xie family. She truly did not want to believe that Xie Jingyu had discarded the children’s bodies...

"Wife, what is it?"

Under Yun Chu’s gaze, Xie Jingyu felt uneasy all over and instinctively touched his own face.

Yun Chu shook her head and said no more.

The carriage soon arrived at the gates of the Xie residence.

They had left in the morning to visit the Yun family, then went to the outskirts, and with some delays on the road, it was already evening by the time they returned.

The orange sunset of high summer fell on their shoulders, casting long shadows.

He Shi stood in the courtyard and immediately spotted the two entering side by side, the man tall and elegant, the woman stunningly beautiful. What a perfect pair.

She suppressed the emotions rising in her heart, walked over, and curtsied: "Lord, Lady."

"I still have matters to attend to. I shall return to my courtyard."

Without a single extra word, Yun Chu turned and left with her maids.

Xie Jingyu watched her retreating figure and let out an almost imperceptible sigh.

"He Shi," He Shi spoke, "The lady left alone in the morning. How did she return with you, my lord?"

Xie Jingyu replied casually: "We met on the road."

"How come the lady has changed her clothes?" He Shi had been focusing on embroidery lately and was well-versed in fabrics. "The dress the lady is wearing is a rare Jin Yun watered silk from Jiangnan. Only the nobility can afford such fabric. Has the Yun family grown so wealthy?"

Xie Jingyu’s expression suddenly darkened.

As the Yun family’s son-in-law, he knew very well that although the Yun family held the rank of a first-class general’s residence, they were not particularly wealthy and could not afford such expensive fabrics.

He quickly entered his own courtyard and coldly ordered: "Go to the Yun family’s gatehouse and ask how long the lady stayed."

The servant was efficient and returned in less than half an hour, reporting: "The lady left the Yun family around a quarter past noon after having lunch."

Xie Jingyu slammed his teacup onto the table.

If she left the Yun family at a quarter past noon, why was she still on the street at dusk?

Could it be that after leaving the Yun family, she went to the Marquis Wu’s residence...

The mere thought of this possibility made Xie Jingyu lose control. He stood up and strode toward the Shengju Courtyard.

Yun Chu had just sat down at the dining table. The hall was cooled with ice blocks, and the maids served the dishes one by one.

She picked up her chopsticks, about to eat, when she heard the young maid outside greet: "Lord, the lady is dining. Please allow this servant to—"

Before the maid could finish, Xie Jingyu had already entered the side hall and sat down at the dining table.

Yun Chu calmly ordered: "Prepare another set of bowls and chopsticks."

Xie Jingyu’s gaze fixed on Yun Chu. He remembered she had a similar outer garment, which she had worn two or three times. If one didn’t look carefully, one might think the one she was wearing now was the same as before. In reality, there were slight differences. Even though both were white, there were subtle distinctions.

This garment was clearly meant to deceive.

Why had she changed her clothes outside? Had she only changed the outer garment, or everything underneath as well?

He picked up his chopsticks and ate a few bites in a controlled manner.

Seeing that Yun Chu had almost finished eating, he coldly said: "All of you, withdraw."

Tingshuang looked at Yun Chu.

Yun Chu smiled slightly. She also wanted to have a good talk with him. She waved her hand, and the maids and servants in the room all retreated, closing the door softly behind them.

The room fell silent.

"Wife, where did you go this afternoon?" Xie Jingyu asked directly. "Did you and Marquis Wu really just meet on the road?"

Yun Chu lowered her eyes and took a sip of tea.

If she hadn’t known that this man had once offered her to Marquis Wu to appease the Xie family’s disaster, she might have truly believed he cared for her.

After doing such a despicable thing, did he still have the right to question her?

Before she could speak, Xie Jingyu suddenly stood up, leaned forward, and grabbed Yun Chu’s wrist.

Then, without warning, he pulled open her outer garment and saw an undergarment he had never seen before.

"Why did you change your clothes outside? You changed everything, inside and out!" Xie Jingyu angrily tightened his grip on her slender wrist. "What did you and Marquis Wu do?!"

"You left me alone at Marquis Wu’s residence. Why didn’t you consider these things then?" Yun Chu said coldly. "Marquis Wu told me that the tea you handed me that day at the Marquis’s residence was laced with a sedative. I’ve been wondering how I could have slept all afternoon at the Marquis’s residence. Doesn’t my lord want to explain?"

Xie Jingyu’s heart lurched: "What else did he tell you?"

"Isn’t this one thing enough to shock me? Could there be other things I don’t know?" Yun Chu pushed Xie Jingyu away with one hand, her eyes sharp. "If you don’t explain clearly, I don’t mind paying a visit to Marquis Wu’s residence to find out."

Xie Jingyu clenched his fists.

This matter could not be explained. Even if he explained it clearly, if Qin Mingheng brought up the wedding night to Yun Chu again, he would once more be put in a passive position.

He raised his eyes, looking utterly disappointed: "Wife, you would rather believe an outsider than your own husband? No one knows what kind of man I am better than you do."

Yun Chu gave a cold laugh.

Yes, no one knew better than her the cowardice and hypocrisy deep in Xie Jingyu’s bones.

---

chapters.title: They Look Alike
chapters.content:
"Wife, on the day of our wedding, Marquis Wu also came to drink the wedding wine. That day, he got drunk."

Xie Jingyu slowly approached Yun Chu.

"It was I who personally helped Marquis Wu to the side room to rest. He kept muttering in his drunken state, and I listened carefully. Only then did I realize he was calling out the name 'Yun Chu.' That was when I found out that Marquis Wu had deep feelings for you."

"After our marriage, he has constantly been tripping me up in secret. Fortunately, with the Yun family as in-laws, he didn’t dare to truly do anything to me. But after Wei Ge’er injured the young master of Marquis Wu’s household, he had a legitimate reason and spared no effort to cause trouble for me... Because I took He Shi as a concubine, the Yun family no longer stepped in to protect me. I know this is my own doing... During that period, I struggled at every step in the official circles, so I had no choice but to bring you to his residence to apologize."

"But I swear to heaven, I did not drug your tea. What man would willingly bring a cuckold upon himself? At the very least, I am not that kind of person!" Xie Jingyu placed his hands on Yun Chu’s shoulders. "Wife, that man covets you and cannot bear to see our marital harmony, so he is sowing discord between us. You must not believe a single word he says."

Yun Chu looked into his eyes.

How sincere they seemed. What an excellent act. No wonder, in her past life, it took her over thirty years to see this man’s true face.

She was already certain that she would get no truth from his mouth. Besides sophistry, what else could he possibly say?

If she wanted to know the truth, she would have to investigate it herself.

She showed a timely look of shock: "Marquis Wu and his wife are deeply in love, and he has no concubines in his household. How could he possibly have deep feelings for me? My lord must have misunderstood."

"Not having concubines does not mean he deeply loves his wife." Xie Jingyu said, "Although there are several concubines in the Xie family’s rear courtyard, in my heart, you, Wife, will always be the first."

Suddenly, he embraced Yun Chu.

"Wife, I have not come to your room since our wedding. I have wronged you. Let me make it up to you today."

Without waiting for her response, he pulled Yun Chu toward the couch.

He only wanted to know whether she had betrayed him and done something improper with Marquis Wu.

Over this period, Yun Chu had been practicing martial arts with Qiutong. In the past, she might not have been a match for Xie Jingyu, but after learning martial arts, not only had her skills improved, but her strength had also increased significantly. She lifted her foot and kicked him. Xie Jingyu lost his balance and fell backward. Fortunately, there was a chair behind him, so he didn’t fall to the ground.

"Lord," Yun Chu’s voice was icy, "Have I not told you that cohabitation is not allowed during my body’s regulation period?"

Xie Jingyu tightened his lips.

Was her resistance truly for the sake of her body’s regulation, or was it because she feared he would discover something...

"Lord, I went to Qing’an Temple outside the city this afternoon." Yun Chu changed the subject. "The master who performed the rites for the children said there seems to be something wrong with the children’s remains..."

Xie Jingyu immediately cast aside his previous emotions and anxiously asked: "What problem?"

"The master said that before the children reincarnate, they will return to their home in this life. But no matter how the master tried to guide them, neither of the two children returned to the Xie family." Yun Chu fixed her gaze on Xie Jingyu. "Lord, why do you think that is?"

Xie Jingyu’s scalp instantly went numb.

He had always believed that stories of masters performing rites and spirits reincarnating were all lies fabricated by people.

But now, he no longer dared to think that.

No wonder Qing’an Temple had such a thriving incense business; it turned out the masters there had real abilities.

"Perhaps, perhaps it’s because this is not the Xie family’s ancestral home." Xie Jingyu racked his brain for a reason. "The children might have returned to the old Xie residence in Jizhou."

Yun Chu nodded: "That must be it."

"The hour is late. Wife, rest early. I still have matters to attend to."

Xie Jingyu stood up, opened the door, and left. His retreating figure looked as if he were fleeing in disarray.

Yun Chu collapsed weakly into the chair.

She could now be absolutely certain that Marquis Wu’s words were true. Those two corpses were truly not her children!

Otherwise, Xie Jingyu would not have shown such an expression.

Otherwise, Xie Jingyu would never have left like that.

To live a second life and still be manipulated by Xie Jingyu; she was truly the biggest fool under heaven!

She wanted to know even more: Why had Xie Jingyu deceived her about the children’s whereabouts time and time again? They were his own flesh and blood. What reason could he possibly have for doing this?

"Tingshuang!" Yun Chu raised her voice. "Investigate where every member of the Xie family was when I confronted He Shi about the children’s burial place!"

Tingshuang nodded: "Yes, Lady!"

Knowing this matter must be kept secret, she only called her most trusted maids to help gather information.

That night, Yun Chu thought she would dream of her two children, but she did not dream at all. When she opened her eyes in the morning, it was still pitch black.

She put on her martial arts training clothes and followed Qiutong to practice in the courtyard for more than half an hour before the sky finally brightened.

After finishing her training and bathing, she came out to find that those who had come to pay their respects had already arrived.

She lifted her eyes toward Xie Pin, who was standing to the side. Compared to a few days ago, under the guidance of Nurse Fu, Xie Pin had made significant progress.

Even just standing there, Xie Pin’s posture showed the effort put into her training. She had developed some grace and refinement.

After the usual pleasantries, Yun Chu was about to have everyone dismissed. She truly did not have the energy to deal with these people.

"Lady!" Tingyu suddenly stepped forward, her face streaked with tears. "Please, Lady, allow this concubine to see Yun Ge’er. It has been so many days since I last saw him..."

"Lady, I have something to say." He Shi stepped forward. "You entrusted Yun Ge’er to my care, and I have done my best. However, when Yun Ge’er first came to my courtyard, he was unaccustomed and cried constantly. It took great effort to soothe him. But then, Concubine Yu sneaked into Bihe Garden, and all my efforts were wasted. Therefore, I do not allow Concubine Yu to meet with Yun Ge’er. I hope you understand, Lady."

"Lady, Yun Ge’er has not attended school for six or seven days. It seems he is ill." Tingyu accused, "Concubine He has never raised a child and does not know how to take care of Yun Ge’er. Please, Lady, let Yun Ge’er return to my side..."

Yun Chu’s voice was calm: "He is ill?"

He Shi lowered her head and replied: "A few days ago, he ate too much ice and caught a chill. I have already called a physician and obtained a prescription. He will be better in a few days. Concubine Yu need not worry."

Tingyu was nearly driven mad. When Yun Ge’er was with her, he had rarely been ill. How could he fall sick so severely in Bihe Garden that he couldn’t even attend school?

He Shi had once given Tao Concubine’s unborn child medicine to cause a miscarriage. She truly feared that He Shi, in her madness, would do the same to Yun Ge’er!

Yun Ge’er was her lifeline. She dared not imagine what would happen if she lost him!

"Lady, I truly know I was wrong!" Tingyu deeply regretted having reported to Xie Jingyu. She sobbed uncontrollably, "Please, Lady, have pity on Yun Ge’er and let him return to his birth mother’s side..."

chapters.title: He's Identity
chapters.content:
Yun Chu closed her eyes to rest.

After listening to Tingyu’s complaints, she finally spoke, "Bing Jie, what do you think?"

Xie Bing hadn’t expected Yun Chu to ask for her opinion.

She thought that perhaps her current status was different now. As the future Princess Consort of Anjing, her words should carry some weight.

She spoke, "Father doesn’t let Aunt Ting raise Yun Ge because he is considering Yun Ge’s future. Aunt Ting shouldn’t, out of fear of losing her child, delay Yun Ge’s prospects. I think it’s better for Yun Ge to stay with Aunt He."

He Shi smiled.

Although she was impatient with raising Xie Shiyun, he had to stay by her side.

If Xie Shiyun was ruined, all of the Xie family’s resources would fall to An Ge. The entire Xie family should belong to An Ge completely.

Only with a better future could An Ge protect Xie Shiyun, who would be like a useless person.

Tingyu knew that no matter what she said, the madam would not soften her heart.

She had betrayed the madam twice. The madam had given up on her, so she vented her anger on Yun Ge, deliberately sending him to He Shi.

She knew she was wrong in many ways, but what was Yun Ge’s fault?

"All of you may leave."

Yun Chu waved her hand.

Tingyu glanced at He Shi, who had a smile on her lips, bit her lip, and left.

Tao Concubine, with her big belly, slowly walked out supported by a maid. She looked at Tingyu, who was walking out of the Sheng Ju with her head down, and turned to Jiang Concubine, saying, "That one who climbed onto the master’s bed behind the madam’s back to become a concubine, not content with her lot, even incites the master and madam’s relationship. If the madam doesn’t punish her, who will she punish?"

Jiang Concubine didn’t want to discuss others’ faults and asked with concern, "There’s still more than a month until your due date. You must take good care of yourself."

"Of course." Tao Concubine was about to complain about the hardships of late pregnancy when she saw He Shi and Xie Bing walking to a tree not far away, whispering. Her eyes narrowed. "Jiang Concubine, have you noticed that the eldest young lady and Concubine He look a bit alike?"

Jiang Concubine was a person of few words. Introverted people were always more observant. She had noticed this long ago but had never mentioned it to anyone.

She nodded, "There are so many identical leaves in the world. Two people looking alike is nothing unusual. Maybe this is the fate between Concubine He and the eldest young lady, which is why they have always been close."

"Not only is the eldest young lady close to Concubine He, but the eldest young master and the second young master are also particularly close to Concubine He." Tao Concubine tapped her chin with her finger. "Think carefully, the eldest young master’s eyes are exactly the same as Concubine He’s. The second young master’s mouth looks like it was carved from the same mold as Concubine He’s. And the eldest young lady also looks so much like Concubine He..."

Jiang Concubine couldn’t help but cover her lips, "They say that when a daughter grows up, she will look like her birth mother..."

"My heavens!" Tao Concubine widened her eyes. "Could it be... could it be... that’s impossible, too preposterous."

"What are you talking about?"

A voice suddenly came from behind.

Tao Concubine and Jiang Concubine were both startled. They turned around and saw He Shi and Xie Bing standing there. Caught gossiping behind someone’s back, they felt somewhat embarrassed.

"N-Nothing." Jiang Concubine tightened her grip on Xie Xian’s hand. "I’m taking Xian Jie to the school."

After saying that, she quickly left.

Tao Concubine touched her pregnant belly, her gaze scanning He Shi and Xie Bing’s faces. "I have to say, Concubine He and the eldest young lady really do look a bit like mother and daughter."

He Shi took a sharp breath.

She hadn’t misheard. Tao Concubine and Jiang Concubine were indeed discussing her and Bing Jie’s appearance.

Xie Bing remembered the teachings of Nurse Fu: no matter what comments she heard, she must not show her emotions. She steadied her mind and coldly said, "Tao Concubine is saying something ridiculous. My mother is the eldest young lady of the General’s Mansion, the Yun family. I am the eldest young lady of the Xie family. How could I possibly look like He Shi, a servant? Don’t humiliate me!"

She turned and left.

Tao Concubine frowned. The eldest young lady’s words were full of disdain and contempt for Concubine He. Could it be that she had guessed wrong?

He Shi lowered her head, clenched her fingers, and quickly walked away.

Yun Chu found that she couldn’t calm down to do anything.

Tingshuang had gone to investigate that day’s matter, and it would take at least three days to find out the result.

She simply ordered someone to prepare a carriage and went to the hot spring villa in the north of the city to take a look. After so many days, the villa should be quite different.

The carriage traveled for about half an hour before arriving at the entrance of the villa.

Last time she came, the weeds were as tall as a person everywhere. Now they had been cleared, revealing the original appearance of the villa.

This was the site of the Wu family’s ancestral temple many years ago. The houses were built with great effort, and even after more than twenty years of being uninhabited, they were not in too much disrepair.

Of course, some repairs were still needed, especially the courtyard walls, roof corners, eaves, and roofs...

"Madam, you truly have foresight!" Chen Defu’s face was full of admiration. "It turns out there is a huge hot spring on the back mountain of this villa. We won’t know exactly how big it is until it’s fully excavated."

It cost three thousand taels of silver to buy this villa, and the total cost of repairs and excavating the hot spring to build hot spring pools would be around seven or eight thousand taels of silver.

But with this hot spring, in just one winter, it could earn tens of thousands of taels of silver, and that was a conservative estimate.

Yun Chu followed Chen Defu towards the back mountain. As soon as they arrived, they saw Jiu Er, dressed in a cyan outfit, distributing tea to the workers to help them cool down.

She paused and asked, "Uncle Chen, what do you think of Jiu Er?"

"She’s a sincere girl." Chen Defu replied. "Although she is physically weak, she never shirks work or rests. She starts working when the workers do. When she first came, she was fair-skinned, but these past few days, she’s tanned quite a bit."

Hearing the sound of their conversation, Jiu Er turned around. Seeing that it was Yun Chu, she quickly put down the tea and came over to pay her respects.

Yun Chu spoke, "The hot spring has been partially excavated. You can start soaking in it. The doctor said at least half an hour a day."

Jiu Er lowered her head, "Madam, Jiu Er is of lowly status. I shouldn’t dirty the hot spring pool."

Yun Chu said indifferently, "But it’s not for you to soak for free. This hot spring hasn’t been used by anyone yet. We don’t know what effects soaking in it will have, so you need to record everything. What does it feel like to soak for a quarter of an hour? What does it feel like to soak for half an hour? Each pool has a different temperature, and the feelings will be different. You need to try them all. After a month, I’ll come back and ask you about it."

Jiu Er was deeply moved, "Yes, Madam."

She knew that Madam had given her this task to ease her psychological burden about soaking in the hot spring.

In the future, her lowly life would belong to Madam. Even if Madam asked her to climb a mountain of knives, she wouldn’t blink an eye.

As they were speaking, Wu Madam, leaning on a crutch, came out of a thatched house in the woods behind them. As soon as she saw Yun Chu, Wu Madam’s face was filled with tears, "Madam Xie, you are the savior of my son and the great benefactor of my Wu family.
