Lately, the old madam’s dissatisfaction with Madam had grown. She would curse her from time to time, and if Madam Zhou tried to advise her, the old madam would only scold her more harshly.

In her opinion, ever since Madam had returned to the Yun family, the inner affairs of the Xie household had been managed by the eldest miss, and everything had gone wrong. It had even dragged her, at her old age, into having to manage household matters alongside the eldest miss...

"Young Lady Yun’s family is a century-old aristocratic family. How can they be so unruly?" The old madam continued. "Letting a married daughter stay at her maiden home for so long, even the imperial family wouldn’t allow it. Madam Yun is determined to slap the Xie family in the face..."

"That’s not true, Old Madam!"

Yun Chu walked in from the main entrance and stood before the old madam.

The old madam was so startled she nearly jumped. Over the past half month, Jingyu had gone to the Yun residence every few days to fetch Yun Chu, but Yun Chu had refused to return each time.

The old madam had assumed that this time would be no different.

She hadn’t expected that while she was cursing someone in her own room, she would be caught red-handed. Had the maids and servants at the door all died?

"My mother may not follow the rules, but she would never secretly bring in children from an outside relationship without telling my sister-in-law." Yun Chu paused. "Oh, I’ve misspoken. My eldest brother, no matter what, would never hide a concubine from his wife, let alone have children with her."

"You! You!" The old madam’s blood pressure surged.

This was outrageous! A junior daring to speak to her elder in such a tone; was she trying to rebel?

He Shi was already dead, had been dead for half a month. Her body was cold, and it was all in the past. Why bring it up again? Was there any point?

"Old Madam, don’t be angry." Yun Chu’s lips curved into a smile. "Half a month ago, I was injured, wasn’t I? Since I was near the Yun residence, I stayed there. Would you have wanted me, an injured person, to endure the bumpy carriage ride back? If my injuries had worsened, wouldn’t you have been heartbroken, Old Madam?"

Her tone softened, and the old madam had no choice but to suppress her anger.

What else could she do? At her age, was she supposed to exchange barbs with her granddaughter-in-law?

Moreover, the Xie family was indeed in the wrong. They had deceived Yun Chu and driven He Shi to her death...

"Since you’ve returned, rest well." The old madam waved her hand. "There are many matters waiting for you to handle. Don’t overexert yourself."

After leaving Anshou Hall, Yun Chu returned to Shengju.

She had once considered this place her home, but after staying at the Yun residence for half a month, she realized that the true home in her heart would always be the Yun mansion.

As soon as she sat down, people from the rear courtyard came to pay their respects, including Concubine Tao, who had not yet completed her month of confinement.

Concubine Tao was still young, and after twenty days of recovery, she looked almost the same as before. However, her premature child was frail, and worry lingered between her brows.

"I heard that Madam was injured. I was so worried." Tingyu spoke up. "I wanted to attend to Madam, but with my current status, it’s difficult to enter the Yun mansion again. I hope Madam can forgive me."

Jiang Concubine looked at Yun Chu. "Madam has lost some weight. If Madam doesn’t mind, I can prepare some nourishing soups for Madam every day for the past half month."

Yun Chu smiled and agreed.

"Madam..." Concubine Tao hesitated before speaking. "I heard that Madam previously consulted Physician Si. Would it be possible to ask Physician Si to also examine Kang Ge?"

Yun Chu replied indifferently, "Physician Si has already left the capital. Even the imperial family cannot summon him, let alone me."

In her past life, Xie Shikang had been born weak. Concubine Tao had cared for him for a few months, but the child’s health had only worsened. So, she had sent him to Yun Chu.

To save the child, Yun Chu had traveled for over two months by boat and carriage to Qingshou in the south to seek a divine physician...

It was during that time away from the capital that something had happened to the Yun family. Her sister-in-law had lost the child she was carrying. Later, when she asked her mother, she couldn’t get any clear answers.

"Madam, what should I do about Kang Ge?" Concubine Tao began to cry. "He vomits as soon as he drinks milk. He can’t keep anything down, and he’s not gaining weight. He’s getting thinner and thinner. I... I can’t raise Kang Ge..."

She hated He Shi to death. If it weren’t for that wretched woman, she wouldn’t have gone into premature labor, and Kang Ge wouldn’t be suffering like this.

He Shi was already dead, but Kang Ge still had to endure such hardship...

"Concubine Tao, you are Kang Ge’s birth mother. If even you can’t raise him, no one else can." Yun Chu said. "The child is young. You need to be patient. From now on, you don’t need to come for the morning greetings. Spend more time taking care of Kang Ge."

Concubine Tao sobbed.

Madam didn’t care anymore. The adults certainly wouldn’t. Her Kang Ge was suffering too much.

Yun Chu lowered her head and sipped her tea.

In her past life, Xie Shikang had survived only because she had sought out famous physicians everywhere. But what had the child she had saved with her own hands done?

Forget it. Things that couldn’t happen in this life were better left unmentioned.

Yun Chu waved her hand, dismissing everyone in the room. Xie Pin stayed behind to give her a detailed report on the household affairs over the past half month.

Yun Chu listened absentmindedly. After Xie Pin finished, she said, "Pin’er, you’ve made a lot of progress. You’ve done well."

Xie Pin’s face lit up with a smile.

Madam Zhou had said that her actions lacked method and often criticized her. For a moment, she had actually believed that she was incompetent.

Fortunately, her mother had given her encouragement. She would learn more about managing a household. Only then could she stand firm in the Anning Prince’s residence when the time came.

Thinking of the Anning Prince’s residence, Xie Pin’s smile immediately vanished. She pinched her fingers and said, "Mother, the dowry Father prepared for me was all recorded on a list. But over these days, everything has been taken away. On my dowry list, only ten bedding quilts remain..."

Yun Chu looked at her. "And then?"

"I... I am the future Princess Consort of Anning!" Xie Pin was on the verge of tears. "As a princess consort, with so little dowry, won’t this make people look down on me? It’s not that I care about being looked down on, but I’m afraid outsiders will look down on our Xie family..."

Yun Chu’s expression was ambiguous, as if smiling yet not. "So, Pin’er, you want me to prepare a dowry for you?"

Xie Pin didn’t dare meet her gaze and lowered her head.

Wasn’t it natural for a mother to prepare a dowry for her daughter? But when her mother asked it like this, she found herself at a loss for words.

"Your father’s official career has not been going well lately." Yun Chu’s voice was calm. "The Xie family is but a humble one. Where would a daughter’s dowry come from? If the dowry is too extravagant, it will surely attract the attention of the Censorate. You wouldn’t want your father to be impeached, would you?"

Xie Pin bit her lip.

No matter how humble the family was, they couldn’t possibly fail to prepare a proper dowry.

Even a family that sold tofu on the street could prepare a sixteen-sedans dowry for their daughter’s marriage. And yet, for her...

Her mother wasn’t afraid of the Censorate impeaching her father. She simply didn’t want to spend silver on her. Because her mother knew she was the daughter of Concubine He...

Originally, her mother had been so open-hearted with her, teaching her everything. But now, she had suddenly changed.

It was all He Shi’s fault. Why had she given birth to her but couldn’t secure a good future for her? Why hadn’t she died cleanly before everything was discovered...

---

chapters.title: An Additional Concubine
chapters.content:
Xie Pin left in a daze.

Tingxue entered and reported, "Madam, over the past half month, the master has been taking his medicine. The dregs in the medicine pot have all been personally handled by this servant..."

Yun Chu nodded.

If it weren’t for the fact that murder was against the law, and if she weren’t afraid of the scandal of a Yun family woman killing her husband spreading, she would have ended Xie Jingyu’s life with a single blade.

But there was still a long time ahead. She would take it slow, gradually destroying Xie Jingyu’s spirit and body, to avenge her two children who had died tragically.

Before long, Chen Defu followed Tingshuang into the side hall. Bowing, he reported, "Madam, the matter you instructed has been taken care of. When the second young master heard about it, he caused a huge commotion at the estate and only quieted down after receiving a whipping from the master."

Yun Chu smiled.

She had ordered someone to tell Xie Shi that He Shi had been forced to her death by a son and a daughter working together.

She had also conveniently told Xie Shi that his leg injury could have been cured, but because Xie Shian had intervened, the Xie family had left it untreated.

Xie Shi was the kind of person who would retaliate for the smallest grievance. After learning these two things, he was bound to cause a scene.

She just needed to find an opportunity to bring Xie Shi back.

"And what about He Xu? There hasn’t been much movement from him in Jizhou." Chen Defu asked. "Should we continue to have someone keep an eye on him?"

Yun Chu nodded. "That man still has great use."

With He Lingchong dead, He Xu had become the most crucial figure. Of course, he had to be kept around.

Chen Defu made a note of it. Then, he handed Yun Chu the account books for the ice shop over the past half month.

Yun Chu flipped through them. Even she was surprised to find that the net profit had reached over a hundred thousand taels of silver. With this sum, she could do almost anything.

The hot spring estate would be completed in about a month. By the time deep autumn arrived, it would be ready to open its doors to guests. But before that, she needed to find an ally.

In her past life, this estate had ended up in the hands of one of the four consorts of the imperial harem, Consort Hui. Consort Hui was the birth mother of the Second Prince... The Second Prince had always had a reputation for being virtuous and was highly regarded by the common people. If she hadn’t discovered before her death that Xie Shian was connected to the Second Prince, she would have truly believed that the Second Prince was someone who didn’t scheme or compete...

Xie Shian had failed to win over the Yun family for the Second Prince, so he had resorted to the most ruthless move.

Xie Shian was a blade in the Second Prince’s hand, but the one who had truly orchestrated the downfall of so many in the Yun family was the Second Prince himself.

Fortunately, her father would be returning to the capital soon. She would tell him everything in detail...

As for the matter of the hot spring estate’s ally, she needed to think carefully. There were only a few people who could rival Consort Hui and the Second Prince...

The night passed quietly.

The next morning, after everyone had paid their respects, Yun Chu was about to call for a seamstress to make a few new clothes when Tingfeng rushed in. "Madam, someone from the palace has arrived!"

Yun Chu set aside her affairs and rose to go to the front courtyard.

It turned out to be an old acquaintance, Madam Fu, who served De Consort. Some time ago, she had stayed at the Xie residence for half a month to teach Xie Pin etiquette. After Xie Pin had learned enough, she had returned to the palace.

This time, she brought a message from De Consort: "De Consort invites Madam Xie and Miss Xie to the palace for tea."

Xie Pin nervously clutched the handkerchief in her hands.

The last time she had entered the palace, the memories were still vivid. She was afraid that this time would be the same...

However, this time, De Consort had also invited her mother. Her mother was the eldest daughter of the Yun family. De Consort probably wouldn’t dare to disrespect her mother.

With this thought, she finally felt at ease.

Yun Chu and Xie Pin took a carriage to the palace gates and followed Madam Fu all the way to the entrance of De Consort’s Changqing Palace.

"Madam Xie and Miss Xie, please wait a moment."

Madam Fu left the two of them at the palace doors and stepped into the main hall.

Xie Pin was so nervous that she wrung her hands. Fortunately, they didn’t have to wait long. Madam Fu quickly returned and ushered them inside.

"Greetings to De Consort. May De Consort be in good health."

Yun Chu performed a graceful court curtsy.

"Madam Xie, no need for formalities. Please, take a seat." De Consort smiled and granted them seats.

Xie Pin didn’t dare to sit. She stood beside Yun Chu, her gaze lowered, carefully maintaining her posture to avoid any mistakes.

Yun Chu, on the other hand, appeared completely at ease.

Before her marriage, she had often accompanied her mother to palace banquets. She could maintain her composure even before the Emperor, let alone a consort.

"You truly live up to being the daughter of a general’s family." De Consort smiled. "I invited Madam Xie to the palace because there is something I need to inform you about."

Yun Chu set down her teacup. "Please, Your Highness."

"The wedding date between Miss Xie and the Fourth Prince is approaching. I’ve been feeling rather anxious as well." De Consort spoke as if making casual conversation. "Recently, His Majesty told me that the Fourth Prince’s courtyard is a bit empty. He asked me to select a girl to accompany Miss Xie when she marries into the Anning Prince’s residence as a concubine. That way, they can look after each other."

Xie Pin’s face paled.

She had never expected to hear such words upon entering the palace. This was more humiliating than a slap to the face.

"What’s the matter with Miss Xie’s expression?" De Consort glanced at her. "Do you have any objections?"

"I... I wouldn’t dare." Xie Pin lowered her head, suppressing the emotions in her voice as she spoke carefully. "I was just curious about who the other young lady is."

"It’s the eldest daughter of the Shi family." De Consort smiled. "She’s two years older than you. But since you’ll be the princess consort, even if she’s older, she’ll still have to address you as elder sister."

Xie Pin’s heart sank to the bottom of a valley.

The Shi family was a third-rank noble family. The eldest daughter of the Shi family was the daughter of the previous Madam Shi. Although she was not favored by her stepmother, she was still the legitimate eldest daughter. A legitimate eldest daughter from a third-rank family as a concubine... while she, the daughter of an official’s concubine, was the principal wife. Both of them marrying into the prince’s residence on the same day, she didn’t dare to imagine what awaited her.

She tightly clenched her palm and said insincerely, "It is my fortune to serve the prince alongside Miss Shi."

"You have such an understanding. That’s good." De Consort picked up her teacup. "After becoming the Princess Consort of Anning, you must be magnanimous and tolerant as the mistress. Don’t let me hear any petty rumors about jealousy."

Xie Pin bowed her head deeply. "Yes, I will remember."

As they left Changqing Palace, Xie Pin could no longer hold back her tears, which streamed down her face. "Mother, what should I do? What should I do in the future..."

Without her husband’s favor and with an additional concubine of much higher status and background, she truly didn’t know what to do.

"Wipe away your tears." Yun Chu said. "If someone sees you, they’ll think you’ve been wronged in De Consort’s palace. There will be even greater hardships ahead. As a royal prince, he won’t have just one concubine. Once you’re married, De Consort will quickly arrange for a second one. If all you do is cry, will crying solve anything? Remember, you are the princess consort. Your status is here. No one can do anything to you."

Xie Pin forced her tears back.

Yes, she was the principal wife. In the Anning Prince’s residence, she would be like a mother. Her mother could do whatever she wanted in the Xie family without anyone daring to say a word. When she went to the prince’s residence, even Miss Shi would have to listen to her orders. What was there to fear?

Yun Chu and Xie Pin reached the palace gates. They turned to thank the eunuch who had led them out and gave him a tip.

At that moment, a carriage slowly stopped at the palace gates.

Yun Chu looked up and saw Chu Yi, the Prince of Pingxi.

chapters.title: The Grand General Returns to Court
chapters.content:
The grand palace gates towered, making the people below seem especially small.

Chu Yi, dressed in a dark purple court robe, had just dismounted from his carriage when he spotted a graceful figure in the distance.

Unconsciously, his mind flashed back to the scene in the bandit mountain cabin, the gruesome wound, the porcelain-like skin... It had been their first meeting since that day.

Though he had visited the Yun residence many times, each time he only spoke with Yun Ze in the study, while the two children went in to see her.

On the way home from the Yun residence, Yu Ge’er was always cheerful, chattering nonstop, and Changsheng would smile with pursed lips.

He knew the children liked being with the woman before him.

Yun Chu not only saw the Prince of Pingxi but also noticed another man stepping down from the carriage with him; it was the Second Prince, the Duke of Gongxi.

She lowered her gaze and led Xie Pin forward.

With a graceful curtsy, she said, "Greetings to the Duke of Gongxi."

"Greetings to the Prince of Pingxi."

The Duke of Gongxi smiled warmly. "Lady Xie is too courteous."

For some reason, Chu Yi felt an inexplicable discomfort at the Duke addressing her as "Lady Xie."

"Word has it Lady Xie was unwell," the Duke of Gongxi began. "I hope you are feeling better?"

"Thank you for your concern, Your Highness. I am much improved," Yun Chu replied calmly, though her eyes were icy.

There were many princes in the palace. Currently, only the first four had been enfeoffed. Once the other princes came of age, the imperial court and harem would gradually fall into chaos.

At that time, the Yun family had maintained their integrity, refusing to involve themselves in the struggle for the throne. The Second Prince, in an attempt to win over the Yun family, had visited them three times to no avail. So he used Xie Shian as a pawn, directly expelling the Yun family from the court...

Now, the Xie family was in her grasp.

But taking revenge on the Second Prince was too difficult...

Moreover, even if the Second Prince were truly overthrown, another would surely take his place to court the Yun family...

She decided not to dwell on what she couldn’t understand. Her father would return to court soon, and she could discuss it thoroughly with him and her grandfather then. There would surely be a solution.

"Your Highnesses, this humble wife and my daughter will take our leave now."

Yun Chu curtsied and, taking Xie Pin’s hand, boarded the Yun family carriage.

"Such a waste," the Duke of Gongxi sighed as he watched the carriage disappear from the palace gates. "The Yun family’s legitimate eldest daughter, with her status, should have married into the imperial family. Yet she became the wife of a commoner. Third Brother, don’t you think it’s a pity?"

Years ago, when his father had chosen a consort for him, he had actually preferred the Yun family. However, there had been no suitable-aged daughters at the time. There were distant relatives, but he had not been interested.

Of course, his current consort, the second legitimate daughter of the Grand Scholar, was not bad either. It was just that without military power in his hands, it was somewhat regretful.

Chu Yi said indifferently, "Second Brother, please do not speak such words again. It tarnishes Lady Xie’s reputation."

The Duke of Gongxi chuckled. "If it weren’t for the fact that you already have a pair of children, I would suspect you aren’t a man."

Just now, that had been the former most beautiful woman in the capital, the one who had once been the talk of the town. Even he, who was not fond of women, felt a slight stir in his heart upon seeing her.

Yet his third brother hadn’t even glanced her way.

No wonder Concubine Yin was always worried about the Third Prince’s marriage. A man with no interest in women naturally wouldn’t want to take a wife.

Chu Yi took a step forward.

In truth, when Yun Chu had appeared just now, he hadn’t dared to look at her, afraid of being rude, afraid of offending her...

The two entered the palace and went straight to the imperial study.

However, the emperor was busy. A eunuch said to them, "His Majesty is currently in the inner hall with Concubine Zhou. Please wait, Your Highnesses."

Chu Yi’s expression remained impassive.

Every time he came for an audience, his father was either with Concubine Zhou or Concubine Li... In short, there was always a concubine in the hall.

After waiting about a quarter of an hour, Concubine Zhou emerged from the inner hall, and the two princes followed the eunuch inside.

The emperor, seated on the dragon throne, said, "I summoned you both because there is a matter I need you to handle. The Grand General of the State, who has repelled enemy forces, defended our territory, and protected our people, is a true hero. The Grand General will arrive in the capital soon. You two shall represent me in welcoming him."

Both princes responded in unison, "Your sons accept the decree!"

The Grand General of the State was the person the emperor trusted the most, commanding 300,000 troops. Every five years, when the Grand General returned to the capital to report, the emperor would bestow the greatest rewards. It was no exaggeration to say the entire nation celebrated.

The Duke of Gongxi and the Prince of Pingxi, representing the emperor, rode on fine horses, leading dozens of court officials to the outskirts of the capital to welcome the returning Grand General of the State, Yun Silin.

Yun Silin could only return to the capital once every five years. Leading 300 personal guards, it took half a month of riding from the borderlands to reach the capital.

When they were still 70 or 80 li away from the capital, they caught sight of the two princes they hadn’t seen in a long time. Yun Silin quickly dismounted. "This humble servant greets the Duke of Gongxi and the Prince of Pingxi!"

"Grand General, please rise!" The Duke of Gongxi was quicker than Chu Yi in helping Yun Silin up. "The Grand General has risked life and limb for our dynasty. My brother and I are unworthy of such a greeting. His Majesty and the officials have prepared strong liquor, awaiting the Grand General’s entry into the city!"

Yun Silin cupped his hands in salute, then took the reins and mounted his horse, riding toward the capital with the others.

The common people in the city were already in high spirits.

For a hundred years, the Yun family had defended the nation against foreign invasions, protecting every inch of territory and every citizen... Now that the people lived in peace, many from the Yun family had died on the battlefield, never to return.

"Look! The Grand General of the State has returned!"

"The last time I saw the Grand General was five years ago. Five years later, the Grand General is still as heroic as ever!"

"I prayed for a talisman for the Grand General, hoping he lives to ninety-nine. If the Grand General dies, who will protect our nation?"

"The Yun family’s next generation hasn’t produced a single general!"

"Generations of the Yun family have died on the battlefield. Isn’t that enough? The merits of their ancestors are sufficient. The descendants of the Yun family should live in peace and stability."

...

The emperor, accompanied by civil and military officials, welcomed the Grand General of the State at the city gates.

The Grand General and his personal guards knelt and kowtowed. The emperor ordered a cup of strong liquor to be served to each of the returning men.

"Western frontier enemies are relentless, repeatedly invading our territory. It is all thanks to the Yun family’s generations of defense!" The emperor descended from the city tower and walked to Yun Silin. "A heavenly qilin has its kind, but how can ants in their holes escape? Grand General of the State, upon your return to the capital, I shall remove your battle robe!"

The emperor personally removed Yun Silin’s battle robe.

This was the highest honor.

The battle robe was handed to the deputy general beside them. The emperor picked up a wine cup and clinked it with Yun Silin’s. "To share a drink with you, General, is my honor. Cheers."

"Cheers!"

"Cheers!"

The 300 personal guards of the Yun family and the entire court raised their cups simultaneously.

After the celebration, the general entered the city.

Countless commoners lined the streets to welcome the Grand General’s return. Yun Chu was also in a tavern on the second floor of a street.

Standing by the railing on the second floor, she immediately spotted her father entering the city with the emperor. Her father didn’t seem much different from her memories, commanding and inviolable. Just standing there, he could make enemies tremble in fear without a fight...

Yun Chu watched as her father followed the emperor into the imperial city.

She turned and boarded a carriage back to the Yun residence.

Her father would only return home after reporting to the emperor. Countless officials would come to pay their respects. Today, the Yun residence was destined to be busy.

---

chapters.title: Nightmares Every Night
chapters.content:
It was already the beginning of the eighth month, and the sun was scorching.

With the Grand General of the State back in the capital, guests came and went. Every five years at this time, the Yun family would host a banquet to entertain their visitors.

When Yun Chu arrived, the courtyard was already filled with many guests. Men and women were not seated separately but arranged by official rank, with each family at a table.

As soon as she arrived, the Xie family did as well.

Xie Jingyu arrived with Xie Shian and Xie Pin.

"Mother," Xie Shian and Xie Pin called out in unison.

Yun Chu nodded. "There are many distinguished guests today. Be careful, both of you."

"An Ge’er will follow me. Pin Jie’er, stay close to your mother," Xie Jingyu said. "Don’t say anything you shouldn’t. Don’t embarrass your maternal grandfather."

The four of them entered the Yun family’s gates together.

Once inside, Xie Jingyu saw many high-ranking officials he could never usually associate with, such as the Grand Preceptor, the Grand Tutor, the Six Ministers, and the Grand Secretaries of the Cabinet... Essentially, all the most important officials in the court were present. They gathered in groups of three or five, chatting casually without the emperor present.

Since the Grand General had not yet returned to the Yun residence, only Yun Ze and some collateral branches of the Yun family were there to receive the male guests. Although the younger generation of the Yun family did not hold high ranks, which of the first or second-rank officials dared to show them disrespect?

"Director Xie," his colleague, Director Yuan, came over to greet him. "With General Yun back in the capital, he will probably stay for some time. As his son-in-law, you will have the chance to drink with the current first-rank general. How envious I am."

Xie Jingyu naturally heard the sarcasm in his words, mocking him for relying on the Yun family, for relying on his father-in-law.

He responded coolly, "Then Director Yuan can keep envying."

Director Yuan was taken aback.

Indeed, with backing, one had confidence.

He took a deep breath. "I just feel that Director Xie’s complexion isn’t very good. There are dark circles under your eyes. I don’t know if you’re ill or if you’ve caught something bad. Director Xie, you should find someone to take a look when you have time."

He was just spouting nonsense to save face.

Unexpectedly, his words struck a chord with Xie Jingyu. Ever since He Shi’s death, he had been plagued by nightmares every night and hadn’t had a good night’s sleep.

He felt his body growing weaker, often feeling fatigued. He knew it was from lack of sleep... It seemed he needed to find a physician, get some sleeping medicine, and sleep soundly. Then, perhaps, He Shi would stop haunting his dreams.

"Father, there are so many guests. Uncle is struggling to greet them all," Xie Shian said. "Father, go help."

Xie Jingyu ignored Director Yuan’s gaze and walked toward Yun Ze.

However, everyone knew that the Yun family’s eldest daughter had stayed at her maiden home for half a month not long ago. There must be some discord in her marriage.

Moreover, after Xie Jingyu entered, the Yun family members did not go up to greet him proactively. Especially Yun Ze, who hadn’t even glanced at Xie Jingyu.

What this represented was self-evident.

Those court officials were all astute. None of them had any real intention of engaging in deep conversation with Xie Jingyu.

The Xie father and son sat on the sidelines, while Yun Chu’s area was lively.

Many court officials were still in the palace accompanying the emperor, so among the current guests, there were more women and young ladies. The courtyard was filled with women.

"Word has it that on his way back to the capital, General Yun also eliminated three bandit dens without losing a single soldier. General Yun truly commands his troops like a god."

"Isn’t that right? With General Yun guarding the western frontier, my heart is at ease."

"Looking at it, Madam Yun seems to be with child. What a double blessing!"

"Soon, the Yun family’s second daughter will marry. Then we’ll have to thicken our skins to ask for a cup of wedding wine."

...

Lin Shi smiled. "We’re arranging for people to deliver invitations to each household. If you have time, come and drink a cup of wedding wine, share in the joy."

As they spoke, Madam Tan arrived with her eldest legitimate daughter, Du Ling.

After the incident at Qing’an Temple, Yun Chu had specifically gone to the Du family to inquire about the news. Knowing that Du Ying had not done anything drastic, she was relieved.

Lin Shi welcomed Madam Tan, while Yun Chu approached Du Ling. "Madam Ji."

Du Ling pursed her lips.

Once close friends, but after the incident at Qing’an Temple, where Yun Chu had used her, and Du Ying had cried for a whole month, she actually held some resentment toward Yun Chu.

However, she also knew that at that time, Yun Chu’s illegitimate daughter had schemed against the Fourth Prince. In that situation, Yun Chu had no choice but to use her as a witness to force the Fourth Prince to take responsibility.

Speaking of which, she really had to thank Yun Chu’s illegitimate daughter. Because she had secretly investigated the Fourth Prince, she discovered that in the rear courtyard of the Prince of Anning’s residence, there were at least ten concubines.

She had thrown the facts in Du Ying’s face, and only then did her sister finally stop pining for the Fourth Prince.

Yesterday, the Virtuous Consort had found a concubine for the Fourth Prince, who entered the palace on the same day as the official consort, a slap to the consort’s face.

"Congratulations, Miss Xie," Du Ling said with a smirk, looking at Xie Pin behind Yun Chu. "Soon, you’ll get your wish to marry into the Prince of Anning’s residence. With so many sisters to keep you company, how do you feel, Miss Xie?"

Xie Pin’s face paled.

She forced a smile. "Marrying the Prince of Anning and becoming his consort, bearing children for the imperial family with the sisters of the prince’s residence, is my honor."

Du Ling scoffed.

Xie Pin’s face turned even paler. Unable to bear Du Ling’s gaze, she found an excuse and went elsewhere.

"Lady Xie, your daughter schemed her way to the Fourth Prince. How impressive," Du Ling said. "Be careful she doesn’t scheme against you in the future."

Yun Chu knew Du Ling was concerned for her. The incident at Qing’an Temple had completely passed.

She changed her address. "Ling Ling, when you have time, come to the Xie residence for tea. Let’s have a good catch-up."

Du Ling hmphed. "Then you’ll have to send an invitation. I’ll have to consider carefully whether to go or not."

The two exchanged a smile, and for a moment, it felt as if time had returned to when they were both unmarried.

At this moment, a lively commotion came from the Yun residence’s gates. Yun Chu looked over and saw that her father had returned, accompanied by many people. Several princes had come along, including the Crown Prince, who was ill and hadn’t come, but the Second Prince, Third Prince, Fourth Prince, and Eighth Prince were all present.

The Third Prince, the Prince of Pingxi, had come because he had initially followed General Yun to the battlefield and earned military merits. The two were close friends despite the age difference.

The Fourth Prince, the Prince of Anning, had come because his marriage had been arranged with the Xie family, which was related to the Yun family by marriage. Naturally, he had to attend.

As for the Eighth Prince, he was the son of Consort Yun in the palace. His maternal uncle had returned to the capital, so of course he had come to join in the festivities.

And the Second Prince... Yun Chu knew very well why he had come to the Yun family. He probably intended to win over the Yun family from this point onward.

The people in the courtyard all greeted the princes, bowing before taking their seats.

Xie Pin sat beside Yun Chu, her gaze fixed on the Prince of Anning, who was not too far from her. In truth, she and the Prince of Anning had not met many times.

The first time was at the Grand Princess’s residence. The Fourth Prince had picked up a handkerchief for her and pinned a flower in her hair. She had felt they shared mutual affection.

The second time was at Qing’an Temple...

The third time was at Consort De’s Changqing Palace, where he had watched her punishment without a flicker of emotion.

This was their fourth meeting, and her future husband hadn’t even spared her a glance...

chapters.title: What Should the Yun Family Do?
chapters.content:
The banquet hall was lively.

Duke Gongxi stood up first, raising his wine cup: "On behalf of the imperial family, the court officials, and all the people, I toast to the Great General of the Pillars of the State!"

Everyone present stood up and raised their cups as well.

Since they were all family sitting at one table, many couldn't help but whisper softly.

"Generations of the Yun family have served in the military, but unfortunately, the next generation has no one to succeed the Great General of the Pillars of the State."

"I wonder who will be the next to command the 300,000-strong army."

"Prince Pingxi once followed General Yun into battle, brave and skilled in combat. If General Yun can no longer fight, the military tally should fall to Prince Pingxi."

"Do you think the Empress would agree to Prince Pingxi holding military power? Wouldn't that become the greatest threat to the Crown Prince..."

Everyone's discussions were brief and to the point.

Yun Chu sat quietly at her seat, eating. From the corner of her eye, she saw Lao Ba suddenly leave his seat and sneak over to Jiang Ge'er.

She was a bit surprised. Lao Ba and Jiang Ge'er only met occasionally at palace banquets. When did their relationship become so close?

As she pondered, she saw Lao Ba suddenly take out an exquisite sword from his sleeve. It was only as long as a child's arm, small but delicate.

Jiang Ge'er drew the sword, and the gleam was dazzling. Fearing discovery, he quickly hid the treasure sword back into his sleeve.

Yun Chu sighed.

It turned out that Jiang Ge'er had loved playing with swords since he was so young.

In her previous life, this child left the Yun family at the age of 15, secretly joined the military camp, but before he could make a name for himself, the Yun family fell into disaster and he was taken back...

The Yun family's children had the blood of a military family in their bones, but they couldn't openly love what they loved.

"Madam." Xie Jingyu, who was sitting next to her, suddenly spoke, "Let An Ge'er and Ping Jie'er go to meet their maternal grandfather."

Yun Chu's expression was indifferent: "No need to rush at this moment."

Xie Jingyu was secretly annoyed.

Why was there no need to rush?

It was precisely because most of the important ministers were present. At this moment, letting the children meet their maternal grandfather, whom they had never seen before, as their maternal grandfather, Yun Silin would surely give the children a meeting gift. This would be a public acknowledgment of the children's status. Who would dare to look down on An Ge'er and Ping Jie'er then?

But Yun Chu was unwilling.

Without Yun Chu leading them, if the two children went rashly, they would only become a laughingstock.

Xie Jingyu took a sip of wine to suppress his eagerness.

Yun Chu was impatient sitting with him and even more unwilling to socialize with the people present as Madam Xie.

After eating until she was 70% full, she stood up, took some delicious dishes, had the maids put them in a food box, and carried it to the residence of Old General Yun.

Old General Yun had trouble with his legs and spent most of the day lying on a couch. Naturally, he did not attend the banquet in the front courtyard, so the courtyard appeared cold and quiet.

"Grandfather!"

Yun Chu cheerfully called out and stepped inside.

"I brought you braised lion's head and roast duck..."

Just as she placed the food box on the table, she felt a gust of wind coming from above. She raised her hand and caught a teacup.

"Finally, you have some skills." Old General Yun laughed heartily, "To be able to teach you like this, it seems Autumn Tong has some ability."

Yun Chu's face lit up with a bright smile: "Why doesn't Grandfather praise me for being a good learner?"

Old General Yun coldly snorted: "You little girl, you like to slack off the most. When you were five or six years old, every time I asked you to practice, you would run to your grandmother's room to hide..."

Mentioning his wife, Old General Yun's expression darkened slightly.

The men of the Yun family were mostly on the battlefield. It was usually the men who died first, and the women who became widows. He was the exception, becoming an old widower.

Yun Chu also thought of her grandmother. The only fortune was that when her grandmother passed away, her grandfather was by her side, so there were no regrets...

As she was lost in thought, she heard a noise behind her.

She was about to turn around when a pair of hands pressed down on her shoulders, pushing her against the wall.

She thought it was a bandit who had sneaked into the Yun family to assassinate, but then she heard her father's hearty laughter.

"Hearing the old man praise you, I thought you had learned well." Yun Silin let go of her, "But your skills are still too poor. If you go to the battlefield like this, you'll just be giving away your head."

"Our Yun family doesn't need women on the battlefield!" Old General Yun scoffed, "With so many guests in the front courtyard, what are you doing here?"

"Aren't I here to see you, old man?" Yun Silin sat down at the table, stuffed a lion's head into his mouth, "In the front courtyard, a bunch of people are toasting me, my stomach is full of wine, and I finally get to eat a lion's head."

The old general displeasedly said: "This is what Chu'er brought for me. You scram."

Yun Silin refused and instead snatched the plate away, deliberately making the old general so angry that his beard bristled.

Yun Chu couldn't help but laugh.

This was family. Even after five years apart, there was no estrangement at all.

After teasing his old father, Yun Silin placed the lion's head back on the table, his gaze falling on Yun Chu.

Five years ago, when he returned to the capital, Chu'er got married, and he, as her father, personally sent her off in a grand sedan chair. After five years, she was no longer the girl she used to be.

Just now at the banquet, he saw the son and daughter by her side, the daughter was 13, and the son was 12.

Although the Yun family had written to inform him of these things long ago, he still felt a sense of depression... That scoundrel from the Xie family, when he asked to marry Chu'er, actually dared to hide such a big matter...

But Chu'er could no longer have her own children, so the matter of Xie Jingyu having children before marriage seemed impossible to pursue...

"Father, why are you looking at me like that?" Yun Chu showed a relaxed smile. She sat down and, after the two elders had eaten enough, she spoke, "Father, have you ever thought about giving up military power?"

Yun Silin thought he had misheard and cupped his ear: "What?"

"An ancient saying goes, 'When the cunning hare is dead, the good hound is boiled; when the enemy state is destroyed, the plotting minister perishes.'" Yun Chu said softly, "There will come a day when Father leads the army to occupy the Western Frontier. By then, will our Yun family, like that good hound, be at the mercy of others?"

"Impossible!" Old General Yun spoke up, "I understand what Chu'er means. You're afraid that the Yun family's high merits will alarm the Emperor, causing him to fear us. This reasoning, both your father and I understand. Therefore, the Yun family has long learned to restrain its prominence. For example, the Yun family's collateral branches hold offices no higher than the fifth rank. Also, the Yun family's main branch can only marry and wed below their status. Our Yun family has fully demonstrated its loyalty, and the Emperor also knows that the Yun family has been loyal for generations. He will certainly not do such a thing."

"But the Emperor is getting old." Yun Chu continued, "When people get old, they are easily influenced by the voices around them, making judgments against their true intentions. Now, the princes in various palaces are growing up, and the struggle for the succession is about to begin. Our Yun family, holding heavy military power, will certainly become the object of competition among the various palaces. Even if the Yun family has no such intention, we will be framed with false charges. If the Emperor listens to slander, then what will become of the Yun family?"

---

chapters.title: I Had a Dream
chapters.content:
"Some time ago, I had a dream."

Yun Chu began slowly.

"In the dream, it was probably more than ten years later. Father led the Yun family army to defeat the Western Frontier, and the vast Western Frontier was incorporated into the territory. The Yun family achieved such great merit, and the whole country celebrated... It was at that time that someone suddenly submitted a memorial, saying that the Yun family intended to rebel. They even found letters proving that the Yun family had colluded with foreign countries. The Emperor ordered a thorough investigation. The result of the investigation was that the Yun family had colluded with foreign countries and attempted to support the Eighth Prince to the throne. With both human and physical evidence, it shocked the court and the public. All 100+ members of the Yun family were thrown into the heavenly prison, and the family was confiscated!"

"Grandfather, to prove the Yun family's innocence with his own life, used this very sword to cut his own throat!"

Yun Chu looked at the big sword placed on the table. This sword, which had beheaded countless enemies, was Grandfather's merit, but in the end...

She continued, "Father achieved such great merit and should have returned to the capital to receive rewards. But as soon as he entered the capital, he was arrested and thrown into an underground prison... Big Brother was the first to be imprisoned and died after a few days of torture. Mother and Big Sister-in-law couldn't bear the prison life and also died... Jiang Ge'er and the rest of the Yun family were all sent to the execution ground..."

She couldn't continue and lowered her head to cover the pain in her eyes.

"And you? What about you?" Yun Silin pressed, "Chu'er, you are a married daughter. Even if the Yun family is in trouble, it shouldn't affect you, right?"

Yun Chu raised her head and smiled: "I am a married daughter, but I am still a Yun. The Xie family, fearing implication, forced me to drink poison."

Behind her, Yun Ze walked in, his eyes full of disbelief: "So, Chu'er, is this the reason for your recent marital discord with Xie Jingyu?"

No wonder recently, no matter what happened in the Xie family, Chu'er never mentioned returning to the Yun family. He had thought it was because of Concubine He.

But a few years ago, when Cong Rain became a concubine, Chu'er didn't have a falling out with the Xie family either. So, in fact, it was this dream that caused the rift between Chu'er and the Xie family?

"You can have such a dream, which shows that you worry daily about the Yun family's downfall. That's not surprising because the Yun family has indeed reached too high a position and cannot afford any mistakes. But—" Yun Ze looked at her, "How could you dream that the Xie family would give you poison to drink? 'Day has its thoughts, night has its dreams.' In daily life, has the Xie family done something excessive to you, making you fear they would kill you?"

"Big Brother, the focus is not on the Xie family, but on our Yun family." Yun Chu said, "In more than ten years, the Yun family might be executed. What can we do now to avoid such an outcome?"

"Dreams are the opposite of reality. Chu'er, don't scare yourself." Yun Silin patted her shoulder, "Tell your father, what grievances has that scoundrel Xie Jingyu caused you? Your father will teach him a lesson."

Yun Chu gave a bitter smile.

Xie Jingyu's life was almost over; there was no need for her father to intervene.

The entire Xie family, she could handle alone. But as a married daughter, she couldn't influence the path the Yun family took. Therefore, she could only discuss it with her father and brothers.

But it was obvious that the three men in front of her didn't believe her dream at all. Instead, they were more concerned about whether she had been wronged in the Xie family.

"My dream is not only about the Yun family but also some things that will happen in the future." Yun Chu said, "I dreamed that the Crown Prince was seriously ill, and indeed, the Crown Prince fell ill. I dreamed that Xie Shian became the top scholar, and that was also the case. I also dreamed that next, Father will receive an imperial decree to lead people to the Southern Frontier to execute the General of Chariots and Cavalry..."

Old General Yun's eyes widened in shock.

The Crown Prince had indeed been ill recently and was still bedridden.

Xie Shian had indeed become the top scholar in the imperial examination, and the Xie family had even hosted a banquet for guests.

But receiving an imperial decree to go to the Southern Frontier?

To execute the General of Chariots and Cavalry?

That seemed impossible.

Their Yun family had always been stationed in the Western Frontier. If they were sent to the Southern Frontier, the Western Frontier would be left vulnerable.

Moreover, the General of Chariots and Cavalry was the Emperor's nephew from the Empress Dowager's family, a general highly valued by the Emperor. How could someone be sent to execute him?

"I know none of you believe me." Yun Chu said slowly, "Then just wait and see."

Her serious expression made the three generations of Yun family men also become solemn.

At this moment, a voice came from the courtyard: "Is General Yun here? The Minister of War has urgent matters to discuss with General Yun."

"Everything Chu'er just said, keep it to yourselves." Old General Yun said, "We'll talk about this after the Emperor issues the decree. Dismissed."

Yun Silin walked out and saw Prince Pingxi, Chu Yi. He smiled and gave Chu Yi a punch: "I heard that all the bandits within a hundred miles of the capital have been driven out or killed by you. Impressive, impressive."

"No matter how impressive, it's not as good as General Yun. The title of Great General of the Pillars of the State makes the neighboring small countries tremble in fear, enhancing our national prestige." Chu Yi took the punch, "The Minister of War is a bit anxious. General Yun, please go quickly."

Yun Silin nodded and quickly walked towards the front courtyard.

Yun Chu walked out of the old general's courtyard and saw Chu Yi, who hadn't left yet.

He probably came directly to the Yun family after leaving the palace. In his official attire, he exuded an imposing manner, and from head to toe, he was filled with a cold aura.

However, when he turned his head, Yun Chu was surprised to find that the icy coldness in his eyes slowly faded.

"Madam Xie."

Chu Yi called out.

Although he internally rejected these three words, he could only address her as such.

"Greetings, Your Highness." Yun Chu curtsied, "Does Your Highness have any business to attend to?"

Chu Yi had come to find the Minister of War, following the Yun family servants here. The next thing would be to return to the banquet to continue drinking.

He said, "No."

"I have something I would like to discuss with Your Highness." Yun Chu smiled, "Your Highness, please come this way."

She led Chu Yi to a pavilion in the Yun family. Chu Yi had one guard with him, and she had two maids, all standing at the edge of the pavilion.

Not far away was the main road of the residence, with many servants coming and going busily. Their conversation here was not inappropriate.

Chu Yi sat opposite her. As he breathed, he once again smelled that familiar fragrance and couldn't help but ask: "Madam Xie, what perfume are you using?"

As soon as he asked, he felt it was abrupt.

Asking a married woman about such a private matter was somewhat presumptuous.

He was grateful for his quick mind and immediately added, "Changsheng likes you. I think she would also like the perfume you use."

"I use jasmine fragrance made by my mother." Yun Chu said, "Next time, I'll have someone bring some to give to Changsheng."

Chu Yi slightly furrowed his brows, almost imperceptibly.

Jasmine fragrance?

There was a bit, but more of that familiar, unknown fragrance, very faint.

When he was close to her, he could smell it clearly.

He must have smelled this scent before.

When was it?

He couldn't remember.

"Your Highness." Yun Chu interrupted his thoughts, "I want to discuss a business venture with Your Highness. I wonder if Your Highness is interested."

Chu Yi wasn't particularly interested in discussing business.

But for some reason, he wanted to hear her talk.

He nodded: "Go on." Yun Chu spoke methodically: "I bought a manor in the outskirts of the capital and unexpectedly discovered a hot spring, which is slightly larger than the imperial hot spring. If I hand it over to the imperial family, I would be reluctant, but if I keep it for myself, there are many hidden dangers. So, I thought of asking Your Highness to share the risk and the profits. What do you think?"

Chu Yi took a sip of tea and said, "Why me?"

chapters.title: The Business Deal Was Sealed
chapters.content:
Yun Chu was also wondering why she had chosen Prince Pingxi.

In her past life, this hot spring resort had been taken by Concubine Hui, and all the profits went to the Second Prince, providing ample funds for his rebellion.

The only ones who could rival Concubine Hui and the Second Prince were the Crown Prince and Prince Pingxi. Although the Sixth and Seventh Princes would gradually rise in power in a few years, based on the current situation, she could only choose between the Crown Prince and Prince Pingxi.

It seemed she didn’t need to hesitate; she was more inclined to cooperate with Prince Pingxi.

Because Prince Pingxi was the father of Yu Ge’er and Changsheng, wasn’t he?

She lifted her gaze and replied, "Your Highness and my father are friends. I think Your Highness wouldn’t maliciously take this resort from me."

A hint of disappointment flickered in Chu Yi’s eyes.

So that was the reason; it was that simple.

"It’s your resort. Of course, I won’t take it." He spoke, "This deal, I accept."

Yun Chu was surprised.

She hadn’t expected it to go so smoothly.

She hadn’t even mentioned how to split the profits, yet he had already agreed.

"Your Highness can have fifty percent of the profits." Seeing that the man seemed about to refuse, she continued, "But it must be opened under Your Highness’s name."

Chu Yi frowned.

Even if it was operated under his name, fifty percent was too much, after all, he hadn’t contributed anything.

He spoke, "How about a 20-80 split? I take 20, you take 80."

Before Yun Chu could respond, he added, "If Madam Xie refuses, then there’s no need to discuss this deal further."

Yun Chu had no choice but to swallow the rest of her words.

A sudden silence fell between them. The summer wind carried warmth as it blew, and the ice blocks in the pavilion slowly melted.

The cicadas chirped tirelessly, loud yet somehow peaceful.

Yun Chu felt the atmosphere was a bit awkward. She stood up. "Your Highness, we should return to the banquet."

Chu Yi stood up as well, and the two walked out of the pavilion.

At that moment, a group of children came running over, chasing each other. The adults were drinking and talking, so the children, with nothing to do, started making trouble.

"Stop! All of you, stop!"

A few boys at the back held slingshots, aiming at the ones running ahead.

*Whoosh*, a small stone flew from the slingshot, heading straight for Yun Chu’s face.

Yun Chu quickly sidestepped to avoid it.

But another hand was faster, stretching out in front of her and catching the stone.

Chu Yi tightly gripped the stone; it was a thumb-sized, sharply edged pebble. If it had hit her face, it would have at least left a bruise, if not drawn blood.

"Who?" he coldly spat out a single word.

It was as if an invisible net had suddenly descended from above. The children, who had been chasing each other, all froze in their tracks.

The children all looked toward one person, Young Master Xuanwu, the heir of Marquis Xuanwu.

The young master stepped forward, his face calm. "It was me."

Even though the man before him was a prince, he hadn’t actually hurt anyone. Even a prince couldn’t do much to him for that.

"Do you know what would happen if this stone had hit someone?" Chu Yi asked, his voice unreadable.

But Yun Chu could sense that the man in front of her was already angry.

However, the young Marquis Xuanwu was too young to discern the emotions of others. Indifferently, he replied, "But it didn’t hit anyone, did it?"

"In that case—" Chu Yi took the slingshot from the young master’s hand, "why not try it?"

He placed the stone on the slingshot and aimed it at the young master’s face.

The young master’s face instantly paled.

This stone was one he had painstakingly found, sharp and jagged. If it hit someone, it would definitely hurt, and if it hit the face, it would surely swell.

He had specifically brought it to hit the heir of Marquis Xingguo, how dare that boy mock him for being short at the banquet earlier!

Chu Yi let out a cold laugh.

He pulled the slingshot back.

He did it very slowly, stretching it to its limit.

"Your Highness, stop!" Marquis Xuanwu, Qin Mingheng, quickly stepped forward, blocking the child. "Children fighting is normal. As adults, we should just watch. Don’t you agree, Your Highness?"

Chu Yi smiled.

If he had truly intended to act, the stone in his hand would have already left a bloody hole in the young master’s face.

He was just trying to scare him, to teach the young master a lesson.

If it weren’t for the fact that this stone had almost hit the woman beside him, he wouldn’t have bothered with such a trivial matter in the past.

"Marquis Xuanwu, I agree with your words. Children’s matters should not involve adults." Chu Yi threw the slingshot aside. "Since Marquis Xuanwu understands this principle, then why, at the last Xie family banquet, did your son get into a dispute with the second young master of the Xie family, and you stepped in to break the second young master’s leg?"

Qin Mingheng looked up in shock.

That incident had happened so long ago that even he had almost forgotten it.

As Prince Pingxi, busy with state affairs every day, how did he even know about such a trivial matter between two children from another family?

His gaze fell on Yun Chu’s face.

How were these two together?

"One rule for the magistrate, another for the common people. Marquis Xuanwu, you are no magistrate, and I am no commoner." Chu Yi’s voice was icy. "Your son causes trouble everywhere. If you don’t discipline him properly, Marquis Xuanwu, one day someone will use your own methods against him."

With that, he gave Yun Chu a glance and turned to leave.

Yun Chu’s face showed no extra expression. Keeping a distance from Chu Yi, the two of them, one in front and the other behind, walked out of the backyard.

Watching their figures disappear down the path, Qin Mingheng’s eyes turned extremely sinister.

When they reached the front courtyard, the banquet was almost over. Many court officials, burdened with urgent matters, had left early to attend to business. Once the high-ranking officials left, the lower-ranking ones naturally saw no point in staying, and the gathering slowly dispersed.

Sitting in the carriage on the way back to the Xie residence, Yun Chu kept thinking about what major events would happen next and how she could make her father believe her sooner. If they really had to wait for the imperial decree, going to Nanyue would take at least another two years...

But in her past life, she had been a woman of the inner quarters, secluded in the backyard. Unless something huge happened in the court, news wouldn’t reach her ears. Then there were natural disasters and man-made calamities, like the continuous heatwaves this summer, the floods in the south next year, and the unrest in the north... But these were all future events, and it would take time to verify them now.

Although she didn’t know about court affairs, every small event that would soon happen to the Yun family, if they unfolded exactly as she said, her grandfather and father should believe in that dream of hers.

"Madam."

Xie Jingyu, who was sitting beside her, suddenly spoke, interrupting Yun Chu’s thoughts.

She opened her eyes. "What is it?"

"Why didn’t you take An Ge’er to see your father." Xie Jingyu tightened her lips. "During the banquet, you said there was no rush. I thought that after the banquet, you would take the children to visit their maternal grandfather. But you... just because you know the children are He Concubine’s, you don’t want them to meet their maternal grandfather?"

"Whether An Ge’er and Ping Jie’er are He Concubine’s children or not doesn’t matter. What matters is that you, Xie Jingyu, deceived me for five years!" Yun Chu’s lips curled into a cold smile. "You deceived me, and you deceived the entire Yun family. My father has just returned to the capital from the western frontier, full of joy. If I took them to meet him now, wouldn’t that be deliberately making him uncomfortable?"

Xie Jingyu’s eyes filled with disbelief. "Uncomfortable? How can you say that? An Ge’er and Ping Jie’er have called you mother and shown you filial piety for four whole years. They gave you their true hearts, how can you say they make you uncomfortable?"

---

chapters.title: Xie Jingyu Falls Ill from Anger
chapters.content:
Yun Chu laughed.

"Filial piety? True hearts?" She sneered. "An Ge’er’s spot at the Imperial Academy was secured by the Yun family. Ping Jie’er’s position as a princess consort was earned by me. The face of your Xie family is maintained by my dowry... Everything you, Xie Jingyu, couldn’t do, I did for you. They *should* be filial to me! But the truth is, I worked hard to pave the way for them, and they, along with you, deceived me for four years. How can such filial piety and true hearts not make me uncomfortable?"

"You, you—"

Xie Jingyu felt a sharp pain in her chest.

Immediately after, her mind felt as if it had exploded into blossoms. Her vision went black, and she collapsed onto the carriage floor.

When she woke up again, she was on her own bed. Instinctively, she tried to push herself up, but found that her left hand wouldn’t obey her at all.

A wave of panic swept over her.

She looked up and saw Yun Chu sitting by her bedside.

For some reason, seeing her calm, expressionless face, an inexplicable fear arose in her heart.

"The physician said you drank too much, and the fire in your liver attacked your heart, causing a blockage in your blood flow. Your left hand is temporarily unusable." Yun Chu picked up a bowl of medicine and handed it over. "Rest at home for the next few days. I’ve already arranged for someone to request leave for you."

Xie Jingyu forced her left hand up, but even with all her strength, she couldn’t lift it an inch.

Yun Chu had a maid help her sit up and placed the medicine bowl in her hand. "The physician said not to get angry. Avoid extreme emotional fluctuations."

Staying emotionally calm might buy her some more time.

If she kept getting angered into fainting like today, her body wouldn’t be able to take it.

Xie Jingyu wanted to speak, but her throat hurt terribly, and she couldn’t make a sound. She could only watch helplessly as Yun Chu left.

Outside, Yun Chu lowered her voice: "No need to send medicine over anymore."

She wanted Xie Jingyu to slowly waste away from illness, not die suddenly from poisoning...

Tingshuang nodded in understanding.

As she reached the door, she saw the old madam hobbling over with her cane, followed by Lady Yuan, who grabbed her and asked, "How is Jingyu? What did the physician say?"

"He drank too much, which caused his illness. He just took his medicine and fell asleep." Yun Chu said. "Old Madam and Mother, don’t go in and disturb his rest."

"How could he suddenly fall ill? His body has always been strong; he’s never been sick before." The old madam was anxious. "If I had known, I wouldn’t have let him go to the Yun residence."

Lady Yuan spoke up, "General Yun has returned to the capital after five years. As his son-in-law, how could he not attend? It’s his own fault for drinking too much."

"The physician said it’s nothing serious." Yun Chu added, "I was thinking of finding a time to let the children formally meet their maternal grandfather."

The old madam had just heard from Xie Shian that Yun Chu hadn’t taken them to meet their grandfather. When she heard this, she had actually been quite displeased, but because Jingyu had suddenly fallen ill, she hadn’t pursued the matter.

Now that Yun Chu had brought it up herself, the old madam felt a little more at ease. "That’s only right. When do you think your father will be free?"

"My father said that he wants to meet every child registered under my name, one by one." Yun Chu lifted her gaze. "Including Wei Ge’er."

"This... that might not be a good idea." The old madam tightened her grip on her cane. "Wei Ge’er is... your father might not like him. Let’s forget about it."

"Since they are children registered under my name, they are my father’s grandchildren. My father also wants to find a good place for Wei Ge’er." Yun Chu smiled. "Wei Ge’er has been reflecting at the estate for so long; he should be more sensible now. I’ll arrange for someone to bring him back."

Lady Yuan immediately nodded. "Yes, yes. Wei Ge’er can’t just be left to waste away. It’s rare that Father-in-law is willing to help, so we should take him to see him."

The old madam felt an inexplicable sense of foreboding in her heart.

But when she tried to think carefully, she couldn’t pinpoint where this feeling came from. She could only conclude that she was overthinking.

Yun Chu returned to her courtyard.

She had someone bring pen, ink, paper, and an inkstone. She wrote down the minor events that would soon happen to the Yun family on paper. Since they weren’t major events, she sometimes mixed up the order.

But it didn’t matter, as long as the events happened soon, it would be fine. She mainly wanted her family to believe in that dream.

As for why she didn’t just say she was reborn; it was simply too absurd. It had taken her several days to accept the fact herself.

As she wrote, Tingshuang entered to report, "Madam, the servant sent to investigate Marquis Xuanwu has returned."

Yun Chu paused her pen and folded the paper away. "Let him come in."

The servant entered the hall with a bow, respectfully saying, "This servant greets Madam. Madam ordered this servant to investigate Marquis Xuanwu, and this servant did find something."

Yun Chu gestured for him to continue.

Ever since she found out that the man from her wedding night was Marquis Xuanwu, she had arranged for people to keep an eye on that despicable man.

He had taken her innocence and thought he could get away with it? He was dreaming!

"This servant followed Marquis Xuanwu for more than ten days and finally discovered that he actually has another courtyard in the west city’s Tofu Alley. It’s a modest two-section courtyard. This servant gave many gifts to the neighbors, and only then did I learn that there are two women living there, both of whom call Marquis Xuanwu ‘husband’!" The servant lowered his voice. "This servant suspects that these two women don’t know Marquis Xuanwu’s real identity. They probably live there as his unofficial wives. I heard that one of them is even pregnant, about five or six months along."

Yun Chu let out a cold laugh.

The outside world said that Marquis Xuanwu deeply loved his wife, that his inner courtyard was clean and free of concubines, and that every woman in the capital envied the Marchioness of Xuanwu.

The more a man proclaimed his love for his wife, the more disgusting he was, no better than Xie Jingyu.

It was no wonder Marquis Xuanwu behaved this way. The Luo family not only held a high official position but was also very wealthy. Relying on the Luo family’s money, he could maintain the facade of his declining marquisate.

If one were to ask what Marquis Xuanwu cared about most, first would naturally be the most precious thing to the Qin family, the hereditary title that could be passed down.

Second would probably be children.

He had risked offending Prince Pingxi to protect his own child. In this regard, he was a bit better than Xie Jingyu.

It was just unclear whether he cared more about his legitimate son or his illegitimate children...

Yun Chu tapped her fingers on the table. "Find an opportunity. When Marquis Xuanwu goes to that small courtyard, lead Lady Luo there."

As she spoke, she tossed a money pouch over.

The servant’s face lit up. "Madam, rest assured. This servant will handle it."

After the servant left, Yun Chu said, "He seems clever and reliable. Give him a raise in his monthly allowance."

Tingshuang noted this down.

"Oh, right." Yun Chu’s face showed a slight smile. "This morning at the Yun residence, Yu Ke’s parents came to me. They wanted to propose a marriage. Tingshuang, what do you think?"

Tingshuang had been pondering how much to increase the servant’s stipend. Hearing this sudden question, her fair face instantly turned red.

She thought of the time when Madam had stayed at the Yun residence. She had stayed by Madam’s side to serve her, and that man had come to see her every day, bringing either rouge or hairpins.

She could afford rouge and hairpins herself, but what had truly moved her was the day by the lake when he had draped his cloak over her shoulders...

But if she married, she wouldn’t be able to stay by Madam’s side to serve her. If she had to choose one, she would rather not marry.

"If you marry Yu Ke, you can manage the hot spring resort for me." Yun Chu, of course, noticed her inner conflict. "Prince Pingxi and I will co-manage it, and I need a trustworthy person to live at the resort. Tingshuang, you are the most suitable candidate."

Tingshuang’s eyes lit up instantly.

Even if she got married and couldn’t stay by Madam’s side, as a married woman, she could manage external affairs and would be able to help Madam even more.

So, she could have both the fish and the bear’s paw.

Blushing slightly, she nodded.

chapters.title: The Dream is Real
chapters.content:
The next morning, Yun Chu went to the Yun residence and settled Yu Shuo's marriage.

Yu Ke's mother was a trusted maid by Lady Lin's side, and Yu Ke's father was the chief steward of the outer courtyard of the Yun residence. Both were born servants of the Yun family, having served the family all their lives. Thus, they had requested a favor to have Yu Ke's servant status removed early, allowing him to train in the military camp outside the city.

"This marriage can be set for half a month later; it's an auspicious day," Mama Yu said with a smile. "Our Yu family has a small courtyard outside the city, big enough for the two of them to live in. Even when they have children, there will be enough space. In the future, it will be convenient for Yu Ke to go to the military camp and for Tingshuang to serve the eldest miss."

For ordinary people, marriage arrangements were not as complicated as those of large families. As long as both parties agreed, they could get married at any time.

After setting the date, the heavy weight in Yun Chu's heart silently lifted.

Then, she went to Yun Silin's study. Two guards stood at the door, one was her father's deputy general, and the other was a guard she recognized who often followed Prince Pingxi.

"Eldest Miss, the general and Prince Pingxi are in a meeting. Please wait in the side hall."

Yun Chu nodded and entered the side hall to sit and drink tea.

She had just sat down when the study door opened. Yun Silin saw Chu Yi out. "Your Highness's concerns are indeed possible. Who knows when this heat will end? So many people have died from it. Fortunately, there are occasional downpours; otherwise, the crops would have dried up too. Who knows how many riots there will be."

Chu Yi spoke, "Once the emperor's decree comes, I will come discuss with the general again."

For months, the extreme heat had killed countless people. Many commoners outside the city gathered and caused disturbances. Although not as deadly as bandits, they still caused panic.

The emperor would surely order him to suppress the riots. Since those were ordinary civilians, he couldn't use the same approach as with bandits. Hence, he came to the pillar of the nation, the grand general, for advice.

As he was about to leave, he looked up and saw a bright figure sitting in the side hall.

Without any effort, he could capture her presence.

"Oh, right, I also have something to ask of you," Yun Silin patted his head. "My daughter has been learning martial arts recently. I've been wanting to find a suitable weapon for her. You're a prince with many connections; can I trouble you with this?"

Chu Yi asked, "May I ask what kind of weapon Miss Yun prefers?"

The title "Miss Yun" rolled off his tongue much more naturally than "Madam Xie."

Yun Silin was a straightforward man and didn't find the address odd at all. He waved toward Yun Chu, "Chu'er, come here!"

Yun Chu put down her teacup and walked out of the side hall, down the steps, and over. "Greetings, Your Highness."

Yun Silin said casually, "Chu'er, I've asked His Highness to find a weapon for you. Whatever you like, just tell His Highness."

Yun Chu didn't know what to say.

She had just bothered Prince Pingxi over business matters, and now her father was asking the prince to handle something as trivial as finding a weapon...

"It's still troublesome to bother Your Highness," she refused. "I'm just a beginner; any good weapon would be wasted on me."

Chu Yi said, "Five years ago, I followed General Yun to the western frontier, and it was General Yun who found the sky-piercing halberd for me. Now, I am finding a weapon for General Yun's daughter, which can be considered repaying this kindness."

Afraid that Yun Chu would refuse again, he cupped his hands in a salute, bid farewell, and left.

"Father, how can you ask His Highness to do such a thing?" Yun Chu held her forehead. "Don't you know your daughter's capabilities? What use would such a fine weapon be to me?"

Yun Silin laughed heartily, "It's precisely because your skills are poor that you need a powerful weapon to protect yourself. Prince Pingxi and I have a life-and-death friendship. Don't feel burdened."

Since he put it that way, Yun Chu let the matter drop.

She followed Yun Silin into the study and took a piece of paper from her sleeve, handing it over.

Yun Silin unfolded the paper and took a look. His expression changed instantly. "Chu'er, are these all things that will happen in your dreams?"

Yun Chu nodded.

Yun Silin's face was filled with shock.

The paper was filled with matters concerning the Yun family. Apart from the specific times being a bit vague, the causes, processes, and outcomes of each event were extremely clear.

Generally speaking, people's dreams were vague. Most people forgot their dreams upon waking, and even if they remembered, they wouldn't recall them so clearly.

Originally, he didn't believe his daughter's dreams, but the things on this paper were too real.

At this moment, a servant's voice came from outside the study. "General, the clan elders have arrived and say they have important matters to discuss."

Yun Silin folded the paper. "Let's go, Chu'er. Let's go listen to what it is."

In his mind, his daughter was still a member of the Yun family. Since the clan elders had come, they naturally had to meet those elders.

Yun Chu followed him to the main hall. Before she even entered, she heard crying.

A woman from a collateral branch was holding Lady Lin's hand, crying, "Qin'er has suffered too much. She's been married for half a year and is beaten almost every day. Her leg was even broken... If she stays in the Fang family, she might lose her life..."

Yun Chu and Yun Silin exchanged a glance.

The first thing written on her paper was that Yun Qin, a woman from a collateral branch of the Yun family, would seek a divorce.

Yun Silin's heart was shaken to the core.

The Yun family had too many collateral branches. It was just the right person, at just the right time, seeking a divorce.

Everything matched perfectly.

This meant that Chu'er's dreams were real!

Everything in the dreams would come true!

"Madam, I beg you to intervene and help Qin'er divorce, so she can leave the Fang family!" the woman said.

As soon as these words were spoken, the group of clan elders sitting to the side immediately objected.

"The Yun family has been in the capital for a hundred or two years and has never had a divorce. If one woman divorces, it will affect the marriage prospects of all Yun family women."

"Now that the general has returned to the capital and the emperor personally welcomed him, which prince in the palace doesn't give the general some face? The Fang family should also restrain themselves."

"Otherwise, how about this: a few of us elders and Madam will go to the Fang family together to pressure them. I believe they won't dare to do such things again."

"I also think this is the best approach."

"Yes, this is the way."

The elders unanimously agreed to this plan.

Among these elders, there was only one man; the rest were old women, as most Yun family men had died early.

Yun Silin strode in, and the hall immediately fell silent.

Lady Lin spoke, "General, you must have heard just now. The Fang family dares to abuse our Yun family's married daughter. I plan to go to the Fang family with the elders now. What do you think?"

Yun Silin humphed.

Chu'er had written clearly on the paper that after the Yun family pressured the Fang family, they did indeed quiet down for a while.

But after he left the capital, the Fang family became bold again and even blinded Yun Qin in one eye. However, for various reasons, she still couldn't divorce. In the end, he found an excuse to send that Fang family man to the western frontier, and he never returned to the capital for the rest of his life.

Breaking a leg wasn't enough; they had to lose an eye too. This was unreasonable.

---

chapters.title: A Yun Family Woman Divorces
chapters.content:
Yun Chu's expression darkened.

This woman from a collateral branch of the Yun family was someone she had never met. She had only heard about this distant cousin named Yun Qin from her mother.

Thus, she hadn't thought of Yun Qin at all initially.

Yun Qin had been beaten by her husband's family to the point of having a broken leg and a blinded eye. Even so, under the elders' intervention, she still couldn't successfully divorce.

It was her father who transferred Yun Qin's husband to the western frontier, preventing the tragedy of her being abused to death.

She knew that divorce was extremely difficult, especially for a prestigious family like the Yun family. For the sake of the family's reputation, divorce was even more difficult.

"If I go to the frontier to guard the border, the Fang family will surely return to their old ways," Yun Silin said coldly. "Every woman of the Yun family, whether legitimate or illegitimate, whether from the main line or a collateral branch, carries the blood of the Yun family. No one is allowed to suffer such a great injustice!"

Lady Lin asked, "Then what do you think should be done?"

"As Qin'er's mother said, divorce," Yun Silin declared. "If the Fang family doesn't agree, then list a dozen charges against them. If they dare not release her, submit the charges to the Ministry of Justice!"

In Chu'er's dream, he had sent that Fang family man away, but the Fang family still had many people. Although Qin'er would no longer be beaten by her husband, she would likely still suffer from her mother-in-law's cold looks, her brother-in-law's bullying, and her sisters-in-law's schemes. It would be better to just divorce directly...

As soon as he said this, the hall erupted.

"General, this must not be done! Our Yun family still has so many unmarried women. If one woman divorces, it will be difficult for all unmarried women to find marriage partners in the future."

"The Yun family is at least a first-rank family. With the general personally pressuring them, I think the Fang family won't dare to do excessive things again!"

"There are clearly better ways; why choose the path of divorce?"

"Please reconsider, General!"

"..."

Yun Silin raised his hand to silence everyone.

He wasn't a meticulous person and couldn't think of all the consequences. If this had happened before, with so many people advising him, he would have followed the elders' suggestions.

"If the Yun family's divorce deters people from seeking marriage, it only shows that those people have impure intentions!" He looked at everyone in the hall.
