"If a person is upright, responsible, and doesn't abuse his wife, there's no need to worry about the Yun family divorcing them in the future... Having one more divorced woman in the Yun family is actually a way to filter out scum for the unmarried women. Why not do it?"

Everyone was shocked.

This was the first time they had heard such a viewpoint.

It was well known that divorce was a bad thing. No large family had ever heard of a daughter divorcing.

But in the master's mouth, divorce had become a fortunate thing?

This was absurd!

Nonsense!

A few elders exchanged glances and were about to refute.

"Qin'er will lose her life if she doesn't divorce!" Yun Silin said, emphasizing each word. "Elders, I ask you one thing: is the life of a Yun family woman more important, or is the face of the Yun family more important?"

This question stumped the elders.

In their view, the century-old reputation of the Yun family was naturally more important.

But if they said this out loud, who knew how many married women would be disheartened? Those married Yun family women might also distance themselves from the Yun family.

Moreover, most of them were women, with daughters, granddaughters, and great-granddaughters. If such a thing happened to their direct descendants, what would they choose?

Human hearts were made of flesh and blood; they could all empathize.

The hall fell silent.

Yun Silin spoke, "Since no one has any objections, this matter is settled. Yun Ze, you will handle this personally."

Qin'er's mother was overjoyed and wept, "Thank you, General! Thank you, General..."

When she had proposed the divorce, she knew the elders wouldn't agree. She had only wanted to use this excessive demand to force the elders to help find a solution.

She hadn't expected the general to directly agree to this outrageous request.

Yun Silin waved his hand, "One stroke cannot write the character 'Yun.' If I can't even protect my own people, how can I be worthy of being the head of the Yun family?"

With things as they were, the elders had no choice but to accept the situation.

The turbid air in Yun Chu's chest slowly dissipated.

Whether she could divorce or not, she truly didn't care. Her life was already set; it would be the same no matter where she was.

She was happy that another person in the Yun family had escaped the tragedy of the previous life.

Her father should believe her now. With her father at the helm, her grandfather and eldest brother strategizing, the Yun family would surely be able to reverse the fate of being executed.

After dinner, Yun Chu returned to the Xie family.

She had been going to the Yun family often lately, and the Xie family had long since grown used to it.

"Madam, the master left for a social engagement an hour ago," Tingfeng reported. "Madam Xie tried to persuade him but failed."

Yun Chu smiled, unconcerned.

Of course, she couldn't persuade him. Xie Jingyu had already been demoted, and she had even requested seven days of leave for him. A man who valued his career so much would naturally be anxious.

When someone invited him, how could he still consider his illness? Most social engagements involved drinking, and alcohol was a great catalyst for the poison.

Her smile slowly faded.

If Xie Jingyu died, she would be a widow of the Xie family. Would she really have to stay in the Xie family for the rest of her life?

Although she didn't care where she was, the Xie family was truly too disgusting.

Today's events at the Yun family had given her some inspiration.

"Madam, the second young master has returned."

Yun Chu's lips parted. "Let's go welcome him."

A carriage stopped at the Xie residence's gate. Xie Shiwei, supported by a servant's arm, got out of the carriage. His right leg was completely useless; he needed the servant's support to climb the steps.

He looked up and saw only Yun Chu standing at the door to welcome him.

He lowered his head and bowed, "Mother."

"Are you tired from the journey?" Yun Chu asked with a smile. "Your father went out for a social engagement. Your elder brother is still at school. The old madame and Madam Xie are taking a nap. They will come see you later... Are you hungry? I've had them prepare the dishes you like. Come, let's go back to your courtyard to wash your hands and eat."

Her gentle smile gave Xie Shiwei a sense of illusion, as if he were still the second young master of the Xie family.

But his useless right leg reminded him that everything was different now.

He had thought his leg was crippled and could never be healed... It was only a few days ago that he learned the truth: his elder brother had urged their father not to treat his injury. His own elder brother, with whom he shared the same mother, had turned him into a cripple! All because he had offended the Marquis of Xuanwu, and the Xie family had abandoned him!

He should be grateful, shouldn't he? At least he had kept his life!

But his mother, who had always doted on him, had been poisoned by his elder brother and elder sister!

He was crippled!

His mother was dead!

Why had his life been ruined like this?

Why had his mother died so unjustly?

Why could his elder brother enter the Imperial College?

Why could his elder sister marry into the royal family?

"Shi Wei, what's wrong?" Yun Chu's gentle voice brought Xie Shiwei back to his senses.

He suppressed his hatred and said, "Thank you, Mother."

He had been away from the Xie family for so long. Upon his return, only his mother had come to welcome him. He had vaguely heard the coachman say that the Xie family hadn't wanted to take him back. It was his mother who had insisted on letting him visit his maternal grandfather, which was why he had the chance to return to the Xie family.

His mother, who had no blood relation to him, cared for him so much.

Those so-called family members were nothing but cold-blooded monsters!

chapters.title: Xie Shiwei Returns to the Manor
chapters.content:
Xie Shiwei returned to the manor, and Yun Chu had specially arranged a family banquet.

The banquet was set in the old madam’s courtyard, and people from all the other courtyards came, making it quite lively.

The old madam sat in the seat of honor and watched as a young servant helped Xie Shiwei walk into the courtyard.

Though she disliked this grandson, he was still a descendant of the Xie family. Moreover, the Yun family had said they would find a position for Wei’ge, so perhaps he would have some good fortune in the future.

"Wei’ge, come, let your great-grandmother take a look at you."

The old madam pulled Wei’ge over, touched his face, and put on a kind expression.

"You’ve lost a lot of weight. Our Wei’ge must have suffered on the farm."

Xie Shiwei remained silent.

Soon, Xie Jingyu and Xie Shian arrived together.

Xie Shiwei suddenly lifted his head and looked over.

He saw Xie Shian dressed in fine brocade robes, his hair tied with a jade crown, looking every bit the elegant young master, full of vigor and spirit.

Meanwhile, he himself was dressed in coarse cloth, like a servant of the Xie household, and with his broken leg, his life was ruined.

He couldn’t control the rage surging in his chest. He strode forward and grabbed Xie Shian by the neck.

"Cough, cough, cough!" Xie Shian, completely caught off guard, was choked and couldn’t breathe. "Xie... Xie Shiwei, have you gone mad? What are you doing!"

Xie Jingyu raised his right hand and slapped Xie Shiwei hard across the face. "Ungrateful wretch! You just returned, and now you’re causing trouble. Do you want to anger me to death!"

Xie Shiwei was knocked onto the table, and the dishes that had just been served were all overturned.

Several concubines screamed in shock.

"Wei’ge, what’s gotten into you?" Yuan Shi hurried over to restrain Xie Shiwei. "This banquet was arranged especially for you. Why are you making such a scene?"

"Xie Shian, I have a question for you!" Xie Shiwei’s eyes burned with fury as he stared at the elder brother he had once admired the most. "Back when my leg was injured, wasn’t it you who stopped the family from calling a doctor for me? My leg could have been healed, but because of you, I became a cripple for life. Isn’t that true?!"

Xie Shian’s expression remained calm. "Your leg was beyond healing to begin with. It had nothing to do with anyone."

"Then what about Concubine He? How did she die!" Xie Shiwei roared. "Didn’t you force her to her death!"

At these words, the expressions of everyone in the courtyard changed.

The death of Concubine He was known only to a few. Everyone else believed she had committed suicide after being accused of practicing witchcraft.

Now, hearing Xie Shiwei say that Xie Shian had forced Concubine He to her death, the other concubines couldn’t believe the truth was so shocking...

"Silence!" the old madam barked angrily. "We brought you back to the Xie family to secure your future, but you’re spouting nonsense and causing trouble. Someone, take the second young master away!"

Xie Shiwei struggled with all his might. The servants were kicked and punched, and he even bit a few of them.

The two tables of food in the courtyard were overturned by him, and the chaos grew out of control.

Xie Jingyu was so enraged that his chest burned. The doctor had warned him not to get angry, but in such a situation, it was impossible to control his temper.

He saw a wooden stick on the ground, picked it up, and struck Xie Shiwei on the back.

Xie Shiwei let out a miserable howl.

"Enough, stop this." Yun Chu walked over, took the stick from Xie Jingyu’s hand, and threw it to the ground. Then she took Xie Shiwei’s arm. "Wei’ge, for my sake, stop making a scene. I’ll have someone take you back to your courtyard."

Xie Shiwei could lash out at anyone, but he couldn’t bring himself to be angry with Yun Chu. After all, it was she who had brought him back here.

He said nothing more and followed Yun Chu back to his own courtyard.

"Wei’ge, don’t blame your father for hitting you. No matter how angry you are, you shouldn’t have grabbed your elder brother by the neck," Yun Chu said, sitting on the edge of the table. "Your elder brother has to attend school every day, and soon he’ll be going to the Imperial Academy. If people see bruises on his neck, won’t they gossip about the Xie family behind our backs?"

Xie Shiwei looked up. "Mother, tell me the truth. Did Elder Brother have something to do with Concubine He’s death?"

"Wei’ge, who told you these things? Don’t believe them. Concubine He did something terrible and couldn’t face the consequences, so she drank poison and died," Yun Chu’s expression changed drastically. "Your elder brother is the child your father is most proud of. All of your father’s efforts and the Xie family’s resources are focused on him. If you continue to oppose your elder brother, your father will certainly not spare you. I can protect you for a while, but can I protect you forever?"

Xie Shiwei clenched his fists tightly.

He had merely offended the heir of the Marquis of Xuanwu, and the Xie family had abandoned him.

Yet Xie Shian, who had killed his own mother with his own hands, still received everything the Xie family had to offer!

Why was it so unfair!

"It’s getting late. You should rest well. I’ll leave now."

Yun Chu patted his shoulder and turned to leave the courtyard.

Just as she reached the courtyard gate, she saw Xie Shian standing there. "An’ge?"

"Mother, Wei’ge has some misunderstandings about me. I must explain things clearly." Xie Shian spoke. "I’ll go in first."

As soon as he reached the door, a lamp was thrown at his feet. "Get out!"

"Xie Shiwei, it’s me, your elder brother." Xie Shian sighed, picked up the lamp, and said, "Mother is gone. In this world, only we brothers are the closest. Give me a chance to explain."

"Fine, explain it to me then!" Xie Shiwei limped out of the room. "Explain why you didn’t allow the family to call a doctor for my leg! Explain why you forced Mother to drink poison! Speak! Explain it!"

"Your leg was beyond healing to begin with. This matter has nothing to do with me." Xie Shian said slowly. "As for Mother’s matter... it’s complicated. It can’t be explained clearly in just a moment... Wei’ge, rest assured. Even though your leg can’t be healed, once I pass the imperial examinations and enter officialdom, I will give you wealth and honor, and ensure you live a life without worries!"

Xie Shiwei stared at him coldly. "Really?"

Xie Shian nodded. "Of course. But on the condition that, before I pass the examinations, you stay quietly on the farm. I’ll personally take you back to the farm tomorrow. Alright?"

He knew his younger brother all too well, impulsive, hot-tempered, and reckless.

Now that he knew such a huge secret about the Xie family, how could he feel at ease with Grandfather taking Wei’ge away from the Xie household?

Wei’ge had to stay in the Xie family, confined to the farm for life!

Xie Shiwei’s expression suddenly darkened. "What do you mean by ‘stay quietly on the farm’? Are you afraid that if I stay in the Xie household, I’ll take away what belongs to you? Xie Shian, you’re such a hypocrite! For your own future, you killed Mother. Now that I know your secret, are you planning to get rid of me too?"

He grabbed the teacup from the table and smashed it against Xie Shian’s head. Blood immediately gushed out.

The young servants in the courtyard were so frightened that they screamed and rushed over to restrain Xie Shiwei.

"Quick, quick! Go call the master! Call the old madam!"

The two young masters were fighting, and as servants, they couldn’t handle this. They had to call someone with authority to settle the matter.

The old madam had already been considering coming to talk to Xie Shiwei. Mainly, this troublesome boy knew about the suspicious circumstances of Concubine He’s death. Such a scandal must never be revealed. She had come to warn Xie Shiwei.

Halfway there, the servant who came to report said that the second young master had smashed the eldest young master’s head open!

---

chapters.title: The Old Madam Passes Away
chapters.content:
The old madam of the Xie family stumbled, nearly falling to the ground.

She clutched her chest, leaning on her cane, and quickly made her way to Xie Shiwei’s courtyard.

There, she saw her most favored great-grandson, Xie Shian, crouched on the ground, his hand covering his forehead. Blood seeped through his fingers, dripping onto the ground one drop at a time.

The sight of that bright red blood made the old madam’s head spin, and she nearly fainted.

"Wretched creature! How did the Xie family produce such a wretched thing!"

The old madam forced herself to steady her breath and rushed forward. Without hesitation, she swung her cane at Xie Shiwei’s head.

Xie Shiwei, already eight years old and quite tall for his age, reached out and grabbed the cane from the old madam’s hand, then forcefully wrenched it away and smashed it to the ground.

The old madam was furious. This wretched boy dared to fight back!

She stepped forward and grabbed Xie Shiwei by the ear. "Kneel! Kneel down for me! Today, I must make you see reason!"

"I won’t kneel! I refuse to kneel!" Xie Shiwei roared. "The one who should kneel is him! He killed his own birth mother! He should kneel and atone for his sins! What did I do wrong? I only made the Marquis of Xuanwu’s heir’s hand bleed a little. Why should I suffer like this..."

"Bastard!"

The old madam trembled all over and raised her hand to slap him.

But Xie Shiwei dodged, then pushed her hard and bolted.

The old madam’s cane had been taken, and Mama Zhou, who had been at her side, had gone to check on Xie Shian. When she was pushed by Xie Shiwei, she lost her balance. With no one to support her, she fell backward.

*Bang!*

A loud thud echoed.

Xie Shian suddenly looked up and saw the back of the old madam’s head strike the ground. The tile beneath her was instantly stained red.

Xie Shiwei was so shocked that he forgot to run.

Xie Jingyu had just entered the courtyard when he saw this scene.

He immediately grabbed Xie Shiwei and pinned him down. "Tie this unfilial son up and throw him in the firewood shed!"

The stunned servants came to their senses and quickly restrained Xie Shiwei, gagging him and dragging him toward the firewood shed.

Mama Zhou couldn’t worry about Xie Shian anymore. She crawled over to the old madam and saw her lying there with wide-open eyes, her face ashen.

Trembling, Mama Zhou placed her hand near the old madam’s nose. She recoiled in horror. "N-no... it’s not good. The old madam... she’s not breathing..."

Hearing this, Xie Jingyu’s left leg gave out, and he collapsed to the ground.

He tried to stand up but found that, like his left hand, his left leg had no strength at all.

A wave of immense panic swept over him. Using his right hand to support himself, he struggled to his feet, dragging his left leg as he made his way to the old madam’s side. His leg gave out again, and he knelt down.

He reached out to check for breath but felt nothing. The old madam’s wide-open eyes reminded him of countless dreams in which He Shi’s eyes had been bloodshot and hollow.

His hand moved upward, covering the old madam’s eyes.

His entire body trembled, and tears fell uncontrollably, one by one. Soon, he began to sob aloud.

"Father, now is not the time to cry," Xie Shian said, pressing a hand to his forehead and lowering his voice. "Everyone in the courtyard saw Wei’ge push the old madam. They will all think it was Wei’ge who killed her. If this gets out, the Xie family... the Xie family will be ruined..."

Wei’ge would be arrested and interrogated.

The Censorate would impeach Father for failing to educate his son properly.

The Xie family’s descendants would be labeled as unfilial, and he would be implicated as well. Everyone would think he was unfilial too...

Xie Jingyu looked up at Xie Shian.

At a time like this, his eldest son was not grieving the old madam’s death but calculating the gains and losses for himself.

For the first time, he realized that this son was truly selfish and self-serving to the extreme.

But he had to admit, An’ge was right.

If this matter spread, the Xie family would be doomed.

He turned his head and saw four or five young servants and three or four maids in the courtyard. At the courtyard gate, there were also two or three matrons.

With so many witnesses, it would be impossible to keep them silent.

"Father, Great-Grandmother is already dead," Xie Shian said in a low, hoarse voice. "Even if we call a doctor, it’s useless. If Great-Grandmother knew that her death would bring disaster upon the Xie family, she would not rest in peace either. Father, some things must be cut off decisively when the time comes."

Xie Jingyu’s mind was in a whirl.

He had always been a filial man. Otherwise, he wouldn’t have exchanged his newlywed wife for the divine medicine that could save a life.

He hadn’t even accepted the news of the old madam’s death, yet he had to deal with this mess. His head ached so much it felt like it might explode.

"An... An’ge, do as you see fit."

He handed over the decision-making power to Xie Shian.

Xie Shian’s head also hurt, but it was only an external injury. His mind was clear.

He spoke in a deep voice, "Have all the people who saw the old madam die enter this courtyard. Then set it on fire, and burn everything, including the old madam’s body..."

Only the dead could keep secrets.

To the outside world, they would say that there was a fire in the Xie household. The old madam, being elderly, couldn’t escape and was burned to death along with the servants.

Xie Jingyu’s eyes widened in disbelief. He looked at Xie Shian and saw the coldness and resolve on his son’s face.

Then he looked at the old madam. Her face, lined with wrinkles, had turned ashen gray.

When he was young, his father studied while his mother kept him company. It was his grandmother who had raised him. His feelings for her could not be expressed in just a few words.

He had once sworn that he would let his grandmother live a long and prosperous life, that he would let her enjoy her old age in comfort, that he would give her a grand funeral...

But now—

His grandmother had died with her eyes wide open.

Her body was to be burned.

She wouldn’t even have peace in death!

...But he had no choice.

Xie Jingyu closed his eyes and was about to speak.

Then he heard hurried footsteps at the courtyard gate.

Immediately afterward, Yun Chu’s anxious voice rang out. "How could this have happened? Old Madam, what’s wrong with Old Madam! Quick, quick, call for a doctor!"

Xie Jingyu’s heart sank. Why had Yun Chu come?

Xie Shian took a deep breath. "Mother, Great-Grandmother has already passed away. Calling a doctor won’t help."

"What? The old madam is dead..." Yun Chu staggered, her voice filled with grief. "No, I don’t believe she’s just gone like this! What are you all standing around for? You, go call a physician immediately! You, go to Shande Hall and buy some ginseng to revive the old madam! And you, quickly find out where the divine doctor is..."

Several young servants in the courtyard were dispatched by Yun Chu.

She continued giving orders. "Mama Zhou, and the rest of you, quickly carry the old madam to Ansou Hall!"

The remaining servants gathered around, and with many hands, they lifted the old madam and hurried out of Xie Shiwei’s courtyard toward Ansou Hall.

Along the way, many servants who had heard the commotion came to see what was happening. The old madam, covered in blood, was carried out of the courtyard. Nearly two-thirds of the Xie household had witnessed the scene.

Xie Jingyu’s heart pounded so hard it felt like it might burst out of his chest.

He looked at Xie Shian, at this son who was always so clever, but in Xie Shian’s eyes, he saw only confusion.

Seven or eight servants could be burned, but the entire Xie household had so many people. They couldn’t burn them all... The news of the old madam’s death couldn’t be hidden anymore!

chapters.title: A Year of Mourning
chapters.content:
The Xie family had summoned a physician.

The physician carried his medicine case and hurried into Anshou Hall. With just a glance at the old lady, he knew she was beyond saving. Still, he checked her pulse before sighing and shaking his head.

Yun Chu lowered her eyelids.

She had intended to use Xie Shiwei to strike at Xie Shian, but in the end, it was the old lady who had lost her life.

In her previous life, the Xie family had reached the pinnacle of power. The old lady had lived a long, prosperous life, and when she passed, the entire capital had come to mourn her, a grand and glorious funeral.

But in this life, before the Xie family’s rise had even begun, the old lady was already buried.

"Old Lady!" Yuan Shi stumbled in, throwing herself onto the old lady’s body, and began wailing loudly.

The concubines also arrived with their children, kneeling before the old lady’s bed. The maids and servants followed suit, and the sound of weeping filled the air.

Yun Chu forced a look of grief, but she found that not a single tear would fall.

What had the old lady ever done for her? It seemed like nothing. But when she thought carefully, the old lady’s shadow loomed over everything.

A woman who had spent her life upholding the Xie family’s honor, who had lived and died for the family’s glory; now she was dead by the hand of her own great-grandson. Who knew what her final thoughts had been…

Yun Chu turned and walked out of Anshou Hall.

She stood in the courtyard and calmly ordered several stewardesses, "Handle the old lady’s funeral arrangements. Be quick about it."

The stewardesses wiped their tears and hurried off to see to it.

Yun Chu looked at Xie Jingyu, who was sitting on the steps of the courtyard, silently crying. She spoke, "Stop crying for now. I just asked around, it seems the old lady died because Shiwei pushed her. How do you plan to handle this?"

Xie Jingyu looked up at Yun Chu. The feeling of having to look up at her filled him with discomfort. He wanted to stand, but his left leg wouldn’t support him.

He could only remain seated on the steps, his voice low and hoarse. "That cursed child is a menace while alive. Just take a rope and strangle him!"

"Raising a child without discipline is the father’s fault," Yun Chu said. "Shiwei turned out this way, and you, as his father, can’t escape blame. Now that the old lady has passed, as the only grandson in the capital, you are expected to observe a year of mourning. During this time, you won’t need to attend court, so stay home and properly educate Shiwei. He’s only eight, still young. If you, as his father, guide him well, you can still set him on the right path."

Xie Jingyu’s heart sank.

He had completely forgotten about the mourning period!

His career had already been stagnant lately. If he took a year off for mourning, by the time he returned to court, there would be no place left for him!

The old lady had always been in good health; why did she have to die now?

He had no time for grief. All he wanted was to drag Xie Shiwei here, whip him mercilessly, and then strangle him!

Xie Pin, kneeling nearby, wiped her tears.

Fortunately, she was only a great-granddaughter and didn’t need to observe mourning. But even if she did, it wouldn’t matter, her marriage to Prince Anning was in a month, which fell within the period where mourning didn’t prohibit weddings…

Xie Zhongcheng lived at the estate and only returned to the Xie residence the next morning.

Before he even reached the gate, he heard many neighbors gathered outside, discussing the Xie family.

"How could Old Lady Xie, who was always so healthy, just drop dead like that?"

"Don’t you know? Early this morning, I heard the Xie family’s servant hanging white lanterns say that it was Young Master Shiwei who killed the old lady!"

"My goodness, isn’t Xie Shiwei the one who broke the Marquis of Xuanwu’s heir’s fingers? He actually killed his own great-grandmother?"

"What kind of family raises a child like this? Causing trouble is one thing, but killing someone at just eight years old; what will he be like when he grows up?"

"Wasn’t the Xie family able to marry the general’s legitimate daughter only by hiding the fact that they had an illegitimate child before marriage? It’s no surprise that a family with such crooked intentions would raise a murderous monster!"

"The general’s daughter was tricked into marriage, and then it was discovered she couldn’t have children. It’s hard not to suspect that the Xie family had something to do with it, just to make her willing to raise another woman’s child!"

"Like father, like son!"

"Damn it, the Xie family is disgusting!"

Among the speakers was an old woman who had just returned from the market. Unable to contain herself, she took some vegetable leaves and eggs from her basket and hurled them at the Xie family’s plaque.

*Thwack, thwack, thwack*, the Xie family’s entrance was soon littered with debris.

"All of you, stop!" Xie Zhongcheng stepped out of his carriage and roared, "Someone, drive these unrelated people away!"

The onlookers each spat at the Xie family’s gate before dispersing in twos and threes.

Xie Zhongcheng was fuming. He had only known that his mother had passed, but he had no idea she had died at Xie Shiwei’s hands.

He stormed into the courtyard. White banners and lanterns hung everywhere. Everyone was dressed in white mourning clothes. The main hall had already been turned into a funeral hall, with a coffin placed in the center. Most of the Xie family members were kneeling inside, weeping and burning paper money.

He suppressed his anger and entered, offering incense to the old lady before kneeling to burn paper money. Only then did he stand up. "Where is that cursed child?"

Yuan Shi lifted her head, her voice hoarse. "Jingyu locked him in the firewood shed."

At the mention of Xie Jingyu, Xie Zhongcheng frowned. "Where is Jingyu? Why isn’t he in the funeral hall?"

"Jingyu is ill," Yuan Shi said, covering her mouth as she cried. "He has a headache, and his left leg is completely useless. He can’t even walk. I took the liberty of letting him rest in his room."

Xie Zhongcheng’s mind was in chaos. Even Jingyu was sick? At such a young age, with his left leg paralyzed, it sounded terrifying.

He turned and saw Yun Chu entering the funeral hall. He coldly asked, "The old lady has passed, so why aren’t you in the funeral hall?"

Yun Chu lifted her eyelids. "Are you questioning me, Father-in-law? Fine. I’ll kneel in the funeral hall, burn paper money, and kowtow. Let Sister Ping handle the funeral arrangements."

Xie Zhongcheng’s face darkened.

He had only asked a simple question, and now his daughter-in-law was snapping at him. Was he not even allowed to ask?

But he didn’t dare say more. If he really let Xie Pin handle the funeral, the Xie family would likely become the laughingstock of the entire city again.

"I didn’t mean it that way," he softened his tone. "Right now, people outside are saying that Shiwei killed the old lady. This is severely damaging our family’s reputation. Chu’er, what do you think we should do?"

Before Yun Chu could speak, a servant’s voice came from the entrance: "Madam Yun has arrived!"

Xie Zhongcheng saw Lin Shi enter alone, and his expression worsened.

Even though General Yun had returned to the capital, and Yun Zhe, the Yun family’s legitimate son, was at home, they had only sent a woman to pay their respects. This was clearly a sign of disrespect toward the Xie family!

Lin Shi walked into the funeral hall with a cold expression and offered incense.

Originally, she had come with Yun Siling. But as soon as they left the house, they heard many people discussing the Xie family’s affairs. The rumors were truly shocking.

If what the commoners were saying was true, she couldn’t possibly leave her daughter in this den of wolves. Naturally, she also wouldn’t allow the general to come and give face to the Xie family.

---

chapters.title: Murder Requires Official Intervention
chapters.content:
After offering incense, Lin Shi turned around.

"Father-in-law," she said coolly, "on my way here, I heard people saying that the old lady died a tragic death. Is that true?"

"Those commoners are just spouting nonsense!" Xie Zhongcheng said indignantly. "My mother passed away from a serious illness. She was old and couldn’t endure it any longer."

"Is that so?" Lin Shi gave a cold laugh. "Does Father-in-law really think that by saying this, the commoners will stop talking about the Xie family? That the Censorate won’t find out? That it won’t have any impact on your family’s reputation?"

Xie Zhongcheng clenched his fists tightly.

He had never expected that a death in the Xie family would cause such an uproar in the capital.

In the end, it was all because the Xie family had married a Yun family daughter. The Yun family was so highly regarded that the Xie family had been dragged into the spotlight as well.

"I don’t care what happens to your Xie family," Lin Shi said, her voice growing colder. "Xie Shiwei is a child who previously injured the Marquis of Xuanwu’s heir. I thought it was just childish mischief, but who could have imagined he would kill his own great-grandmother! If he can brutally kill a blood-related elder, then what about a stepmother with no blood ties? If he can kill his great-grandmother, he can kill his stepmother! The Yun family will absolutely not allow our daughter to live under the same roof as a murderer!"

"Mother-in-law, you’re overthinking this!" Yuan Shi hurried over. "Shiwei has always respected Chu’er as his stepmother. How could he possibly…"

"Hah! In your Xie family, what *isn’t* possible?" Lin Shi grabbed Yun Chu’s hand. "Chu’er, your mother is taking you home!"

Xie Shiwei’s character was clearly inherited from the Xie family’s rotten roots. The entire Xie household was full of despicable people. It made her suspect that the premature birth Yun Chu had suffered years ago was also connected to the Xie family!

She deeply regretted being blinded by Xie Jingyu’s status as a *zhuangyuan* (top scholar). She regretted arranging such a marriage for her daughter.

It was all her fault; she had ruined Chu’er!

"Mother-in-law, let’s discuss this properly!" Yuan Shi quickly grabbed Yun Chu’s hand. "The old lady has just passed. If Chu’er, as the eldest daughter-in-law, leaves the Xie family now, it will make it impossible for us to hold our heads up in society. Mother-in-law, whatever you want us to do, we’ll do it. As long as Chu’er stays in the Xie family, anything is fine!"

Xie Zhongcheng softened his tone. "Shiwei definitely won’t stay in the Xie family. On this point, Mother-in-law can rest assured."

Lin Shi coldly replied, "He killed someone. He must pay the price. Your Xie family has only one choice: hand Xie Shiwei over to the authorities!"

Yuan Shi’s legs weakened, and she quickly steadied herself against a servant’s arm.

Xie Zhongcheng tightly clenched his fists.

The Yun family was clearly threatening them, forcing them to hand Shiwei over to the authorities, or else the Yun family would very likely sever ties with the Xie family.

The Xie family was already on shaky ground. They couldn’t afford the blow of a divorce.

He quickly weighed the pros and cons in his mind, closed his eyes, and said slowly, "Then… as Mother-in-law wishes."

The Xie family’s servants had already spread the news of last night’s events. The entire capital was buzzing with rumors, each detail vividly described. If they didn’t provide an explanation, the Xie family would forever be nailed to the pillar of shame.

Sacrificing Xie Shiwei to preserve the entire Xie family… seemed like the only acceptable choice.

Yun Chu escorted Lin Shi out. "Mother, rest assured. The Xie family cannot harm me."

"Chu’er…" Lin Shi sighed. "Your parents will always be your support. The Yun family will always welcome you back."

After seeing Lin Shi off, Yun Chu called for Tingfeng. "Go to the firewood shed now. Tell Xie Shiwei that the Xie family is sending him to the authorities. If he accepts his fate, so be it. If he wants to escape, help him. Give him some silver as well."

Tingfeng nodded and left to carry out the task.

Yuan Shi walked out of the funeral hall, holding onto Xie Zhongcheng’s arm, her voice trembling. "Master, do we really have to send Shiwei to the authorities? He’s only eight!"

"He did something wrong, so he must accept punishment," Xie Zhongcheng said, looking at her. "Now that the old lady is gone, the inner courtyard will rely on you to manage it. Don’t always look like you’re about to cry. If you cry, all the other women and children will cry too, and our Xie family will fall into chaos."

Yuan Shi suppressed her trembling voice. "But we still have Chu’er…"

"Only you would still think that this daughter-in-law is truly on the Xie family’s side!" Xie Zhongcheng lowered his voice. "Ever since she found out that An’ge and his siblings were born to Concubine He, she has grown cold toward the Xie family. Remember this: keep the power of the inner courtyard in your own hands. Don’t always rely on others…"

Yuan Shi’s eyes widened in shock. "What did you say? An’ge is Concubine He’s son?"

This revelation completely shattered her understanding, as if she had been struck on the head, leaving her dizzy.

Xie Zhongcheng shook his head. His wife had been ill for over a decade, taking medicine every day. It seemed to have addled her mind. How could she not have noticed something so obvious?

"No wonder… no wonder Mother-in-law had the idea of divorce," Yuan Shi said, her face ashen. "I heard that these past few days, the Yun family’s elders have intervened to arrange a divorce for a married daughter. The Yun family doesn’t fear the consequences of divorce at all. If the Xie family treats Chu’er poorly, the Yun family elders will definitely step in to divorce her!"

Xie Zhongcheng also sensed the Yun family’s strong stance from Lin Shi’s attitude.

He couldn’t help but worry, would the Yun family disregard everything and push for a divorce?

"Once Jingyu recovers, we must make sure Chu’er becomes pregnant," Yuan Shi turned around, pressing her palms together, and walked to the old lady’s spirit tablet in the funeral hall. "Please, Old Lady, bless Chu’er with a son, so that our Xie family may have a true legitimate heir…"

Xie Shian, kneeling beside the spirit tablet and burning paper money, paused for a moment.

He had always known that his mother had consulted a divine physician. He also knew that his parents were taking medicine to regulate their bodies in hopes of having a child.

Given the Xie family’s current situation, his father would stop at nothing to get his mother pregnant. If the Xie family had a true legitimate son, then what would become of him, the eldest son?

His mother had paved the way for him, securing the Yun family’s connection to the Imperial Academy. He had already benefited from the Yun family’s influence…

But once his mother had her own child, once the Yun family had a legitimate grandson by blood, what use would they have for Xie Shian?

Perhaps… he should add something extra to his father’s medicine… No, that was too risky. A single test of the dregs would expose it…

Xie Shian continued burning paper money, but his mind never stopped. Countless thoughts swirled in his head.

Xie Zhongcheng left the funeral hall and headed toward the firewood shed.

He wanted to personally take Xie Shiwei to the authorities, to show all those gossiping commoners that the Xie family upheld justice, even against their own; that they were not a family of depraved minds!

Just as he reached the door of the firewood shed, a servant woman rushed over in a panic. "Master, it’s not good! Young Master Shiwei… Young Master Shiwei is gone!"

Xie Zhongcheng was furious. "What do you mean, gone?!"

"Just now, Young Master Shiwei was still in the firewood shed, complaining of thirst. This old servant brought him water, locked the shed, and when I went back in a moment later, he was gone!"

"That cursed child actually dared to escape!" Xie Zhongcheng roared. "Everyone, go after him! We must capture this criminal and bring him to justice!"

chapters.title: Tingshuang Gets Married
chapters.content:
The old matriarch’s body was kept in the Xie residence for seven days before the funeral was announced.

During these seven days, Xie Zhongcheng led many people in a frantic search for Xie Shiyou, but not a single trace of him could be found.

Many commoners believed that the Xie family had deliberately hidden him away, and their disdain for the Xie family grew. Some troublemakers even went to the yamen to report that Xie Shiyou, the second young master of the Xie family, had cruelly murdered the old matriarch.

Officials from the yamen paid a special visit to the Xie residence to investigate the matter.

Xie Jingyu, who was already ill, vomited blood in shock upon hearing this news.

Yun Chu entered his room carrying medicine. "The old matriarch cannot rest in peace until the truth is uncovered. The officials will find out what happened, and then she can finally be at peace. Husband, do not worry about this matter. Focus on recovering from your illness."

She handed the medicine in her hands to Jiang Yiniang, who was attending to Xie Jingyu by his side.

Jiang Yiniang carefully helped Xie Jingyu drink the large bowl of dark medicinal liquid.

"Wife..." Xie Jingyu spoke, "Could you, in the name of the Yun family, invite an imperial physician to diagnose my pulse?"

He had a terrifying feeling, as if his body was slowly slipping out of his control.

"I have invited Physician Qiu for you. He is the most famous in the capital for treating such conditions, even surpassing the imperial physicians in the palace." Yun Chu lightly pressed the blanket down for him. "Physician Qiu said that your excessive drinking has caused stagnation in your heart, stirring up a great fire in your liver. As long as you take your medicine and rest properly, you will recover. After the old matriarch’s funeral, there are still some matters to attend to. I will go handle them now."

Xie Jingyu raised his hand and grabbed her sleeve. "Wife, I have only ever asked you for this one thing. I really need an imperial physician."

Upon hearing this, Yun Chu smiled. "Husband, are you sure this is the only thing you have ever asked of me?"

Her smile made Xie Jingyu feel a sharp pain in his eyes. His hand gradually loosened.

"Jiang Yiniang, take good care of the master."

Yun Chu left these words behind and turned to leave.

Jiang Yiniang softly said, "Master, you do not know this, but these past few days, the madam has barely slept due to the old matriarch’s affairs. On top of that, the second young master has gone missing, and the officials keep coming by. The madam has been handling everything... I also want to help the madam, but I am not capable. Taking good care of you, master, is the only way I can share her burden."

Xie Jingyu closed his eyes and said no more.

Yun Chu returned to her own courtyard. She had just sat down and had not even taken a sip of tea when a servant woman rushed in urgently. "Madam, the eldest young miss is causing a commotion in the old matriarch’s courtyard!"

Yun Chu frowned. "What is she making a fuss about?"

"The old matriarch has just passed away, and there are still many fine things in the storeroom. The eldest young miss asked Mama Zhou for the storeroom keys, but Mama Zhou refused. They started arguing, and then Concubine Yu and Concubine Tao joined in. It turned into a big mess."

Yun Chu gave a cold laugh.

The old matriarch’s body was not yet cold, and the Xie family members were already fighting over such petty gains.

She spoke, "The mistress is still here, and I, as the lady of the house, am also here. They have no right to fight over these things. Tingshuang, you go and take the storeroom keys to the mistress. Let’s see what the mistress says."

Tingshuang nodded and left. After a short while, she returned and handed the keys to the An Shou Hall storeroom to Yun Chu. "The mistress said that since the Xie family is now under your management, Madam, the old matriarch’s belongings should naturally be kept by you."

Yun Chu took the keys and played with them. She truly did not care for the old matriarch’s meager possessions.

She said, "Open my storeroom. I want to select a few things."

In the blink of an eye, Tingshuang was about to get married.

According to the Yun family’s customs, a personal maid’s dowry of about a hundred taels of silver was already considered very generous.

Yun Chu prepared a banknote for five hundred taels of silver, along with a complete set of gold and jade filigree hair ornaments, and several bolts of fine fabric.

"M-Madam!" Tingshuang was so shocked by these gifts that her voice trembled. "This slave... this slave cannot accept such generosity. Please, Madam, take them back."

"You can accept them." Yun Chu placed the items on the table. "I have already sent someone to the yamen to remove your slave status. From now on, you are a free woman."

Tingshuang fell to her knees with a thud. "Madam, how can this slave deserve such kindness..."

Yun Chu helped her up.

In her previous life, the great fire at the Xie residence had happened around two years later. In any case, in this life, she would not experience that disaster.

But that did not mean she had forgotten the moment when Tingshuang, without a second thought, had thrown herself on top of her to shield her from the falling beam.

"Tomorrow, on your wedding day, I will give all the maids in Sheng Ju a day off. We will all go to your new home to celebrate." Yun Chu smiled. "After your marriage, take a month’s rest, then go to manage the hot spring estate. You will be in charge there as a stewardess, and your wages will not be stingy."

Tingshuang’s throat choked up, and she could not say a word.

The next morning, the matchmaker Yun Chu had invited helped Tingshuang with her hair and makeup, and she changed into her wedding dress. The bridal sedan chair left the Xie residence through the side gate, where Yu Jiu was waiting.

For servants’ weddings, leaving through the side gate was already a great honor bestowed by the master.

Yun Chu, accompanied by the maids and servants of Sheng Ju, went to drink the wedding toast. However, as the mistress, she feared that her presence would make others uncomfortable, so after a drink, she left.

Tingxue and Tingfeng stayed to join the celebration, while she and Qiutong returned.

On the way back, they passed by a jewelry shop called Baibao Pavilion. She remembered that the dowry she was preparing for her half-sister, Yun Ran, seemed to be missing an outstanding hairpin.

She lifted her skirt and stepped out of the carriage, entering Baibao Pavilion. It had been a very long time since she had visited a jewelry shop. As she walked in, she was almost dazzled by the sight.

The counter was filled with many eye-catching gold, silver, and jade ornaments for customers to browse freely. If someone intended to make a purchase, the shopkeeper would lead them inside and bring out even finer items for selection.

"This madam, these are our newly arrived hairpins. Please take a look. Is there anything that catches your eye?"

Yun Chu was actually only twenty years old. Although she had been married for five years, she still had a woman’s love for such beautiful things in her heart.

It was just that over these years, too many things had distracted her attention, and she had basically not bought any jewelry or hair ornaments. The ones she wore in her hair were still the dowry gifts from the Yun family from five years ago.

Seeing these ornaments, her mood immediately brightened.

She currently had hundreds of thousands of taels of silver at her disposal. Buying a few things to make herself happy was not excessive, was it?

"This one, this one, and this one..."

She pointed at the tray with her hand.

The shopkeeper was overjoyed. Selling so many at once meant he had encountered a big customer.

"Just exclude these three. Wrap up the rest." Yun Chu looked at the shopkeeper. "Do you have more? I’d like to see."

The shopkeeper was stunned.

A tray held twenty small hairpins, and this madam had actually chosen seventeen of them, and it was still not enough; she wanted to see more.

He quickly nodded. "Madam, please wait a moment. I will bring out the new stock right away."

The shopkeeper hurriedly called his assistants and brought out all the newly arrived hair ornaments, hairpins, earrings, bracelets... and laid them out in front of Yun Chu.

She selected some for her mother and elder sister-in-law, and also bought one hairpin for each of the maids in the courtyard.

In addition to these, she also bought two long-life locks.

One for Yu Ge’er, and one for Changsheng. She just did not know when she would see them again.

"Madam Xie!"

Just as she was about to get into the carriage, a pleasant female voice called out from behind her.

She turned around and saw the Marchioness of Xuanyu, Luo Shi.

---

chapters.title: The Concubine is Called Chu Niang
chapters.content:
Teahouse.

Yun Chu and Luo Shi sat across from each other.

"Madam Xie, this hairpin in your hair is truly beautiful."

Luo Shi, holding her teacup, noticed the new hairpin in Yun Chu’s hair and sincerely complimented it.

Yun Chu smiled. "Marchioness Luo, surely you did not just want to have tea with me, did you?"

Luo Shi looked at her. "Even when I was still in the boudoir, I had heard many people speak of the eldest miss of the Yun family, the number one beauty of the capital. Suitors had nearly worn out the threshold of your door. I always thought that the eldest miss of the Yun family was like a cloud at the edge of the sky, far, far away from me. No matter how beautiful you were, it had nothing to do with me. But now I realize, I was wrong..."

Yun Chu took a sip of tea.

She had been keeping a close watch on Xuanyu Marquis Qin Mingheng. Naturally, she knew that, under the deliberate guidance of a young servant, Luo Shi had taken people to the small courtyard outside the city where the Marquis kept his concubines, and had caught the Marquis red-handed.

Now, the two concubines in the small courtyard were under the control of the Luo family.

She had not instructed the young servant to hide his identity, so it was not surprising that Luo Shi had come to her.

But why was Luo Shi speaking so strangely? Shouldn’t she be questioning her about why she had guided all of this?

"Madam Xie, did you know that my husband, the Xuanyu Marquis, has kept concubines outside? And not just one, but two." Luo Shi laughed, but her smile was filled with indescribable pain. "Everyone in the capital says I married a good husband. After so many years of marriage, there is not even a concubine in the Marquis’s residence. I, too, had always believed that my husband and I shared a deep affection. But when I saw those two concubines, I realized that my husband had always had someone else in his heart."

Luo Shi stared at Yun Chu. "Those two concubines look like Madam Xie. Especially the pregnant one; when I saw her from the side, I almost thought she was Madam Xie herself."

Yun Chu’s fingers suddenly froze.

It was as if a venomous snake had slithered up from her feet, hissing in her ear and making her scalp crawl.

"I also discovered that there is a secret room in the Marquis’s residence. The walls of that room are covered with portraits, all of them of Madam Xie." Luo Shi’s voice grew hoarse. "So, my husband’s true love is the number one beauty of the capital, the eldest miss of the Yun family, now Madam Xie. Since his beloved married someone else, he found two women who resemble her and kept them outside, living an ordinary married life with them... Then what am I? What do I count as?"

As she spoke, she broke down and began to cry into her handkerchief.

Yun Chu felt as if she had swallowed countless flies, utterly disgusted.

She felt her stomach churning constantly. Only after drinking several large mouthfuls of tea did she manage to suppress the sensation.

She patted Luo Shi’s shoulder, silently comforting her. After about a quarter of an hour, Luo Shi finally stopped crying. "I’m sorry, I must have made a fool of myself in front of Madam Xie."

"If Marchioness Luo has told me all this, then I should not hide the truth either." Yun Chu looked up. "Marchioness Luo, did you know that it was I who intentionally had the young servant guide you to that small courtyard?"

Luo Shi had known that someone was deliberately guiding her, but she had not yet investigated who it was. She had been so overwhelmed with grief that she had lost her mind and did not know what to do.

When she saw that room filled with portraits of Madam Xie, she had completely broken down and come straight to Madam Xie.

She truly had not expected that it was Madam Xie who had guided her to discover her husband’s concubines.

Could it be that Madam Xie had long known about Marquis Qin Mingheng’s dark, shameful intentions?

"Indeed, I have known about the Marquis’s intentions for a long time. Last time, when I accompanied my husband to the Marquis’s residence to apologize, Marchioness Luo probably does not know that the Marquis put something in my tea." Yun Chu’s expression turned cold. "He dared to do such a thing, so naturally, I had to make him pay the price."

With a clatter, Luo Shi’s teacup spilled onto the table. She hastily wiped the tea with her handkerchief and asked anxiously, "He didn’t... do anything improper to Madam Xie, did he?"

Yun Chu pressed her lips together and said nothing.

The events of her wedding night were unspeakable. Just thinking about that night made her bones turn cold.

From Yun Chu’s expression, Luo Shi seemed to read something.

The two of them sat in silence for a long, long time.

Yun Chu looked at her. "As a woman, I want to tell Marchioness Luo something in advance. The Yun family will not let the Xuanyu Marquis off. In the future, there may no longer be a Marquis of Xuanyu’s residence."

Luo Shi’s eyes shot up.

The Yun family was a first-rank general’s residence, and General Yun had just returned to the capital, greatly favored by the Emperor.

If the Yun family wanted to deal with the Xuanyu Marquis’s residence, it would be as easy as snapping their fingers. Making the Marquis disappear was not an empty boast.

"Before things escalate, Marchioness Luo still has time to make a choice." Yun Chu stood up. "Marchioness Luo, take your time to think. I will take my leave now."

Yun Chu had been gone for nearly an hour when Luo Shi finally managed to stand up, steadying herself against the table.

She had not eaten much in the past two days and felt weak. She had to lean on her maid’s arm to keep her balance.

She took a carriage back to the Xuanyu Marquis’s residence. As soon as she entered her own courtyard, a cup crashed at her feet. She looked up and saw Qin Mingheng sitting in her room.

"Finally back!" Qin Mingheng’s face was filled with anger. "Where have you locked Chu Niang and Qiu Wen? Chu Niang is pregnant and cannot be startled. Release them at once!"

At the mention of "Chu Niang," Luo Shi thought of Yun Chu. If Madam Xie knew that this man had deliberately given his concubine this name, she would surely be even more furious.

She slowly walked in and sat down. "I can release them. I can even let them enter the Marquis’s residence. But on one condition: the child must be aborted."

Qin Mingheng’s expression changed. "Impossible!"

"Husband, after we had our son, you said that you feared having too many children would lead to a struggle for the title of heir in the future. We agreed that we would only have one child in this lifetime." Luo Shi looked at him. "That was your promise. If you keep it, then I will let those two women in."

After their son was born, her husband had never touched her again. She had thought it was because he truly did not want more children.

But it turned out that her husband had another family outside. He had only given her face and dignity, while all his affection had gone to those two concubines.

Qin Mingheng’s expression darkened.

He had fulfilled his duty as the Xuanyu Marquis by having a legitimate son with Luo Shi, who could be enfeoffed as the heir.

The child in Chu Niang’s womb was the one he truly wanted, a child who would look like him, and also like Yun Chu...

He had never intended for the child in Chu Niang’s womb to become the heir. He only wanted to live a simple life as a family of three with Chu Niang and the child. This simple wish had been destroyed by the woman in front of him.

His eyes seemed to burn with fire.

Luo Shi pressed her lips together. "I just went to see Madam Xie and told her about your concubines."

"What did you say?!"

Qin Mingheng leapt to his feet.

Yun Chu already despised him. If she found out that he had secretly kept concubines, then he and Yun Chu would never have a chance again.

He had given Luo Shi enough face and respect. Why had she ruined his image in Yun Chu’s eyes...?

chapters.title: Requesting Her Own Divorce
chapters.content:
Luo Shi stared at the man before her in disbelief.

After so many years of marriage, he had always treated her with respect and care. She never expected that beneath his false facade lay such a true nature.

She forced back the bitterness in her eyes and continued, "I’ve already had someone abort the child in Chu Niang’s womb."

One shocking revelation after another made Qin Mingheng lose control of his emotions.

He stepped forward and, before Luo Shi could react, grabbed her slender throat.

"Ugh—"

Luo Shi felt the five fingers around her neck tighten rapidly. A suffocating sensation surged over her like a tidal wave. For the first time, she felt death was so close.

"Mother, let go of my mother!"

The young heir of Marquis Xuanwu rushed in and started punching and kicking Qin Mingheng.

But Qin Mingheng, as if gone mad, pushed the young heir aside with one hand.

With a thud, the child’s head hit the doorframe, and a piercing cry erupted.

Only then did Qin Mingheng seem to wake from a nightmare and release Luo Shi.

"Cough, cough, cough!" Luo Shi coughed violently, instinctively pulling the child into her arms. "Mother is here, Mother is fine, don’t be afraid, don’t be afraid..."

She had the wet nurse take the child away immediately.

Only then did she look at Qin Mingheng. "Husband, I was lying to you just now. I didn’t harm the child in Chu Niang’s womb..."

She had only been testing this man, wanting to know how much that unborn bastard meant to her husband in his heart. Now she had her answer.

Qin Mingheng let out a long, heavy sigh.

He crouched down and helped Luo Shi up. "I’m sorry, Madam. I was too impulsive just now. Does your neck hurt? Should I call a physician to examine you?"

Luo Shi bit her lower lip.

He had turned back into the gentle husband he used to be.

If not for the lingering pain in her neck, if not for the deep experience of that near-death sensation, perhaps she would have been deceived again.

If this man had even a shred of affection left for her, if this man had shown the slightest concern for their child, perhaps she would have hesitated.

But there was no need.

Absolutely no need.

"Chu Niang and Qiu Wen are at the Luo residence." Luo Shi straightened her body. "I will go fetch them back to the marquis’s estate now."

Qin Mingheng pressed his lips together. "You said you told Madam Xie about my concubines. What was her reaction upon hearing it?"

"Madam Xie said that it’s perfectly normal for men to have three wives and four concubines. She advised me to accept it." Luo Shi lowered her eyelids. "It’s getting late. I should return to my maiden home."

She turned and walked out of the room, had the wet nurse pick up the child, and left the Marquis Xuanwu’s estate as quickly as possible.

---

The next morning, after the people who came to pay their respects at Shengju had left, a young servant from the front courtyard hurried to the side hall.

The servant’s name was Duo Xi, around fifteen or sixteen years old, quite clever. Standing at the bottom of the steps, he reported, "Yesterday evening, the marchioness took the young heir back to the Luo residence. This morning, Lady Luo and Lord Luo personally escorted the marquis’s two concubines to the door. They said their daughter was too jealous to tolerate concubines and their children, so on her behalf, they requested a divorce, asking the marquis to divorce his wife. They even said the heir’s title was no longer needed."

Listen Feng’s face was filled with shock. "Why request her own divorce? Why not just separate?"

Yun Chu smiled slightly.

Marquis Xuanwu was, after all, a prominent and respected family. To maintain face, the marquis would never agree to a separation. Who knew how long the dispute would drag on.

But by Luo Shi claiming she was jealous and requesting her own divorce, even giving up the heir’s title, it appeared on the surface that she was at fault, giving the marquis’s estate enough face.

In reality, however, it was Luo Shi’s parents who went to pressure the marquis, forcing him to agree to the divorce.

The Luo family’s reputation might suffer temporarily, but once Marquis Xuanwu fell from grace, Luo Shi’s request for her own divorce would be seen as the wisest move.

So, as long as it was known that Marquis Xuanwu had offended the Yun family, the entire Luo family, including all the clan elders, would quickly distance themselves from the Marquis Xuanwu’s estate.

It had to be said, Luo Shi was a clear-headed woman.

Even after suffering such a heavy blow, she could still come up with the most stable path forward.

The scandal between the Marquis Xuanwu’s estate and the Luo family spread like wildfire through the capital, quickly overshadowing the news of Old Madam Xie’s death.

Yuan Shi let out a sigh of relief, but also a sigh of regret. "The marchioness, upon learning of her husband’s concubines, left the marquis’s estate without hesitation... Back then, if Chu’er had known that He Concubine was a concubine and had three children with Jing Yu, she probably would have left our Xie family as well... Chu’er has been deceived for so many years, suffered so many grievances, yet she still wholeheartedly considered our Xie family. She truly is a rare and good child."

Xie Zhongcheng frowned. "Do you think that little bastard is hiding somewhere?"

At the mention of Xie Shiyou, Yuan Shi’s heart ached. An eight-year-old child, hiding alone outside, who knew how much he had suffered.

She didn’t dare say much. She selected a hairpin from her vanity box, wrapped it up, and went to find Yun Chu. "Chu’er, your younger sister is about to get married. Our Xie family is still in mourning, so we won’t attend the wedding banquet at the Yun residence. Please give this hairpin to Sister Ran on my behalf as part of her dowry."

Yun Chu nodded and placed the hairpin in the box.

Yun Ran’s marriage to the Dai family was set for autumn. By the end of August, it was already past the Start of Autumn, but the weather was still scorching.

Early in the morning was still somewhat cool, but once the sun came out, the temperature rose rapidly. Sitting in a carriage without an ice basin, one could break out in a sweat.

Yun Chu brought Xie Pin with her to the Yun residence for the wedding banquet.

When they arrived, it was still early. The courtyard didn’t have many guests, or perhaps because it was the marriage of a concubine’s daughter, the Yun family hadn’t invited too many people.

Yun Chu went directly to Yun Ran’s courtyard. The women of the Yun family were all there, both inside and outside the house.

The matchmaker, Wu Fu, was combing Yun Ran’s hair. She was dressed in a red wedding gown, her face adorned with exquisite makeup, looking radiant and charming.

"Eldest Sister."

Yun Ran, seeing Yun Chu, called out shyly.

Yun Chu took a box from Tingxue’s hands and placed it in front of Yun Ran. "This is the dowry gift I prepared for you."

Before Yun Ran could speak, a hand reached out from the side, it was the Third Aunt of the Yun family. She took the box. "Chu’er, you are truly generous. This set of red gold hairpiece with emeralds must be worth at least a thousand taels of silver. And that’s not all, there’s also a box of gold beans... Oh my, there’s even a stack of silver notes..."

The women around stretched their necks to look.

In a family like the Yun’s, the dowry for a daughter’s marriage was substantial. The legitimate eldest daughter, Yun Chu, had a dowry of thirty thousand taels of silver. A better-off branch of the Yun family would prepare ten thousand taels for a daughter, while a less well-off one would give five thousand... For Yun Ran, just the gifts from Yun Chu alone amounted to five thousand taels. Adding what her stepmother, Lady Lin, had prepared, it was close to twenty thousand taels. And this was for a concubine’s daughter marrying into the Dai family. Many women couldn’t help but look on with envy.

Xie Pin stood at the edge of the crowd, tiptoeing to catch a glimpse. Seeing the red gold hairpiece and the stack of silver notes, she couldn’t help but turn red-eyed.

Her own dowry consisted only of the wedding dress she had embroidered herself and some private savings, not exceeding a hundred taels of silver...

But she knew in her heart that her mother had reasons for not preparing a dowry for her. She just needed to obey and listen...

---

chapters.title: Marquis Xuanwu Divorces His Wife
chapters.content:
The auspicious hour arrived, and the Dai family’s bridal sedan chair also arrived.

The matchmaker led Yun Ran out. As they reached the gate, Yun Ran looked back at Lady Lin and couldn’t help but cry.

Her birth mother had died in childbirth. She had grown up by her stepmother’s side, who had treated her like her own daughter and never let her suffer any grievances.

After marriage, returning would not be so easy.

Lady Lin’s eyes also moistened.

The matchmaker wiped Yun Ran’s tears, covered her with the red bridal veil, and led her all the way to the gate.

Soon after, firecrackers exploded, and the gongs and drums of the Dai family’s welcoming procession grew louder. The bridal sedan chair was lifted and gradually moved farther away from the Yun residence.

Lady Lin forced a smile. "Alright, my daughter has left home. Everyone, please take your seats and start the banquet. Don’t stand on ceremony, sit down."

The Yun family’s banquet did not separate men and women. The whole family sat at one table, gathered in the front courtyard, young and old, lively and bustling.

Yun Chu sat with Xie Pin and the Yun family members. Beside her sat the Third Aunt of the Yun family and her daughter-in-law, Qi Shi, the wife of her cousin Yun Run, whom she addressed as Sister Run.

The Third Aunt casually asked, "Chu’er, how exactly did that old lady from your Xie family pass away..."

Before she could finish, Qi Shi pulled her arm. "Mother, didn’t you just want to know about the Marquis Xuanwu’s estate? Lady Li over there seems to know a lot. Why don’t you go ask her?"

The Third Aunt, who loved gossip, immediately got up and went to Lady Li.

Qi Shi apologetically turned to Yun Chu. "Chu’er, my mother-in-law is straightforward and outspoken. Please don’t take it to heart."

"You worry too much, Sister Run." Yun Chu smiled. "The Third Aunt is just inquiring about the facts. She doesn’t mean any harm. Why would I take it to heart?"

As she spoke, she heard the group of women around Lady Li discussing the Marquis Xuanwu’s estate and the Luo family.

"Did you say Marquis Xuanwu actually wrote a divorce letter? He keeps concubines and still has the face to divorce his wife."

"Listen to what you’re saying. In this world, which man doesn’t have three wives and four concubines? Luo Shi is domineering, so Marquis Xuanwu can only sneak around. Keeping concubines is just a last resort."

"Marquis Xuanwu has made a wrong move this time. He divorced his legitimate wife and gained two concubines. Who knows what he’s thinking."

"Hasn’t Luo Shi made a wrong move too? Her only son has even lost his title as heir. She ruined her own son’s bright future."

"With a Luo family woman being divorced, it will be hard for Luo family girls to find good marriages in the future."

"The Luo family’s official rank is just too low, only the third rank. Even a daughter from a collateral branch of the first-rank Yun family can smoothly separate, yet Luo Shi, the legitimate eldest daughter of the main branch, was actually divorced."

...

Yun Chu listened casually.

It was true she wanted to take revenge on Qin Mingheng, but she didn’t want to involve Luo Shi, an innocent victim. Since Luo Shi had already extricated herself, it was time to act.

She was about to get up when the banquet hall suddenly fell silent. It turned out a distinguished guest had arrived.

She looked up and saw her father leading Prince Pingxi, along with the prince’s young heir and young lady, slowly walking in.

She looked at the two children. It had been many days since she last saw them. This one glance eased much of her longing.

If she looked any longer, she would want nothing more than to pull the children into her arms. She had to look away and suppress this thought.

The people in the banquet hall were all stunned.

It was only the marriage of a concubine’s daughter from the Yun family, yet a prince had personally come to offer his congratulations.

From this, one could see just how much the imperial family valued the Yun family.

As soon as Chu Hongyu saw Yun Chu, he could barely contain himself. But he knew he couldn’t rush over in such a public setting.

He understood these principles, but Chu Changsheng did not. Her eyes sparkled as she looked at Yun Chu. She broke free from her father’s hand and started walking toward Yun Chu.

"Changsheng!" Chu Hongyu quickly grabbed his sister’s arm. "No, not now. There are too many people. If we go over now, it will cause trouble for Mother. Father said we must not be too intimate with Mother in public. You eat first. I’ll think of a way."

The little girl had no choice but to obediently nestle in Chu Yi’s arms.

"Small Marquis and Small Lady seem to be looking at us." The Third Aunt’s eyes sparkled. "Da’ge’er, the Small Marquis probably wants to play with you. Go find the marquis."

Da’ge’er was the Third Aunt’s grandson, a little over six years old and at the height of mischief. However, he wasn’t bold enough to go over.

Yun Zhenjiang was also sitting nearby. He glanced at Chu Hongyu and knew the boy was looking at his aunt.

Previously, when his aunt was recovering at the Yun residence, this boy came every day, following her around and calling her "Auntie," which was annoying to watch.

His aunt used to dote on him the most. But ever since this boy came along, his aunt barely paid attention to him anymore. It was infuriating.

Yun Zhenjiang huffed and looked away from Chu Hongyu.

After a while, he felt someone tugging at his sleeve. He turned his head and came face to face with Chu Hongyu’s big eyes. He coldly said, "Prince Pingxi’s heir, why are you hiding here pulling at me?"

Chu Hongyu, hiding among the bushes, looked pitiful. "Jiang Ge, can’t I call you Ge? Come here. I have something to tell you."

Yun Zhenjiang coldly huffed, "No time."

"I brought a flying dart. Do you want it?"

Yun Zhenjiang was, after all, only a six-year-old child. He loved these kinds of things. Hearing this, how could he resist? He immediately followed Chu Hongyu to the side of the bushes.

Chu Hongyu took out a flying dart from his sleeve. This was a new toy he had secretly obtained from the Ministry of War, given to him by the Minister of War himself.

He hadn’t even played with it many times himself, yet he was already giving it away.

But he had no choice.

He had finally convinced his father to come to the Yun residence. His father said that just one glance at his mother would be enough. Once the banquet was over, they would have to leave obediently.

So, while the banquet was still ongoing, he had to find a way to get his mother away and have a good talk with her. Giving up a flying dart in exchange for a chance to talk to his mother didn’t seem like a bad deal.

"Given your sincerity, I’ll help you." Yun Zhenjiang held the flying dart, unable to put it down. "But I must warn you, men and women should not touch each other. You are not allowed to always cling to my aunt, not allowed to hug my aunt, and not allowed to..."

"Okay, okay, I remember!" Chu Hongyu smiled. "The banquet is almost over. Hurry and find Aunt Yun. Tell her that I and Changsheng are waiting for her!"

Yun Zhenjiang put away the flying dart and went to find Yun Chu.

The two children waited in the side courtyard for a while before they saw Yun Chu walk in.

"Mother... Aunt Yun!"

Chu Hongyu saw Yun Zhenjiang following behind Yun Chu and quickly changed his address.

The little girl quickly pounced into Yun Chu’s arms, climbing up with all fours. Chu Hongyu was about to do the same when he received a warning look from Yun Zhenjiang.

"Brother Yu, Changsheng, I’ve prepared gifts for you." Yun Chu took out two longevity locks from her sleeve that she had prepared long ago. "This one is for Brother Yu, and this one is for Changsheng. Do you like them?"

"I like them, I like them very much!" Chu Hongyu smugly looked at Yun Zhenjiang. "Jiang Ge, Aunt Yun definitely didn’t give you a longevity lock, right?"

Yun Zhenjiang nodded. "Indeed, she didn’t."

Chu Hongyu was delighted. It seemed that in Aunt Yun’s heart, he was more important than Yun Zhenjiang.

"But, when I was born, Aunt gave me a jade pendant. On my first birthday, she gave me a set of scholar’s four treasures. When I was two, she gave me handmade clothes. When I was three, she gave me... When I was four..."

Chu Hongyu: "..."

He covered his ears.

If he listened any further, he would really feel jealous.

chapters.title: Tenderness in His Eyes
chapters.content:
Chu Hongyu was so jealous his eyes turned green.

Yun Zhenjiang suddenly felt a pang of pity for the boy. He had no birth mother, and probably not many in the palace truly cared for him. And just now, Yun Zhenjiang had even tricked him out of a spinning spear.

Reluctantly, he took out the spinning spear and tossed it to him. "I'm tired of playing with it. Here, take it back."

Chu Hongyu quickly caught it. "You gave this up yourself, so don’t regret it later, okay?"

Yun Zhenjiang huffed.

Yun Chu couldn’t help but laugh. These children were all so adorable.

At that moment, a voice came from behind: "Lady Xie."

She turned and saw a tall figure standing at the courtyard gate.

Dressed in dark brocade robes, his hair tied with a jade crown, and a jade pendant hanging from his belt, the man exuded an overwhelming presence.

Chu Hongyu, feeling guilty, hid behind Yun Chu. He had promised his father he would only take a quick look at his mother, yet here he was, secretly meeting her.

His father would never agree to such requests again.

"There is something I wish to seek Lady Xie’s permission for," Chu Yi said calmly. "Lady Xie must know that my daughter, Changsheng, has been frail since birth. I had a physician visit the hot spring estate, and he said the springs there would benefit her health. So I was wondering... could we set aside a private bath for her at the estate? Rest assured, Lady Xie, I will pay every coin that is due."

Yun Chu nodded without hesitation. "The hot spring estate is managed jointly by me and the Prince. Bringing up money is unnecessary..."

"The preparations at the hot spring estate are almost complete," Chu Yi said. "There are some matters that require Lady Xie’s decision. If you have time tomorrow, perhaps you could pay a visit?"

Yun Chu nodded.

After forming a partnership with Chu Yi, he had arranged a steward for the hot spring estate. Chen Bo had reported that the steward was a loyal servant who managed the late Concubine Yin’s properties and was quite capable. With the steward in place, progress at the estate had been swift.

Since she was in the hot spring business, she couldn’t just be a figurehead; she naturally had to go and see for herself.

"Father, can Changsheng and I go to the estate tomorrow?" Chu Hongyu tugged at Chu Yi’s sleeve, pleading pitifully. "Anyway, Changsheng’s treatment starts the day after tomorrow. Going a day early won’t hurt. Father, please? I promise to write ten pages of calligraphy, or even twenty... Father, just say yes!"

Chu Changsheng remained silent, her misty eyes fixed on Chu Yi.

Chu Yi’s resolve was already wavering.

When he saw the hope in Yun Chu’s eyes, his last bit of resistance vanished.

"Alright, you may go," he said. "But you must behave. If you don’t, I’ll have someone send you both back to the prince’s residence."

"Father, you’re the best!" Chu Hongyu jumped for joy. "Father, I love you the most!"

Chu Changsheng smiled, her eyes curving like crescent moons.

Chu Yi ruffled the little girl’s hair, then looked at Yun Chu. Seeing the woman smiling as well, her eyes like gentle crescents, he felt a warmth in his chest.

Just as Yun Ze entered the courtyard, he caught this scene.

He saw the Prince of Pingxi looking at his sister with an expression he had never seen before. The usually cold and distant man, whose gaze was as icy as his demeanor, actually had tenderness in his eyes.

Yun Ze thought he must have seen wrong. He looked again, no, the tenderness was still there.

Then he looked at Yun Chu.

The Prince of Pingxi’s heir and princess were laughing, Yun Chu was watching the children, and the Prince of Pingxi was watching Yun Chu. It looked like a family of four.

Only his foolish son, Jiang Ge’er, was squatting to the side, playing with mud.

"Cough, cough!"

Yun Ze cleared his throat, breaking the brief tranquility in the courtyard.

"Your Highness," he said, "Earlier, Minister Fang was looking for you everywhere."

Chu Yi’s expression remained indifferent. "What does he want with me?"

"It seems..." Yun Ze hesitated, "I saw Minister Yin speaking with Minister Fang for a long time. It appears they intend to arrange a marriage between the eldest Miss Fang and the Princess Consort of Pingxi."

Chu Yi’s expression subtly shifted.

After the incident with the second Miss Tan, he had made it clear to his mother that he would not consider taking a consort for now.

Why was his mother still letting his maternal family meddle in such matters?

Seeing his elder brother and the Prince of Pingxi in conversation, Yun Chu took the children’s hands and led them to the other side of the courtyard, where there was a swing her grandfather had made for Jiang Ge’er. The three children took turns sitting on it while Yun Chu pushed them, their laughter filling the courtyard.

"Lady Yun, higher, even higher! Wow, I’m flying!" Chu Hongyu, fearless, even tried to stand on the swing.

Yun Zhenjiang puffed up his cheeks, hands on his hips. "We agreed each gets ten pushes! Get off, now!"

"Oh, you’re so stingy!" Chu Hongyu refused. "This is your family’s swing. You can use it every day. Why are you fighting me for it?"

"Changsheng, let’s ignore him." Yun Zhenjiang took Chu Changsheng’s hand. "There are other fun things over there. Come, I’ll take you to play."

Chu Hongyu watched in disbelief as his sister actually followed Yun Zhenjiang meekly. Before the swing even stopped, he jumped off and shouted, "Changsheng!"

Yun Zhenjiang, being mischievous, pulled Chu Changsheng along faster and faster.

Unable to keep up, Chu Hongyu ran to Yun Chu to tattle. "Lady Yun, Jiang Ge won’t play with me anymore!"

Yun Chu crouched down. "Then think carefully about why he won’t play with you."

Chu Hongyu lowered his head, kicking at small pebbles with his feet.

"Before the swing, we agreed each would get ten pushes. But you hogged it all to yourself. Isn’t it natural he doesn’t want to play with you?" Yun Chu ruffled his hair. "Jiang Ge’er isn’t a stingy person. Go apologize, and he’ll play with you again."

Chu Hongyu tilted his head in thought, then turned and shouted, "Jiang Ge, I was wrong! I promise I won’t be greedy again!"

Soon, the three children were playing together again.

The joyful moments always passed quickly. Before Yun Chu knew it, the banquet was over.

Chu Yi led the two children away.

Fortunately, they would all meet again tomorrow at the hot spring estate, so there was no lingering sense of farewell.

After seeing off the guests, Yun Ze called for Yun Chu, and they went to General Yun’s courtyard.

"Chu’er, this is a secret decree the Emperor sent me this morning." Yun Sixin placed the decree on the table. "As you said, the Emperor has ordered me to go to the southern border to execute the General of Chariots and Cavalry. The Emperor received intelligence that the general has been secretly colluding with the King of Nanyue, plotting to seize several of our southern border cities..."

Yun Ze was also just hearing of this, his face filled with shock. "Has the General of Chariots and Cavalry gone mad? He is the Empress Dowager’s own nephew. Why would he commit treason?"

General Yun spoke up. "You young ones probably don’t know this, but the current Empress Dowager is not the Emperor’s biological mother."

Yun Ze’s face showed sheer astonishment.

This was the first time Yun Chu had heard of this as well.
