"Given that the Empress Dowager holds great military power and has long been under the Emperor’s suspicion, never having returned to the capital all these years, it’s not surprising that the General of Chariots and Cavalry has developed rebellious intentions." Yun Sixin said, "But none of that is the point. The point is, Chu’er, in your dream, our Yun family is executed in a little over ten years..."

---

chapters.title: No Need for Knives or Swords
chapters.content:
The three generations of the Yun family fell silent.

They had always feared that their merits would invite the Emperor’s jealousy. Even after years of deliberately lowering their profile, in a little over ten years, they would still face the fate of execution.

Throughout history, how many great generals had been killed by the very emperors they served after achieving fame and success?

They couldn’t help but sigh when reading about those wronged generals in history books. But to learn that one day, such a thing would happen to the Yun family...

Dying in battle was one thing; they would die with honor.

But being framed for treason and having over a hundred family members beheaded? Who could accept that?

"If what Chu’er dreamed is bound to happen one day, then our Yun family cannot sit and wait for death," Yun Ze said slowly. "Father, what if we return our military power and retire from the army?"

As long as they controlled the military, one day their achievements would make the Emperor uneasy. If they gave up their military power, wouldn’t all future disasters be avoided?

"The Emperor would likely refuse," Yun Sixin shook his head. "Before there is someone capable of replacing me, the Emperor will never allow the Yun family to retire. Moreover, the border countries have been repeatedly testing our defenses. If I just abandon my post, who knows how many common people will suffer..."

Yun Chu gave a bitter laugh.

Yes, as long as the Yun family still had value, the Emperor would never let them go.

But once the Yun family was no longer useful, many things would be out of their control.

Moving forward was difficult, and retreating was just as hard.

The Yun family was placed in such a position, appearing prosperous on the surface, but in reality, they were standing over a furnace, being scorched.

"Our Yun family has served in the military for generations. Countless men have died on the battlefield, and in the end, even our women and children are to be executed. It breaks my heart!" General Yun said coldly. "Since giving up power won’t work, then we must choose a better tree to nest in... Our Yun family originally pledged loyalty only to the Emperor, but now we are forced to involve ourselves in the struggle for the throne. The Eighth Prince is of our Yun family’s blood..."

"The Eighth Prince is too kind-hearted," Yun Ze shook his head. "Aunt also has no intention of seizing the throne. Why drag them into this?"

General Yun turned to Yun Chu. "Did you see in your dream who eventually becomes Emperor?"

Yun Chu thought for a moment before answering, "In the dream, the Fourth Prince dies, the Fifth Prince is crippled, the Sixth Prince is exiled, the Seventh Prince supports the Second Prince, the Eighth Prince dies... The Crown Prince’s position is unstable, and the Third Prince is also suspected of rebellion... As for who ultimately takes the throne, it’s hard to say. After all, the younger princes are still growing up."

The expressions of the others grew solemn.

If they chose to support a prince, they had to be extremely careful. One wrong move, and like in Chu’er’s dream, they would lose everything.

"More than ten years until the disaster befalls the Yun family, and here you all are, looking like you’re attending a funeral!" General Yun huffed. "Keep this matter buried deep in your hearts. Don’t let the women and children at home worry. We still have time. We’ll think carefully about what to do. With this old ginger here, rest assured, our Yun family won’t be finished just like that."

"Prepare for both possibilities," Yun Sixin said. "I will try to cultivate a successor as soon as possible. Yun Ze, you should privately contact several princes. It doesn’t matter which one, test them all and see which is the most suitable."

Yun Ze nodded. "Father, leave this to me."

Yun Chu paused before saying, "So, Father, you still have to go to the southern border?"

She picked up a brush and paper from the desk, writing as she spoke. "This trip to the southern border is extremely dangerous. After you left with your men in the ninth month, all contact was lost for two months. When you returned to the capital, two years had passed, and many things had happened in that time..."

The men of the Yun family never discussed court or battlefield matters with the women. For example, at such an important moment, her mother and sister-in-law were not present. She was only here because of the dream she had, which allowed her to participate in the Yun family’s decision-making...

She knew about her father’s experiences in the southern border because one day, after he had too much to drink, he had recounted those two years in broken fragments.

"Father, you must remember a woman named Qiu Xiang." Yun Chu pursed her lips and wrote the name on the paper. "This woman was someone you rescued on the road on a whim. She then took advantage of the situation and became your concubine. Because of her, you were lured into Nanyue and held captive by the King of Nanyue..."

Before Yun Chu could finish, General Yun raised his hand and slapped the back of Yun Sixin’s head. "You still had the mind to take a concubine? What nonsense is this?"

The mighty General Yun Sixin, who commanded three hundred thousand troops, now sat there rubbing the back of his head with a wronged expression.

An event that hadn’t even happened yet, and might not even occur in the future; why was he getting slapped for it?

Yun Chu felt no sympathy for her father.

As for elders taking concubines, she, as a junior, had no right to say anything. But after returning to the capital, her father had never told her mother about this. From beginning to end, her mother had no idea that her father had been deceived so miserably by a woman...

"Chu’er, this matter stays between us," Yun Sixin said awkwardly. "Father promises you, if that woman, Qiu-something-Xiang, ever appears, I’ll kill her!"

Yun Ze said dryly, "Chu’er only mentioned it once, and you already remembered her name is Qiu Xiang."

Yun Sixin: "..."

Could they not have a proper conversation?

The family discussed for a little over an hour before finally covering everything that needed to be said.

After finishing the serious matters, Yun Chu took a letter from her sleeve and handed it to Yun Sixin. "Father, please place this letter in the study of Consort Liu."

Yun Sixin frowned. "How are you involved with Consort Liu?"

Consort Liu was the husband of the Grand Princess. After becoming the Emperor’s son-in-law, he had relied on his status to look down on many people, and his reputation was terrible.

"This is a letter I wrote, imitating the handwriting of the Marquis of Xuanwu," Yun Chu said calmly. "To be honest with Father and Brother, the Marquis of Xuanwu once humiliated me. This is my way of ensuring the Marquis of Xuanwu’s household disappears from the capital."

The three Yun men were stunned.

Chu’er was a generous and tolerant person. Even when thoughtless servants bumped into her, she never took it to heart.

When some noblewomen in the capital gossiped behind her back, saying she wasn’t worthy of the title "Capital’s First Beauty," she had only laughed it off.

But now, Chu’er wanted to make the Marquis of Xuanwu’s household disappear.

What had the Marquis of Xuanwu done to make Chu’er take such drastic measures?

And what kind of humiliation was it...

The three men didn’t know how to ask, nor did they dare.

"Chu’er, why didn’t you tell me earlier?" Yun Ze took a deep breath. "Although I’m only a seventh-rank official, remember, I am the legitimate eldest son of the Yun family. Even if Father hadn’t returned to the capital, I still have the power to deal with the Marquis of Xuanwu’s household."

"I’ll cut him down!" General Yun stood up from the couch, grabbing a long sword. "Isn’t that man named Qin Mingheng? He’s really asking for it!"

"Grandfather, please sit back down." Yun Chu took the long sword from his hands. "If a letter can solve this, there’s no need for knives or swords. Don’t bring bad luck upon yourself."

In her past life, Consort Liu’s scandal in the palace would soon be exposed, and the Marquis of Xuanwu’s household would be taken down along with it.

chapters.title: Xie Shian Sends Flowers
chapters.content:
Night fell, and the lights were just lit.

Yun Chu and Xie Pin only then returned to the Xie residence.

On this day, Xie Pin had met many people at the Yun family whom she had never even been able to speak to before. She was increasingly convinced that her choice at Qing'an Temple back then had been the right one.

Even without a dowry, it didn’t matter. Once she became the Princess Consort of Anjing, she would have everything she needed.

The next morning, Xie Shian was still the first to come pay his respects.

There was a scar on his head, left from when Xie Shiyu had struck him the last time. If one didn’t look closely, it wasn’t noticeable.

"Huaide Academy will be on break in a few days," Yun Chu said, looking at him. "In September, you’ll start at the Imperial College. Once your father recovers, have him find a way to introduce you to the teachers there first."

Xie Shian had originally wanted to ask his maternal grandfather to take him to meet the Chancellor of the Imperial College, but since his mother had already spoken, he didn’t dare make the request.

He cupped his hands in respect and left the flower hall.

Soon after, the others came to pay their respects.

Many things had happened in the Xie family recently, and the mindset of the Xie family members had subtly changed.

Ling Yu stood quietly with Xie Shiyou, saying nothing beyond the usual pleasantries.

Tao Concubine brought Xie Shikang every day. He was a premature child, more difficult to care for than most, and even with the help of a wet nurse, her young body was nearly exhausted.

Jiang Concubine, on the other hand, was attending to the ailing Xie Jingyu day and night, and her complexion was terrible from the strain.

"If there’s nothing else, you may all withdraw," Yun Chu waved her hand, and the concubines bowed their heads and left.

She returned to her inner chamber, changed into a more comfortable outfit, and brought some toys that children would like, preparing to set off for the hot spring villa in the outskirts of the capital.

Just as she stepped out of the Shengju courtyard, Jiang Concubine returned and said, "Madam, the master says he has important matters to discuss with you and requests your presence."

Yun Chu frowned. "Tell him I’m not available."

Jiang Concubine lowered her voice. "Yesterday afternoon, the master sent me to Shengju several times, but since you weren’t back, he gave up. Madam, you should go see him."

Yun Chu estimated she would return around noon.

She pursed her lips and followed Jiang Concubine toward Xie Jingyu’s study courtyard.

As soon as she entered, she was hit by the pungent smell of medicinal herbs that permeated the entire courtyard.

"Master, Madam has arrived."

Jiang Concubine reported at the doorway, and after Yun Chu entered, she turned and went to check on the medicine stove in the courtyard.

Yun Chu stepped inside. "You sent Jiang Concubine to fetch me; what is it you wish to discuss?"

Xie Jingyu’s gaze fell on her clothes, which were different from usual. He asked, "Are you going out, Madam?"

"Mm, to the villa outside the city to have a look," Yun Chu replied casually. "It’s getting late. If there’s something, say it quickly."

As she spoke, she noticed Xie Jingyu’s face was terrifyingly pale. His skin had always been fair, but illness had turned it a ghastly white.

She also noticed that on the windowsill by the sickbed, at some point, a potted plant had appeared.

She approached and examined it carefully, then couldn’t help but curve her lips into a smile. She recognized this flower.

Some time ago, while searching for a contraceptive prescription for Xie Jingyu, she had come across this flower in a book. It could render a man sterile and had many side effects.

She asked, "Who sent this flower?"

"It was brought by An’ge a few days ago," Xie Jingyu said, reluctant to discuss the matter. After a pause, he continued, "Has my father-in-law been busy lately? Could you ask him to take An’ge to meet the Chancellor of the Imperial College?"

Yun Chu smiled.

Xie Shian was truly ruthless, even to his own biological father.

She said, "My father will be leaving the capital in a few days. I’m afraid he won’t have time to meet the Chancellor. An’ge is so outstanding; I’m sure he’ll catch the Chancellor’s eye without my father’s introduction. Husband, focus on recovering. Don’t worry about this."

With that, she turned and walked out.

Yun Chu, accompanied by Tingxue, set off for the outskirts of the capital. She dozed off in the carriage for a while and soon arrived at the villa’s entrance.

This was her third time here, and the scene before her was vastly different from her previous visits. The villa’s entrance looked brand new, with no trace of the twenty-plus years of abandonment. Inside, it was spacious and grand, with lush trees, artificial hills, flowing water, and ornate carvings, all arranged with a sense of layered beauty.

"Greetings, Madam Xie!"

Cheng Zhuangzhu, along with the villa’s servants, bowed to Yun Chu.

Apart from the steward and a housekeeper who were from Prince Pingxi’s residence, the rest were mostly people arranged by Manager Chen. Among them, Tingshuang and Jiu’er were Yun Chu’s trusted aides.

"Currently, we are still short a few accountants," Cheng Zhuangzhu said respectfully. "His Highness suggests that Madam Xie should arrange the accountants."

Accountants were the ones who managed money. Normally, both parties in a collaboration would try to fill the accounting positions with their own people to secure more benefits.

Prince Pingxi’s suggestion made it unclear whether he truly didn’t mind or if this was a test.

Yun Chu naturally wouldn’t agree outright. She said, "I can only arrange three. For the remaining two, I’ll have to trouble Steward Cheng to select a few trustworthy candidates."

Cheng Zhuangzhu bowed his head in agreement.

Just as she finished speaking, a carriage stopped at the villa’s entrance. Before it even came to a full stop, a little dumpling rushed in through the main gate.

" Aunt Yun, I missed you so much!"

Chu Hongyu scrambled up onto Yun Chu.

Yesterday, with that fellow Chu Zhenjiang watching, he hadn’t even been able to properly hug his mother.

Yun Chu had just lifted the little guy up when Chu Changsheng also rushed in. Yun Chu scooped her up with one arm, holding one child in each arm.

Fortunately, she had deliberately chosen a comfortable outfit; otherwise, it would have been inconvenient to hold two children. And fortunately, these two children were so thin and light; otherwise, she wouldn’t have been able to carry them. Though, she hoped they would gain some weight, become a little chubbier...

Seeing this scene, Cheng Zhuangzhu was stunned.

When had Madam Xie become so close with the two young masters of the prince’s residence?

He looked up and saw Prince Pingxi enter with a calm expression, his gaze falling on Madam Xie, a faint smile on his lips.

He was stunned once more.

As an old servant of the Yin family, he had always handled affairs for the prince and frequently interacted with him. He could say that he had never seen the prince smile like this before.

In fact, he had only ever seen the prince give cold smiles. A peaceful smile like this was something he had never witnessed.

"Yu’er, get down," Chu Yi said in a calm voice. "You’re a boy. It’s improper to be carried by Madam Xie."

The woman before him was holding two children, her waist bent, clearly struggling.

Chu Hongyu refused to budge.

Chu Yi’s expression darkened, his gaze clearly threatening.

The little guy knew that if he didn’t obey, his father wouldn’t take him out again next time.

He had no choice but to climb down from Yun Chu with a pitiful look.

Yun Chu, still holding the quiet little girl, saluted Chu Yi. "Greetings, Your Highness."

Chu Yi waved his hand. "Since we are jointly managing this villa, it would be too formal for Madam Xie to greet me with a salute."

Yun Chu increasingly felt that this prince, whom everyone feared, was actually quite approachable...

---

chapters.title: The Two Surnames
chapters.content:
The group walked inward.

Yun Chu led the children at the front, with Chu Yi following a step behind, and more than a dozen servants trailing after.

Soon, they reached the hot spring area. Originally a natural spring, it had now been fully developed into bath pools, some open-air public pools, others private and partitioned.

"There are thirty-six pools in total, large and small," Chu Yi said. "Each needs a name. I’m not skilled in such matters, so I’ll have to trouble Madam Xie."

Though Yun Chu’s martial skills were not exceptional, her literary talents were among the best in the Yun family. She nodded in agreement.

As they walked along, they arrived at the entrance of a small courtyard. The gate was flanked by lush flowers and plants, blooming vibrantly in the summer heat.

Inside, various flowers were in full bloom, and the path was embedded among the flower beds, as if leading into a secret garden. It lifted everyone’s spirits.

"Madam Xie, this courtyard was personally designed by our prince," Cheng Zhuangzhu said from the side. "Please take a look and see if there’s anything that needs improvement."

The entire villa had many individual courtyards, each equipped with separate bath pools for men and women. Most of the courtyards were similar in design, but this one was particularly unique. Not only was it filled with rare and exotic flowers, but the edge of the pool was inlaid with multicolored stones that looked like gemstones, dazzling to the eye.

Yun Chu assumed this was a hot spring pool that Prince Pingxi had specially built for Consort Yin.

She was about to speak when Chu Hongyu exclaimed, "Wow, there are so many crabapple trees planted here! So that’s what Father meant when he asked me what kind of flowers Aunt Yun likes!"

The corners of the courtyard walls were lined with crabapple trees, identical to those in the Shengju courtyard where Yun Chu lived.

She was somewhat stunned. Could it be that this pool...

"Madam Xie is the mistress of the hot spring villa. Naturally, the most unique pool belongs to her," Chu Yi said, his expression unreadable. "There is still an empty plot here. Whatever flowers Madam Xie likes, I will have them brought and planted."

Yun Chu pressed her lips together.

In her first year of marriage to the Xie family, she had planted a large patch of crabapple trees in Shengju. She used to love crabapple blossoms, but at some point, she had begun to feel a growing aversion to them.

She wanted to escape the crabapple trees, just as she wanted to escape the Xie family.

After a moment of silence, she said, "Move these crabapple trees to another courtyard. Here, plant orchids or jasmine, either is fine. Tingshuang, you handle this."

How could she trouble His Highness with such a trivial matter?

Tingshuang was standing behind her and, upon hearing the instruction, immediately stepped forward. "Yes, Madam."

Chu Yi paused but said nothing more.

"Changsheng, come here quickly! The water is so warm and comfortable!" Chu Hongyu, unable to resist, dipped his little hand into the pool and eagerly called to his sister. The little girl trotted over.

The two children sat at the edge of the hot spring, took off their shoes, and dipped their four tiny, fair feet into the water, splashing each other.

"Yu’er, don’t do that," Yun Chu said gently. "Changsheng is frail. If her clothes get wet, she’ll catch a cold."

The little boy’s eyes darted around, and he shifted his small bottom to a different spot. Bending over, he cupped some water and splashed it toward Chu Yi.

The little girl followed her brother’s example, happily splashing water from the pool, most of which landed on Chu Yi.

Chu Yi’s entire outfit was thoroughly soaked.

His face darkened.

His attendant, standing nearby, silently took a step back.

That morning, His Highness had spent a good quarter of an hour selecting this particular set of clothes. Though the attendant couldn’t tell the difference between this and any other set, His Highness had meticulously chosen it. And now, it was completely ruined by the young master...

"Changsheng, run! Father is going to hit someone!" Chu Hongyu grabbed his sister’s hand and leaped out of the pool. Barefoot, they dashed outside.

A large group of servants rushed after them.

"Young Master, wait! Slow down!"

"Princess, don’t run barefoot. Let this old servant help you with your shoes..."

In an instant, the crowd dispersed, leaving only Yun Chu, Chu Yi, and the maids attending to Yun Chu.

Chu Yi cleared his throat. "Madam Xie, don’t misunderstand. I rarely hit children."

Yun Chu nodded. "Mm, I know."

Chu Yi felt that he was only making things worse.

Before he could say more, Yun Chu said, "Your Highness, your clothes are wet. You should change first."

Chu Yi had no choice but to go change.

Yun Chu continued to admire the small courtyard. It was clear that a lot of effort had gone into it, and she couldn’t find a single flaw.

She stepped into the house. The main room had a hall and an inner chamber, with side rooms on either side and a study. Though small, it had everything one could need.

She sat at the desk and had Tingfeng grind ink, then began writing names for the various pools. This task was effortless for her...

As she wrote, the two children ran over after their romp. "Aunt Yun, what does this character mean? And this one?"

Chu Hongyu asked curiously, and Yun Chu patiently taught him the characters without the slightest impatience. The little girl also blinked her big eyes, listening intently.

"Yu’er, what do you think would be a good name for this hot spring villa?" Yun Chu asked.

She had already come up with names for all the pools, but the villa itself still needed one. This was truly a challenging task.

Chu Hongyu swung his short legs, pondering deeply for a long while. "How about 'Above Chu and Yun'? 'Chu Yun' refers to the clouds in the sky. Soaking in the hot spring would be like soaking in the clouds, so comfortable, so enjoyable. It’s sure to attract many people."

"Above Chu and Yun..." Yun Chu repeated the name a few times, a smile appearing on her face. "That’s actually quite good."

"I also think the name works," Chu Yi, now in fresh clothes, walked in and looked at the paper on the desk. "Madam Xie’s handwriting is elegant yet bold and powerful. Madam Xie, why not write these four characters? I’ll have them framed as the villa’s signboard."

Chu Hongyu clapped his hands. "Yes, yes! Aunt Yun, you write it!"

He was truly clever. His surname and his mother’s surname combined made "Above Chu and Yun." He hadn’t expected both his mother and father to approve.

The little boy leaned over the desk, and seeing "Chu" and "Yun" written side by side, his heart swelled with joy.

After Yun Chu wrote the four characters, she belatedly realized that this was a combination of her surname and Prince Pingxi’s...

She looked at the man before her. His expression was as calm as ever, as if he hadn’t noticed anything unusual.

If she were to point it out as inappropriate, it would only make her seem overly sensitive.

At that moment, Cheng Zhuangzhu, who had been waiting at the door, entered and took the characters away, immediately arranging for the best craftsman to frame them as a sign.

Yun Chu’s lips parted slightly, then closed again.

She took out the names she had prepared for the pools and showed them to Chu Yi one by one.

Chu Yi read them carefully. "Everyone says Madam Xie is exceptionally beautiful, hence the title of the capital’s most beautiful woman. But in my view, Madam Xie deserves the title of the capital’s most talented woman."

Yun Chu: "..."

That was a bit of an exaggeration.

Chu Hongyu tugged at Chu Yi’s sleeve. "Father, since Aunt Yun is so amazing, can she be my teacher?"

Yun Chu laughed. "Yu’er, don’t talk like a child."

The prince’s residence would never hire a married woman as a teacher, and she, as a married woman, could never take up a teaching position there.

Just as they were speaking, Cheng Zhuangzhu approached. "Your Highness, Madam Xie, lunch is ready. Please proceed to the flower hall to dine."

Yun Chu hadn’t planned to stay for the meal, but the two children, one on each side, tugged at her, their big eyes full of hope, making it impossible for her to refuse. She had no choice but to follow them to the flower hall.

chapters.title: Accidentally Eating Wild Mushrooms
chapters.content:
The flower hall on the manor was a true flower hall.

Surrounded by flowers of all colors, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple, it offered an ultimate sensory delight.

The hall was lit with some kind of incense, probably to repel mosquitoes, as not a single one could be seen.

"Madam Xie." Chu Yi gestured for her to proceed. "I still have some matters to attend to. I’m afraid I must trouble Madam Xie to dine with the two children first."

Zhuang Zhuangzhu silently lowered his gaze.

Before the Prince arrived at the manor, he had already cleared his schedule. There was truly nothing urgent to handle now.

For the sake of Madam Xie’s reputation, the Prince had come up with such an excuse.

Their Prince was not a meticulous man, yet at this moment, he had even considered such a small etiquette. It was truly rare.

He always felt that not only the young prince and the young princess treated Madam Xie specially, but even the Prince seemed to regard her differently in his heart.

Chu Yi turned and left the flower hall.

The moment he was gone, Yun Chu let out a sigh of relief.

The saying "men and women should not sit together after the age of seven" didn’t strictly mean seven, but rather that after children became self-aware, women should avoid dining at the same table as unrelated men.

From a young age, she had been taught to keep her distance from men. Because of these two children, she and Prince Pingxi had grown too close, though their daily interactions still barely stayed within the bounds of propriety.

Although she had agreed to stay and dine with Yu Ge at the manor, she had thought she would just stand to the side and chat with Yu Ge and Changsheng...

Now that Prince Pingxi had left, she no longer had to worry about those formalities.

She took a seat at the dining table.

The two children each had their own dedicated chefs preparing their meals, with a wet nurse and a maid standing behind each of them. There was practically nothing for her to do.

"Madam Xie, all the dishes on this table are made from common ingredients found on the manor," Zhuang Zhuangzhu respectfully explained. "This is a wild vegetable, its name isn’t very pleasant, but it has a sweet and refreshing taste. This is wild pheasant from the manor; the meat is exceptionally tender and delicious. The fish was also caught from the manor’s lake. The physician says that because the fish are affected by the hot spring water, eating them is beneficial to one’s health..."

Yun Chu was trying wild game for the first time, and just as Zhuang Zhuangzhu had said, the flavors were indeed sweet and delicious. She ate with great relish.

As she ate, she suddenly felt an itch on her arm. She put down her chopsticks and rolled up her sleeve, only to see her arm covered in dense red spots.

Before she could think much about it, she lost consciousness and slumped forward from her chair.

Fortunately, Tingshuang and Tingfeng were standing right behind her and quickly caught her.

" Aunt Yun!"

Chu Hongyu let out a terrified scream and rushed forward.

"Madam!" Tingfeng was also badly startled. "Madam, what’s wrong with you? Madam!"

In that instant, countless red bumps appeared on Yun Chu’s neck and face.

Tingshuang’s expression changed. "Zhuang Zhuangzhu, were there mushrooms in the dishes?"

Zhuang Zhuangzhu hurriedly replied, "There are many wild mushrooms on the manor’s low hills. The head chef specially used wild mushrooms to make a vegetable dish with infused oil. Could it be that Madam Xie cannot eat mushrooms?"

Tingshuang recalled that more than a decade ago, when Madam was around four or five years old, she had eaten wild mushrooms and broken out in red bumps all over her body. Not only on her skin, but also in her mouth, and her throat had swollen shut, nearly causing her to suffocate...

"Quickly, go and invite Physician Bi!" Chu Yi had appeared at some point, his voice cold as he ordered, "Be quick about it!"

Physician Bi was the dedicated physician for his prince’s residence, responsible for the health of the two children all these years.

He clearly remembered that when Changsheng was a little over a year old, she had suddenly broken out in a rash all over her body and fallen into a coma. It was Physician Bi who had saved her.

Later, they found out that it was because the wet nurse had eaten mushrooms that day, and Changsheng had drunk the wet nurse’s milk, causing her to develop a mushroom rash.

He didn’t know if Madam Xie was in the same situation, but for now, he could only send for Physician Bi first.

He saw Yun Chu slumped in the arms of Tingshuang and Tingfeng. Without thinking, he walked over and bent down, preparing to lift her horizontally into his arms.

As he got closer, he clearly caught the unique fragrance that belonged to her.

His fingers hesitated, and he took a few steps back. In a calm voice, he ordered, "You two, help Madam Xie to the inner room."

The wet nurse, who was specifically assigned to the two children, quickly stepped forward to help Tingshuang and Tingfeng. They supported Yun Chu as they walked from the flower hall to the courtyard and placed her on a bed.

"Your Highness, this servant deserves ten thousand deaths!" Zhuang Zhuangzhu dropped to his knees with a thud, then raised his hand and slapped himself twice across the face.

Having served Chu Yi for many years, how could he not understand the special place Madam Xie held in the Prince’s heart? And yet, he had caused Madam Xie to fall into a coma.

If anything happened to Madam Xie, he wouldn’t be able to compensate with his life.

His actions terrified Chu Hongyu into wailing loudly. "Father, is Aunt Yun going to die? No, I don’t want that..."

Chu Changsheng’s large eyes filled with tears, which fell silently as she cried without a sound.

Chu Yi, who had been about to lose his temper, suppressed his anger and said coldly, "If I ever see wild mushrooms on this manor again, you can forget about keeping your head on your shoulders."

Zhuang Zhuangzhu wiped the sweat from his forehead. "Yes, Your Highness!"

Chu Yi picked up his daughter. "Changsheng, be good. Don’t cry. Father will take you to see Aunt Yun."

Chu Hongyu sniffled as he followed behind, and the three of them entered the courtyard where Yun Chu was resting. Jiu Er stood guard at the gate, while Tingfeng and Tingshuang attended to her inside.

Chu Hongyu wiped his tears and asked in a choked voice, "Sister Jiu Er, how is Aunt Yun?"

He was too afraid to go in. He was afraid he wouldn’t be able to hold back his sobs, afraid that he would scare his sister into crying as well.

Jiu Er shook her head. "In response to the young prince, Madam is still unconscious."

Just as she spoke, Tingshuang’s delighted voice came from inside. "Madam, you’re awake!"

Yun Chu slowly opened her eyes.

She felt as if her throat was blocked by something, making it difficult to speak. Though uncomfortable, there was no feeling of suffocation.

She vaguely remembered that when she was four or five years old, she had also eaten wild mushrooms and then slept for three days and three nights. Perhaps because she was older now, her body’s resistance to wild mushrooms had strengthened somewhat, otherwise she wouldn’t have woken up so quickly.

" Aunt Yun, it’s really great that you’re okay!"

Chu Hongyu rushed in without hesitation, grabbing Yun Chu’s hand, and still couldn’t help but cry quietly.

He had finally found a mother he liked, but they hadn’t even had the chance to live together yet. He couldn’t bear the thought of losing her...

Chu Changsheng wriggled out of Chu Yi’s arms and took a step forward, but she didn’t notice the door sill and nearly fell flat on her face.

Chu Yi simply scooped his daughter up and carried her inside. However, he only stood at the doorway and did not go any further. The little girl went around the screen and threw herself onto Yun Chu, not minding the red rashes on her face at all, and clung to her affectionately.

Through the screen, Chu Yi faintly saw the two children leaning against Yun Chu.

At that moment, he wondered: If she had never married, would he have been able to walk past the screen to her side?

But it seemed that wouldn’t work either. An unmarried woman had even stricter rules about interactions between men and women. He might not even have been able to see her.

Whether she was married or not, he had no right to stand by her bedside.

Unless... he was her husband.

This thought, once it appeared, spread rapidly like weeds through his heart.

---

chapters.title: I Am Not a Boy
chapters.content:
Physician Bi arrived quickly.

Carrying his medical case, he hurried into the inner room where Yun Chu was. He took out a thread and placed it on Yun Chu’s pulse.

"Blood deficiency leading to wind, to be avoided at times." Physician Bi quickly came to a conclusion. "Since she has eaten wild mushrooms, she should avoid them in the future. This old man will prescribe two formulas: one to nourish the blood, and another to relieve the itching on the skin."

The physician picked up a brush and soon wrote out two prescriptions, which Jiu Er took and quickly had someone from the manor who could ride a horse go to the pharmacy to fill them.

"This old man has practiced medicine for more than thirty years, and Madam Xie is only the second person I’ve encountered who faints and breaks out in rashes after eating wild mushrooms." Physician Bi spoke up. "The first was the young princess."

Yun Chu’s heart skipped a beat, her face filled with disbelief.

Could it be that little Changsheng also couldn’t eat wild mushrooms?

This was too much of a coincidence.

"Madam Xie can take a hot spring bath later to quickly eliminate these rashes." Physician Bi looked at Chu Yi, who was standing to the side. "Since the young princess is also at the manor, perhaps tomorrow we can try acupuncture on her in the hot spring water to see what therapeutic effects it might have."

Upon hearing this, Chu Changsheng’s body trembled involuntarily. She shrank into Yun Chu’s arms, her entire body shaking uncontrollably.

Chu Hongyu sniffled and clenched his small fists. "Physician Bi is a bad man! He always gives my sister acupuncture. All the needle marks on my sister’s body are from him. Bad man! A terrible bad man!"

Physician Bi rubbed his nose.

He had been living with the young prince and princess for more than three years. Whenever the two young masters saw him, they would hide as if they had seen some kind of monstrous beast.

But by now, he was used to it.

However, a gentle female voice suddenly spoke up: "Yu Ge, Physician Bi performs acupuncture on Changsheng to help regulate her body. You wouldn’t want to see your sister so weak that she can’t even hold a cat, would you?"

Her voice was a little hoarse, but it was gentle and carried a sense of strength.

Chu Hongyu, of course, understood this reasoning. But every time his sister received acupuncture, she would become even more silent afterward, to the point where even he, her own brother, couldn’t get close to her.

He really felt too much heartache for Changsheng, not that he deliberately disliked Physician Bi.

He pursed his lips, let go of Yun Chu’s hand, walked around the screen, and went up to Physician Bi. Lifting his head, he said, "Physician Bi, I’m sorry. I shouldn’t have called you a terrible bad man. Can you forgive me?"

Physician Bi was so shocked that his eyes nearly popped out of their sockets.

In the past, when the young prince called him a terrible bad man, the Prince had not intervened, but the young prince simply didn’t listen to the Prince.

Yet just now, with a single sentence from Madam Xie, the young prince had come to apologize on his own.

This was like the sun rising in the west.

He stroked his beard and said, "If the young prince can keep the princess company and talk to her to distract her a little while this old man performs acupuncture, then this old man will forgive the young prince."

Chu Hongyu nodded. "I would have done that even if Physician Bi hadn’t said so."

Physician Bi burst into laughter and followed Chu Yi outside.

"Old Bi." Chu Yi spoke slowly. "Are there many people in this world who faint and break out in rashes after eating wild mushrooms?"

Physician Bi shook his head. "Not many. In my entire life, I’ve only seen two: the young princess and Madam Xie... Most people with such symptoms cannot eat shellfish, crabs, peanuts, and other allergenic foods. Wild mushrooms are indeed rare."

Something flickered in Chu Yi’s mind, but he couldn’t grasp it.

He had someone escort Physician Bi to the guest courtyard of the manor, then turned and ordered the servant women of the small courtyard, "You few, prepare everything. Attend to Madam Xie for her hot spring bath."

The servant women cupped their hands and accepted the order. "Yes, Your Highness."

After the servants returned with the medicine, it was decocted, and Yun Chu drank it. The swelling and pain in her throat subsided significantly, but her body was still covered in dense red rashes.

She got up, preparing to soak in the hot spring.

Chu Hongyu clung to her. "Aunt Yun, can I soak with you? Please..."

Before Yun Chu could respond, Chu Yi’s voice came from outside. "Chu Hongyu, what have I told you? Men and women should not touch!"

"I’m not a boy, I’m a girl!" Chu Hongyu had a thick face. "Aunt Yun, just pretend I’m a girl, okay? I really want to soak in the hot spring with you."

Yun Chu: ...

For a moment, she truly didn’t know what to say.

But after all, he was only a four-year-old child, not yet at the age where strict gender separation was observed.

She had people prepare clothes, dressed the two little ones in special hot spring attire, and changed into her own clothes. Then, holding the hands of the two children, she entered the hot spring pool together.

Chu Yi’s face was as dark as the bottom of a pot.

Although he couldn’t see that side, he could hear the sounds. The boy’s laughter had even startled the birds from the trees.

Madam Xie really spoiled that child too much...

"Your Highness!" At this moment, his attendant entered and reported, "Concubine Yin requests that Your Highness enter the palace to discuss an important matter!"

Chu Yi rubbed his fingers together.

The important matter his mother spoke of was likely about him taking a princess consort.

Although he had previously agreed to take a princess consort, Yu Ge was strongly against it and had even fallen into the water because of it.

He spoke, "Go tell the palace maid who delivered the message that I already have someone in mind. Ask my mother to stop worrying about this matter."

The attendant’s eyes widened in shock.

His Highness had someone in mind?

He spent every day with His Highness, so why didn’t he know?

But His Highness had never had any woman around him! How could he suddenly have someone in mind?

Wait...

The attendant’s gaze turned toward the direction of the hot spring pool. Although he couldn’t see that side, he could hear the young prince repeatedly calling out "Aunt Yun."

Could it be... Madam Xie?

But Madam Xie was already married, with a husband, sons, and daughters!

"Still standing there in a daze for what!"

Chu Yi barked coldly.

The attendant snapped out of his thoughts and quickly left to carry out the task.

Chu Yi’s expression was dark.

Someone in mind... Who was the someone in mind?

Fifteen years ago, as General Yun set out on his campaign, she had stood on the city wall to see off Yun’s army.

At that time, she was only ten years old. He hadn’t dared to think anything, and any small feelings he had were ruthlessly strangled in their cradle by his own hands.

If he had known that five years after the campaign, he would be drinking her wedding wine, would he still have hidden those feelings?

Chu Yi gave a bitter laugh.

Even if the Yun family had known his feelings, it wouldn’t have mattered.

The Yun family would never allow a Yun daughter to marry a prince, and the Emperor would never bestow a marriage between him and her.

Those hidden feelings of his had long been buried by the river of time... But then the two children had inexplicably become attached to her...

Every meeting, every conversation, every moment of being so close to her was like a pot of water poured onto his heart. The seeds that had long been dead began to slowly sprout, growing small green leaves...

But he couldn’t!

He couldn’t ruin her.

Chu Yi turned and walked out of the small courtyard.

Yun Chu and the two children soaked in the hot spring pool. Although it was the middle of summer, the area was surrounded by plants and trees, and ice blocks had been placed around, so there was no oppressive heat.

Chu Hongyu, like a loach, darted around in the hot spring pool, occasionally bursting into laughter. His laughter infected Chu Changsheng, and the little girl also revealed a sweet smile.

chapters.title: Changsheng Spoke
chapters.content:
After soaking in the hot spring for a while, Yun Chu felt a slight feverishness and noticed that the red rashes on her body had indeed faded significantly.

She stood up and sat on a rock by the pool, smiling as she said, "Changsheng, look, there are so many flowers over there. Auntie wants one red flower, three blue flowers, and five yellow flowers. Can you help pick them for me?"

"I will, I will!" Chu Hongyu eagerly tried to go over.

Yun Chu shook her head at him.

Changsheng wasn’t unable to speak; rather, she refused to communicate with the outside world for some reason.

The physician could treat her body, but it was difficult to eliminate her resistance to this world.

Since Yun Chu could enter Changsheng’s world, perhaps she could also lead the little girl out of that small world.

The little girl hesitated for a moment, glanced at Yun Chu, then took some time to understand the meaning of her words. She walked along the edge of the pool to the other side.

There were flowers of various colors blooming there. The little girl searched and found the colors Yun Chu wanted. She picked them, counted them, and then walked back to hand them to Yun Chu.

"Wow, Changsheng, you’re amazing!" Yun Chu picked her up and placed her on her lap. "Auntie loves them so much. Thank you, Changsheng!"

The little girl pressed her lips together, smiling shyly.

"Changsheng, look, this is a red flower. Red—" Yun Chu taught her to open her mouth. "You say it with Auntie: *Hong*..."

The little girl parted her lips but made no sound.

Yun Chu thought that perhaps the pronunciation was too difficult. Babies learning to speak usually started with "father" and "mother."

She changed her approach and patiently said, "Come on, Changsheng, say it with Auntie: *Die*..."

"Yun Chu, let me teach my sister." Chu Hongyu crawled over, pointing at Yun Chu. "Changsheng, look, *Niang*, this is our *Niang*."

Yun Chu was about to correct him.

It had been so hard to get this little rascal to call her "Auntie," and now he was leading the little girl astray.

Before she could speak, she heard a soft, tender voice: "*Niang*..."

The voice was soft and sweet, like a piece of candy coated in milk, melting one’s heart.

Yun Chu’s face was filled with disbelief. "Changsheng, was that you speaking just now?"

"Yes, yes, yes! It was my sister’s voice!" Chu Hongyu’s face was full of joy. "Quick, Changsheng, say it again!"

The little girl looked at the two people in front of her, both gazing at her expectantly. Her eyes curved like crescent moons as she clearly spoke this time: "*Niang*."

"Heavens, my sister really can talk!" Chu Hongyu jumped three feet high and quickly rushed out of the pool. "Father King, Father King! My sister can talk. Come quickly, my sister really can talk!"

The wet nurses guarding the door were all in disbelief. Could the little princess really speak?

They didn’t bother to verify and turned to find Chu Yi.

By the time Chu Yi arrived, Yun Chu had already changed clothes for the little girl. She was all smiles. "Changsheng, call your father..."

"*Die*..." the little girl timidly called out.

Just now, Yu Ge’er had taught her to say *Niang*, and Yun Chu had taught her to say *Die*.

Chu Yi’s heart pounded violently in his chest, and his hands trembled uncontrollably. He stretched out his arms. "Changsheng, come, let Father hold you."

The little girl clung to Yun Chu’s neck and refused to let go.

Yun Chu softly said, "Changsheng, that is your father. He is the one who has always loved and protected you. He is the person in this world who loves you the most."

The little girl lifted her head and slowly turned to look at Chu Yi. Only then did she slowly extend her hand.

Chu Yi’s face, like a melting glacier, bloomed instantly. He took his daughter into his arms, his voice as gentle as could be. "Changsheng, can you call me *Die* again?"

Chu Changsheng softly called out, "*Die*."

"Father King, look! My sister really can talk!" Chu Hongyu was as happy as a monkey, jumping around. "My sister doesn’t just know how to call *Die*; she also knows how to call *Niang*. Changsheng, call it for Father King to hear!"

Chu Changsheng immediately obeyed, looking at Yun Chu and sweetly calling out, "*Niang*!"

One call of *Die* and one of *Niang*, strung together, gave Yun Chu a strange feeling.

Standing together with the father and son of the Prince of Pingxi’s residence, that strange feeling became obvious... It was as if they were a family of four...

She quickly banished this absurd thought from her mind and said, "Your Highness, it’s getting late. I should go back now."

"Don’t go, Auntie!" Chu Hongyu hugged her leg tightly. "Changsheng has acupuncture treatment tomorrow, and each session takes half an hour. Auntie, won’t you stay and keep Changsheng company?"

Yun Chu’s heart softened.

She realized that she simply couldn’t resist these two children.

"Changsheng, tell Auntie to stay!" Chu Hongyu quickly called his sister for help.

The day was too short. His happiness had just begun, and now it was about to end.

How he wished to live carefree days with his mother, his sister, and, reluctantly, his father in this estate...

Chu Changsheng slid down from Chu Yi and tugged at Yun Chu’s hand. "*Niang... Niang...*"

She repeatedly called out only this word, her big eyes full of expectation, hoping Yun Chu would not leave, hoping she would stay with her.

Yun Chu slightly turned her head. "Tingfeng, go back to the Xie residence and tell them that there are still some matters to handle at the estate, so I won’t be returning tonight."

Tingfeng nodded and left with the coachman.

When they returned to the Xie residence, it was already evening. Tingfeng went to the courtyard where Xie Jingyu stayed. A maidservant was boiling medicine in the courtyard, and Tingyu was attending to him inside.

Seeing Tingyu dutifully serving Xie Jingyu his meal, Tingfeng’s eyes revealed mockery. However, she lowered her head, hiding the emotions in her eyes, and said, "Master, the mistress still has unfinished business at the estate and will return tomorrow."

Tingyu’s fingers paused. "Is the mistress so busy with matters at the estate?"

As far as she knew, the mistress’s dowry was managed by Steward Chen. He presented the account books to the mistress for review every season. The mistress rarely went to the estate in person to handle matters. How could she be so busy that she wouldn’t return until nightfall?

"Yan Concubine doesn’t need to manage the dowry, so naturally, she doesn’t know how busy the mistress is." Tingfeng lowered her gaze. "Master, this servant must return to the estate to attend to the mistress. I take my leave."

She walked out with her head down.

Tingyu fed Xie Jingyu a bite of food and casually said, "Master is so ill, yet the mistress still has the mind to deal with outside matters... Just now, Tingfeng didn’t even ask about Master’s condition..."

Xie Jingyu’s expression was very grim.

Yes, he was so ill that he couldn’t even get out of bed and needed someone to feed him. Yet Yun Chu, for the sake of a little business, didn’t return home all night.

If the silver she earned was used for the Xie family, he wouldn’t say anything. But now, she didn’t even manage her sister’s dowry, and she ignored all the places in the Xie residence that needed money... What was the point of earning so much silver?

---

chapters.title: Giving You a Bouquet
chapters.content:
Night fell.

The sky was dotted with countless stars, and the vast starry expanse made one’s heart feel open and free.

Yun Chu sat in the courtyard, moonlight spilling over her shoulders.

At this moment, her mood was very peaceful. She didn’t need to think about anything, no schemes, no plans, no darkness. She could just quietly admire the moon and stars.

Outside the small courtyard, Chu Hongyu and Chu Changsheng were whispering to each other. The two little ones, under the moonlight, stepped into the flower bushes.

The old wet nurse was at her wit’s end. "Oh, little ancestors, don’t go so deep. There might be snakes at night. Be careful..."

Chu Hongyu didn’t care about that. He pulled his sister along to pick many, many flowers of various colors, then had the old wet nurse tie them together with a rope.

He held the bouquet and slipped into Chu Yi’s courtyard.

This courtyard was adjacent to Yun Chu’s, separated by a tall wall.

"Father King!"

Chu Yi, who had been reading official documents, looked up and saw his son and daughter running in.

He put down his brush, picked up the little girl, and placed her on his lap. "Changsheng, call me *Die*."

Chu Changsheng didn’t call him *Die*. Instead, she forcefully stuffed the large bouquet into his arms and softly said, "Give... give... *Niang*..."

Chu Yi didn’t understand and didn’t know what it meant.

"Father King, Auntie Yun really likes flowers." Chu Hongyu said with a smile. "You take these flowers and give them to Auntie Yun, okay?"

Chu Yi frowned. "Nonsense."

"Father King, just give them to her, give them!" Chu Hongyu shook his arm. "It was Auntie Yun who taught my sister to call *Die*. Shouldn’t you thank Auntie Yun?"

Chu Yi: "..."

He should express his gratitude, but giving flowers was such a trivial way to do so.

In the world of adults, interests came first. A bouquet of flowers was far too light a gesture.

Seeing that Chu Yi wasn’t speaking, the little one instantly turned upset. "Father King, you’re too much! You won’t even grant this small request. Humph! From now on, Changsheng won’t call you *Die* anymore! Changsheng, let’s go!"

"Wait." Chu Yi pinched the space between his brows. "Leave the flowers."

Chu Hongyu huffed through his nose. "I don’t want you to give them anymore. I’ll go find Uncle Cheng Xu!"

Cheng Xu was the son of the estate’s steward and also Chu Yi’s most capable guard. He was only twenty years old, in the prime of his youth.

Chu Yi stood up directly, took the bouquet from Chu Hongyu’s hands, and strode out. He quickly reached the entrance of Yun Chu’s courtyard.

As he arrived, his steps faltered.

It was because of her that Changsheng had started to learn to speak. He had originally planned to give estates, shops, silver, or jade... but he had never thought of giving flowers.

Under the moonlight and starlight, this bouquet of unnamed flowers was dazzling and beautiful, yet they still paled in comparison to her appearance.

He didn’t know how to present this bouquet.

"Father King, if you don’t want to give them, then don’t!" Chu Hongyu said, hands on his hips. "I’ll have Uncle Cheng Xu give them instead!"

Cheng Xu, standing in the night: "..."

Did this have anything to do with him? Couldn’t he just quietly be invisible?

Yun Chu, sitting in the courtyard, heard Chu Hongyu’s voice and called out, "Yu Ge’er, what are you doing at the door? Come in with Changsheng."

She was a little puzzled. The two children hadn’t come to pester her.

"Auntie Yun, I have something to do. I’ll come later!"

Chu Hongyu gave his old father a hard push, then pulled his sister along and ran off.

Chu Yi finally stepped over the courtyard’s threshold, walked around the wall, and entered. Tingshuang and Jiu Er were standing guard there. They greeted him, "Greetings, Your Highness."

Yun Chu, who had been casually reclining on a rattan chair, stood up immediately upon hearing the two maids’ greetings. She slightly bent her knees. "Your Highness."

She looked up and saw the man in front of her holding a large bouquet of flowers.

The flowers looked familiar, as if they were from the flower bushes at the courtyard entrance. In the middle of the night, had the Prince of Pingxi gone to pick flowers?

"Yu Ge’er said you like flowers." Chu Yi forced the words out.

Once he started speaking, the rest of the words didn’t seem so hard to say.

"Thank you for being willing to stay at the estate for the two children, and thank you for your patience in teaching them. Meeting you is the greatest blessing in the children’s lives. This bouquet is for Madam Xie. I hope Madam Xie will have smooth sailing in all things."

Yun Chu raised her hand and accepted the flowers. The fragrant scent filled her nose, and this night seemed even more beautiful.

A smile appeared in her eyes. "I also wish Your Highness all the best."

Chu Yi looked at her crescent-moon-like eyes. The clear depths held fragments of moonlight and starlight, causing his heartbeat to inexplicably skip a beat.

The seed that had sprouted in his heart, with only two tender leaves, under her gaze, seemed to grow into a towering tree in a short moment, lush and flourishing, almost bursting from his chest.

At this moment, countless fireflies took to the sky.

In the forest, among the grass and trees, and on the shoulders of the two, the fireflies dragged their bright little lanterns, flying around.

"So beautiful." Yun Chu couldn’t help but sigh. "The last time I saw fireflies was when I was a child. I went fishing in the suburbs with my father, but he didn’t catch a single fish. Before we knew it, it was dark, and we got lost on our way back. I was so scared I cried... To comfort me, my father caught many fireflies."

As she spoke, she couldn’t help but laugh.

That night, accompanied by the fireflies, she and her father had crossed half a mountain but still couldn’t find the way down. In the end, her eldest brother came to take them home.

The exhaustion and panic of that night had long been forgotten. The memory of those fireflies had grown brighter and brighter over time, becoming precious.

It had been a unique night.

She looked into the distance and saw Chu Hongyu and Changsheng chasing fireflies... This was also a unique night.

Chu Yi turned his head to look at her and unconsciously said, "The last time I saw fireflies was about five years ago. I returned to the capital with your father after a campaign. When we were near the capital, we saw some. Your father said he wanted to catch some to give to you as part of your dowry. But it was early spring, and there were too few fireflies, so it didn’t happen... The day your father and I arrived in the capital was the day of your wedding. Your father didn’t go to the palace to report for duty first. Instead, he took me to your Yun family residence. I was fortunate enough to have a drink at your wedding banquet."

At the mention of her wedding day, the smile on Yun Chu’s face suddenly disappeared.

Her life had been completely ruined starting from that night...

Chu Yi keenly noticed the change in her mood and immediately changed the subject. "Madam Xie gave Yu Ge’er and Changsheng longevity locks. I also had someone prepare a small gift to return to Madam Xie. I hope Madam Xie won’t refuse."

Yun Chu was thinking of a reason to decline when she saw Chu Yi’s attendant, Cheng Xu, bring over a tray. On it was a piece of jade the size of an adult’s palm.

This was an uncarved piece of raw jade. The red stone glowed translucently under the moonlight.

"This isn’t anything worthy of presentation." Chu Yi said, "Like a stubborn stone by the road or a flower in the woods, it only represents my gratitude to Madam Xie. Please accept it, Madam Xie."

"Just take it, Auntie Yun!"

Chu Hongyu and Chu Changsheng appeared from nowhere. The two of them worked together to pick up the red stone and stuffed it into Yun Chu’s arms.

With things having come to this, Yun Chu knew that if she continued to refuse, she would seem overly pretentious. She smiled and said, "I’ll have this jade made into pendants for Yu Ge’er and Changsheng, one each. How about that?"

Chu Hongyu pouted. "No way! This is what Father King gave you. How can you give it to me and my sister?"

Chu Yi felt a sense of relief. This little guy had finally shown some understanding.

"Should make three pendants: one for me, one for my sister, and one for Auntie Yun!" Chu Hongyu grinned, showing his white teeth. "If there’s any left, then make one for Father King."

Chu Yi: "..."

Thank you, kid. He only deserved the leftovers.

chapters.title: Investigating the Xie Family
chapters.content:
The night was long and endless.

Yun Chu slept deeply.

Feeling a slight itch on her nose, she let out a big sneeze and opened her eyes.

Before her were two magnified faces, two pairs of bright, watery eyes reflecting her own; it was Yu'er and Changsheng.

Last night, these two little ones had sneaked in, insisting on sleeping with her. After she had Jiu'er and the Prince of Pingxi inform them, she had let the two children stay.

Though they had been restless for most of the night, they had slept exceptionally well in the second half. She hadn’t slept this well in a long time.

"Mother, you're awake!" Chu Hongyu called out sweetly. When there were no outsiders around, the way he called her "Mother" was far too natural.

"Mother..." the little girl followed, then climbed into Yun Chu's arms.

Not to be outdone, Chu Hongyu wrapped his arms tightly around Yun Chu's neck.

The little girl lifted her leg and draped it over Yun Chu's waist.

"Changsheng, don't push it," Chu Hongyu huffed, "You held Mother all night last night, and I didn’t say anything. Now you still want to monopolize her? I won’t allow it!"

He kicked the little leg off Yun Chu's waist with his foot.

The little girl withdrew her leg, her eyes widening as tears slowly welled up, looking utterly wronged.

Before Yun Chu could say anything, Chu Hongyu, as the older brother, couldn’t bear it first and compromised, "Alright, alright, I’ll give you half the space."

He reached out and grabbed his sister’s little foot, placing it on Yun Chu’s stomach.

Only then did the little girl break into a smile, wrapping her arms around Yun Chu’s neck, her face pressed against Yun Chu’s, looking completely content.

Yun Chu, with a child in each arm, felt her chest fill with warmth.

At this moment, the servants waiting outside heard the noise and knocked before entering.

The maid Tingshuang, who served Yun Chu, was already used to this scene. But Zheng Mom, who served the two young masters, was utterly shocked.

She knew the two young masters liked this Madam Xie, but she didn’t realize it had reached this extent... If she wasn’t mistaken, the Prince also treated Madam Xie differently... All three of them, father and children, liked this woman exceptionally.

If Madam Xie were still Miss Yun, she might have become the future Princess Consort of Pingxi. Unfortunately, Miss Yun had become Madam Xie five years ago... What a pity!

"Yu'er, Changsheng, wake up." Yun Chu sat up with the two children in her arms.

Zheng Mom and several other servants quickly approached, "Young Master, Young Lady, let’s get dressed first..."

Yun Chu took the clothes, "I’ll do it."

Such opportunities were rare; she also wanted to be closer to the children.

She carefully dressed both children one by one, then helped them wash up. As for combing their hair, Yun Chu wasn’t very skilled, so she carefully selected a hairpin for the little girl.

Soon, the three of them finished their morning routines. She took the children’s hands and walked out. In the flower hall, breakfast was already prepared.

Just as they finished eating, Chu Yi entered from the courtyard gate.

Seeing the physician Bi Langzhong following him, the little girl was so frightened that she immediately scrambled into Yun Chu’s arms. Chu Hongyu also stood protectively in front of his sister like a mother hen.

Physician Bi laughed in exasperation, "You two brats were saved by this old man’s hands. Why are you treating your lifesaver like an enemy?"

He and Chu Yi were old acquaintances, of course, so he wouldn’t truly mind.

He placed his medical case on the table and continued, "Young Lady, don’t panic. This time, the acupuncture will be done in the hot spring. The spring water will cushion the pain, so it won’t be as painful as before. Relax, it will be over quickly."

At the mention of "acupuncture," the little girl’s body began to tremble, and she clung tightly to Yun Chu’s neck.

Yun Chu picked her up and stood, softly coaxing, "Changsheng, there are some nasty little worms living inside your body. Physician Bi uses silver needles to kill those worms. Once the worms are all gone, your body will naturally get better."

Chu Changsheng’s long lashes were already dotted with tears as she shook her head in refusal.

Yun Chu leaned close to her ear and whispered, "After this acupuncture session, Mother will give you a little gift."

She took out a small pouch from her sleeve, opening it just a little to let the little girl peek inside.

Chu Changsheng’s eyes immediately lit up.

Inside was a little doll, identical to the one her brother had, except her brother’s was a boy doll, and this one was a girl doll.

Her brother carried his doll pouch at his waist every day and wouldn’t even let her touch it.

Now, she would have her own doll!

Seeing that this worked, Yun Chu immediately put the pouch away and softly said, "Mother will go with you to the hot spring pool. We’ll get rid of the little worms together, alright?"

Chu Changsheng nodded without hesitation.

"Prince, this Madam Xie is much better at coaxing children than you," Physician Bi couldn’t help but sigh. "The Prince is unmatched in bandit suppression, but when it comes to coaxing children, you’re really not good at it."

Chu Yi coldly replied, "If you don’t speak, no one would mistake you for a mute."

The group walked to the hot spring pool. Yun Chu was about to accompany the little girl into the water, but the little girl shook her head at her.

Chu Hongyu spoke up, "Aunt Yun, my sister means she can do it alone."

Chu Changsheng, barefoot, walked down into the hot spring pool and sat on the chair that the wet nurse had already prepared. Physician Bi also entered the water.

The little girl’s outer garment was removed, and silver needles were inserted one by one into the acupuncture points on her back. Although the hot spring water cushioned the pain, the little girl still bit her lower lip in pain.

Her small face turned pale, and large beads of sweat rolled down one by one.

Yun Chu’s heart also tightened.

How could she bear to just stand by? She immediately stepped into the pool and took the little girl’s trembling hand.

After about a quarter of an hour, or perhaps half an hour, the acupuncture finally ended. As soon as all the silver needles were removed, the little girl’s body went limp, and she fainted in Yun Chu’s arms.

Yun Chu quickly carried the child out of the water. Zheng Mom wrapped the little girl in a clean blanket, and a group of servants rushed over.

Yun Chu was about to follow when Chu Yi spoke, "She will sleep for at least a day and a night before waking up. Madam Xie, you should also go back and change your clothes."

Yun Chu looked down and saw that her wet clothes were clinging to her body. Immediately, Tingshuang draped a cloak over her shoulders.

She bowed to Chu Yi, then turned and walked into the inner room, where Tingshuang helped her change her clothes.

Tingshuang was now dressed like a married woman, her hair pinned up, exuding some of the composure and authority of a managing matron.

Originally, Yun Chu had given her a month off, but when something suddenly came up in the military camp and Yu Ke was not at home, Tingshuang, having nothing to do, had come to stay here.

With Tingshuang here, Yun Chu felt very much at ease.

She first went to check on the unconscious Chu Changsheng, then picked up Chu Hongyu, "These past two days with you have been very happy, but it’s getting late. Aunt Yun has to go home now."

Chu Hongyu’s nose twitched.

He had thought that if they spent a lot of time together, he could bear to part, but he found that the more time they spent together, the more he wanted to stay together forever.

But he knew that these two days had already been precious, and he couldn’t ask for more.

He obediently climbed down from Yun Chu, waving his hand, "Goodbye, Aunt Yun."

Yun Chu gently touched his face, then looked at Chu Yi, who had been standing silently to the side, "Prince, I’ll take my leave now."

Chu Yi nodded, watching as she, supported by the maid, got into the carriage.

Only when the carriage had driven far away did he retract his gaze and look at the attendant behind him, "Cheng Xu, go investigate the Xie family’s affairs."

Cheng Xu nodded, "Prince, should I start from when Master Xie was in Ji Province, or from when he entered office?"

Chu Yi said indifferently, "Investigate the Xie family’s inner household matters."

Cheng Xu looked confused and scratched his head.

When had their Prince ever cared about someone else’s backyard affairs?

---

chapters.title: Inviting the Retired Imperial Physician
chapters.content:
The carriage soon arrived at the Xie residence’s gate.

Stepping down from the carriage, Yun Chu looked up at the plaque above the Xie residence’s gate. These two characters were written by Xie Jingyu himself, gleaming under the sunlight.

She thought of her previous life. After Xie Shian was appointed as the top scholar, the Xie family had moved to a new residence. In the capital, where every inch of land was precious, not far from the Yun family’s alley, they had purchased a large five-courtyard mansion. At that time, it was Xie Shian himself who had written the characters "Xie Residence," and countless people had come to offer their congratulations.

The Xie family’s prosperity seemed as if it were still before her eyes.

But in this life, everything was completely different...

Yun Chu stepped over the threshold and entered. As soon as she returned to her courtyard, a servant came to report, "Madam, the Madam requests your presence."

Yun Chu took her time changing her clothes and drinking a cup of tea before going to Yuan Shi’s courtyard.

Upon entering, she saw her father-in-law, Xie Zhongcheng, was also there.

Xie Zhongcheng’s expression was not pleasant.

Yesterday, he had sent someone to Shengju to invite his daughter-in-law over, but the people at Shengju first said the Madam was not there, and in the end, they actually told him that the Madam would not be returning that night.

In all his years, this was the first time he had ever seen a woman not return home at night.

Had the Yun family never taught their daughter about a woman’s virtues?

But he didn’t dare voice these thoughts; he could only suppress them, hence his unpleasant expression.

"Chu’er is back." Yuan Shi said gently, "How were the matters at the estate handled? Smoothly?"

Yun Chu nodded, "Mother, is there something you need?"

Yuan Shi’s face showed a hint of embarrassment. She glanced at her husband before saying, "With September approaching, An’er will soon enter the Imperial College. Our Xie family is of humble origins, and An’er will certainly not be favored by the teachers at the Imperial College. Your father and I have been thinking of sending some gifts to the teachers. Chu’er, what do you think?"

Yun Chu’s expression remained calm, "Mother can handle this matter herself."

Yuan Shi nudged Xie Zhongcheng.

Xie Zhongcheng, with his hands behind his back, said coldly, "There are several teachers at the Imperial College. Sending gifts to all of them will cost a lot of silver. As An’er’s mother, you should be the one to cover this expense."

Although the Xie family was of humble origins, they were not particularly poor. Because the Xie family was highly respected in their hometown of Ji Province, many wealthy people had placed their properties under the Xie family’s name. Every year, they could earn several thousand taels of silver without lifting a finger. Over the years, they had saved up tens of thousands of taels.

But after the old madam passed away, and with the capital’s countless people criticizing them, to save face, the Xie family had held an extravagant funeral, spending every last tael they had saved.

Now, the Xie family was in a difficult period, the laughingstock of the capital’s tea and meal conversations. Only if An’er could make a name for himself could the Xie family shake off these...

An’er’s future must not be delayed.

Xie Zhongcheng continued, "Each teacher must be prepared with a gift worth nearly two thousand taels of silver before they will take An’er seriously."

A mocking smile appeared on Yun Chu’s lips.

The Xie family had indeed reached such a state that they could only pin all their hopes on Xie Shian.

Unfortunately, Xie Shian...

Seeing that she wasn’t speaking, Xie Zhongcheng’s face darkened, "What, you’re unwilling?"

"It’s not that I’m unwilling." Yun Chu sighed, "I only have about five or six thousand taels of silver on hand, which I was saving to invite an imperial physician to treat my husband. Since Father-in-law insists, then inviting the imperial physician can wait. Let’s prepare the gifts for An’er’s teachers first."

At these words, Xie Zhongcheng fell silent.

Over the past two days, he had visited Xie Jingyu’s residence many times. Watching his son’s body grow weaker and weaker, and seeing that countless medicines had no effect, he wished he could take the illness upon himself.

An imperial physician would certainly be much better than those quack doctors on the streets, but the Xie family couldn’t afford one.

If his daughter-in-law was willing to step in, that would naturally be for the best.

"Chu’er, can you really invite an imperial physician to the Xie residence to diagnose him?" Yuan Shi said joyfully, "Let’s put An’er’s matter aside for now and focus on curing Jingyu’s illness first."

Yun Chu spoke, "The imperial physicians in the palace naturally cannot be invited, but I know a retired imperial physician who used to treat the Empress. Many first-class families seek his treatment, though it will cost some silver."

Yuan Shi immediately turned and took out her own cash box, pulling out a money pouch and handing it to Yun Chu, "Chu’er, Jingyu is still young. We must cure his illness. Only then can our Xie family avoid ruin."

Yun Chu took the money, "Mother, rest assured. My husband will be fine."

After she left, Yuan Shi said, "Once Jingyu’s illness is cured, he will surely find a way to pave the path for An’er. We won’t have to worry about this anymore."

Xie Zhongcheng sighed.

For now, this was the only way.

Yun Chu handed the money pouch to Tingfeng, instructing him to make a trip. By evening, Tingfeng returned with an old man to the Xie residence.

Xie Jingyu was lying on the bed, and Concubine Jiang was attending to him, feeding him medicine. He felt as if he spent all day taking medicine, yet his body showed no sign of improvement.

Seeing his body gradually losing control, anyone would be afraid.

He was already in such a state, yet his wife, the one he was bound to for life, had not returned home last night, spending the entire night away.

Earlier, Concubine Jiang had said she had returned to the residence, but she hadn’t even come to see him once.

He had hidden the matter with He Shi, which was indeed his mistake, but was it not also her mistake to ignore her husband’s illness?

*Bang!*

Xie Jingyu raised his hand and knocked over the medicine bowl.

Concubine Jiang quickly crouched down to pick up the pieces, "This medicine must be taken for the illness to improve. My lord, let me bring you another bowl."

Xie Jingyu said in a deep voice, "There’s no need to bring more of this medicine!"

If the medicine couldn’t cure his illness, it was better not to take it at all!

Concubine Jiang was about to persuade him further when a gentle voice spoke, "My lord is right. There’s no need to brew this medicine anymore."

Xie Jingyu looked up and saw Yun Chu entering through the doorway. Seeing her bright and beautiful face, countless emotions surged in his heart.

He was about to question her when he saw an old man enter behind her.

"Husband, this is a retired imperial physician who used to specially treat the Empress for her well-being." Yun Chu sat down on a chair a few steps away from the bed, "Let the old physician diagnose your pulse and see how to treat you."

Xie Jingyu’s face was filled with disbelief.

Previously, when he had asked Yun Chu to invite an imperial physician to treat his illness, she had looked indifferent, leading him to believe she hadn’t taken his words to heart at all.

But now, it turned out she still cared for him, even going so far as to invite the imperial physician who had treated the Empress...

"Madam, thank you..."

The countless words in Xie Jingyu’s heart were reduced to this short sentence.

After five years of marriage, he had wronged her too much. Once his illness was cured, he would never let down his wife again.

He extended his hand, and the old physician placed his fingers on his pulse.

The old physician’s expression suddenly changed, "Master Xie’s pulse... something is not right... It seems... as if he is suffering from infertility?"

Xie Jingyu’s eyes widened abruptly, "Impossible!"

He had fathered so many children one after another. How could he possibly be suffering from infertility...?

chapters.title: Sorry, Yun Chu
chapters.content:
"Lord Xie, your listlessness is due to the influence of medicine..." The old imperial physician looked grave. "May I ask what medicine Lord Xie has taken recently?"

Aunt Jiang hurriedly brought over the medicine Xie Jingyu had taken in the past few days.

The old imperial physician smelled it, tasted it, and shook his head. "This is indeed the medicine for Lord Xie's condition. Is there anything else?"

Xie Jingyu suddenly remembered that before falling ill, he had been taking medicine to regulate his body, said to help him and his wife conceive a legitimate son.

He looked at Yun Chu with disbelief.

For some reason, a voice in his heart told him that this matter was connected to Yun Chu.

"Husband, why are you looking at me like that?" Yun Chu's eyes were clear. "It seems husband suspects me, his wedded wife. There should still be some of that body-regulating medicine left. Someone, go fetch it for the imperial physician to examine."

The servant outside immediately brought the remaining medicine.

The old imperial physician carefully smelled it, pinched a bit between his fingers, and continued shaking his head. "This is medicine to regulate a man's body. The prescription is exquisite. Taking it for three months will surely result in a son."

Xie Jingyu pressed his lips. "Wife, I misunderstood you just now..."

"No need to explain." Yun Chu's voice was indifferent. "Please, imperial physician, examine carefully to find out where the problem lies."

The old imperial physician nodded and carefully took Xie Jingyu's pulse. Suddenly, his gaze fell on the flowerpot on the windowsill, and he hurried over.

At the Shichen hour, Xie Shian returned from school.

As soon as he entered the gate, he was summoned by a servant from Xie Jingyu's courtyard.

He thought his father wanted to ask about his studies. When he entered, he saw the servants all lowering their heads, the atmosphere heavy.

His heart sank. It seemed his father's illness had worsened again.

Xie Shian walked to the door and saw Yun Chu inside. He bowed. "Father, Mother."

"Kneel down!"

Xie Jingyu's cold shout used all his strength.

Seeing Xie Shian standing still, he picked up the cup from the bedside and threw it at him. "I told you to kneel! Didn't you hear me?!"

Xie Shian didn't understand what was happening.

But his father was so angry, he didn't dare ask. He straightened his back and knelt.

Xie Jingyu's eyes seemed to spray fire. He couldn't believe that his painstakingly cultivated eldest son had poisoned him.

He had placed so much hope in this son, and now he felt just as much heartbreak, grief, pain, and anger!

He couldn't help but crawl out of bed, picked up the flowerpot from the windowsill, and smashed it in front of Xie Shian.

Soil and shards exploded in front of Xie Shian, his face suddenly changing.

"Speak! Why did you do this?"

Xie Jingyu supported himself on the table, panting heavily.

The old imperial physician had said that because of this flower, he would never be able to have children again in this lifetime.

Moreover, it was because of this flower's medicinal properties that his illness had worsened...

If they hadn't discovered this flower in time, he would have died violently within a month...

"Father, what's wrong with this flower?" Xie Shian pretended to be calm. "A peasant woman sold it to me, saying it could calm the mind. That's why I bought it and placed it in Father's bedroom."

Yun Chu spoke slowly. "An Ge'er, do you really not know what kind of flower this is?"

Xie Shian didn't dare meet her eyes. He lowered his head. "Son truly doesn't know. Please, Father and Mother, enlighten me."

"An Ge'er, you have disappointed me too much." Yun Chu shook her head. "You have always been smart, well-read, and thoughtful in everything you do. Do you think your father and I would believe you brought a flower here for no reason?"

Her voice turned cold. "The doctor said I suffer from infertility. Should I also suspect that it has something to do with you?"

Xie Shian suddenly raised his head. "No, Mother! I didn't do such a thing!"

"You did this, and I can understand why." Yun Chu showed a bitter smile. "You were afraid that after your father and I had a legitimate child, we would neglect you, distance ourselves from you.
