That's why you did this... But understanding is one thing, accepting and forgiving is another. An Ge'er, I will never be able to have a child of my own in this lifetime... Are you satisfied now?"

She finished, pressed her lips tightly, and walked out of the room.

Xie Shian had a belly full of explanations.

Before he could stand up, a foot struck his chest. Xie Jingyu had used all his strength to kick him there.

"How could I have such a rebellious son!" Xie Jingyu collapsed onto the bed. "Get out! Get out of here!"

He had always been proud of Xie Shian, certain that this son would be the future pillar of the Xie family, believing this son would change the Xie family's fate.

But this son's methods made him shudder.

But thinking again, someone who could unhesitatingly force their own birth mother to her death, how could they tolerate the appearance of a true legitimate child taking everything away?

His son was cold-hearted, indifferent, and selfish. Such a person would have no trouble climbing to high positions...

In the end, the Xie family would still have to rely on An Ge'er.

Xie Jingyu closed his eyes.

The only one he had wronged was Yun Chu...

He already had many children, but Yun Chu would never be a mother.

Xie Shian clutched his chest and walked out.

He looked at the servant waiting at the door and lowered his voice. "Has anyone been to Father's courtyard?"

The servant lowered his head. "More than an hour ago, Madam brought an old imperial physician to diagnose Lord's pulse."

Xie Shian's brows furrowed.

He had checked medical books. The flower needed to be placed in the room for at least a month to take effect.

But he had brought it less than ten days ago. How could the imperial physician have detected its influence on his father's body?

He felt something was wrong but didn't know where.

He walked towards Sheng Ju.

Xue, guarding at the door, said, "Madam is resting. Young Master, please return."

Xie Shian said, "Then I will come tomorrow morning to apologize to Mother."

Yun Chu sat in the room, indifferent to the Xie family's affairs.

She was drawing, designing three pendants: one for Yu Ge'er, one for Changsheng, and one for herself.

But the raw jade given by the Prince of Pingxi was too large. After making three pendants, at least two-thirds remained.

She thought for a moment and drew some jewelry, styles suitable for little girls. A full set of hair ornaments, little girls would surely like them.

The remaining scraps could be made into small beads. Paired with tassels she made herself, they could be hung on Yu Ge'er's fan or sword.

Yun Chu spent two days finalizing the drafts, then took the drawings to the craftsman.

As soon as she reached the street, she heard many people discussing Liu the Imperial Son-in-law.

"Have you heard? Liu the Imperial Son-in-law has been beheaded!"

"But Liu was personally chosen by the Grand Princess, deeply favored by her. How could he be beheaded?"

"My cousin's nephew works in the palace. He said Liu the Imperial Son-in-law committed a breach of etiquette in the court, greatly disrespecting the Emperor. The Emperor, in a fit of rage, personally beheaded him!"

"Didn't you see many yamen runners passing by earlier? I heard the entire Liu family has been arrested!"

"But even if Liu the Imperial Son-in-law committed a breach of etiquette, what does that have to do with the rest of the Liu family?"

"Who knows the ins and outs of court affairs..."

---

chapters.title: Marquis of Xuanwu Arrested
chapters.content:
Listening to the street discussions about Liu the Imperial Son-in-law, Yun Chu felt a sense of disorientation.

In her previous life, the Liu incident only became public in September. This time, it happened half a month early, probably because her father and eldest brother had intervened.

The common people thought Liu had committed a breach of etiquette in court, angering the Emperor, leading to his beheading.

In reality, after court adjourned, Liu had an illicit affair with a concubine in the rear palace and was caught in the act by the Emperor. No man could accept being cuckolded, let alone the ruler of a nation. The Emperor immediately drew the long knife from his guard and, without hesitation, beheaded Liu.

The Emperor was old, and his strength was lacking. It was said that it took many blows before Liu's neck was severed...

The royal scandal could not be spread, so only a few knew the truth.

The Emperor didn't trust others to handle Liu's case and specifically assigned it to her father. A series of charges were established, and the first act was to confiscate the Imperial Son-in-law's mansion.

And the letter she had written in the voice of Marquis of Xuanwu was placed on Liu's desk.

The letter's content was simple: "...I know something about the affair between the Imperial Son-in-law and Concubine Tian. If you want me to keep silent, prepare ten thousand taels of silver and send it to the Marquis of Xuanwu's residence..."

Knowing the royal scandal and using it for blackmail was something the Emperor would never tolerate. The Marquis of Xuanwu's residence would soon disappear from the capital.

Yun Chu's expression was cold.

In her previous life, until her death, she never knew that someone else had taken her place on her wedding night.

He ruined her life and wanted to live leisurely as the Marquis of Xuanwu, with a virtuous wife at home and a beautiful concubine outside, simply delusional!

Yun Chu had just finalized the details of the drawings with the craftsman when a large group of officers passed through the street, heading to the Marquis of Xuanwu's residence.

Soon, those officers escorted the Marquis of Xuanwu through the street.

Countless commoners discussed animatedly.

"What's going on today? First Liu the Imperial Son-in-law, now the Marquis of Xuanwu?"

"Liu was arrested for breach of etiquette. What crime did the Marquis of Xuanwu commit that the court is making such a public arrest?"

"Who knows what's happening..."

Qin Mingheng was escorted along, equally confused.

Since divorcing Luo Shi, he had become the laughingstock of the capital's tea and meal conversations. To avoid ridicule, he hadn't attended court for many days, staying home to accompany his wife, Chu Niang, and reading the Four Books and Five Classics to the child in her womb.

He had just heard from his servants about Liu's affair with a palace concubine and was shocked that a high-ranking Imperial Son-in-law could do such a thing. Then, officials barged into the Marquis's residence and arrested him.

Since inheriting the title, he had always followed the rules, never doing anything improper. He truly didn't understand what crime he had committed to be publicly arrested and paraded through the streets, damaging the reputation of the Marquis of Xuanwu's residence!

He lifted his head and, in the dense crowd, saw a face he had yearned for day and night.

It was Yun Chu!

In that instant, he suddenly understood why he was in this situation.

It was her... She used the Yun family's power to frame him with a false charge... just to revenge the wedding night!

She was the love of his life, the one he had admired for so many years. For her, he could give up anything.

But she... she wished he were dead.

He looked at Yun Chu and saw the coldness in her eyes, saw her satisfaction. His heart felt as if it were being slowly cut by a knife, the pain unbearable.

That night, it clearly wasn't him. Why should he bear her revenge?

Qin Mingheng suddenly began to struggle. The two officers could barely hold him down, almost letting him escape.

"Let go of me!" he roared. The two officers ignored him, forcefully escorting him through the bustling street.

Qin Mingheng fixed his gaze on Yun Chu.

He had done nothing wrong. A false charge would never convict him. He would definitely be acquitted!

Then, he would personally ask this woman if she had a heart at all!

Yun Chu watched Qin Mingheng being taken away, her expression unchanged.

The next morning, she heard that Luo Shi, who had been divorced by the Marquis of Xuanwu, had beaten the drum of appeal to the Emperor, accusing her former husband of communicating with the remnants of a criminal's party. She even presented crucial evidence.

Originally, the court was still searching for evidence against the Marquis of Xuanwu. Luo Shi's action dealt a fatal blow to him.

The court immediately issued an edict: the title of Marquis of Xuanwu was revoked, all property of the Marquis's residence was confiscated, and all male descendants for three generations, including Qin Mingheng, were to be exiled three thousand li away.

The previous generation of the Marquis's family had already passed away, and the next generation only included Qin Mingheng and Luo Shi's only legitimate son.

In this dynasty, when a couple divorced, the children were always awarded to the male party. However, since Luo Shi had reported the crime and the legitimate son was young, the court made an exception, allowing the Marquis of Xuanwu's legitimate son to change his surname to Luo, thus avoiding exile.

Yun Chu couldn't help but sigh. If Qin Mingheng hadn't kept a concubine, Luo Shi would never have been so decisive in cutting ties with the Marquis's family.

Qin Mingheng was accused by his own wife, a consequence of his own actions. It was his just deserts... It was a pity for the newly acquired concubine, who was said to have been so frightened that she went into premature labor...

"Excellent, truly excellent!" Xie Zhongcheng looked delighted. "Back then, Wei Ge'er only made the young master of the Marquis's family get a scraped finger, and his leg was broken in retaliation... Hahaha, let the Marquis of Xuanwu rely on his power to bully others, let him be tyrannical. Look, retribution has come, hasn't it?"

"Evil has its consequences, and heaven will collect its due!" Yuan Shi said indignantly, then sighed. "I wonder where Wei Ge'er is now. At such a young age, alone and away from home... what a pitiful child..."

"Why bring him up?" Xie Zhongcheng changed the subject. "September is approaching, and An Ge'er will soon enter the Imperial College. The day before yesterday, I heard that they need to register early at the Imperial College. I wonder if Jingyu can get up to see An Ge'er off."

Xie Jingyu's condition had improved slightly, but only slightly.

His left hand was completely immobile, and his left leg could barely support him. Having stayed in the house for too long, he also wanted to go out for some fresh air.

Moreover, with the old madam's passing, the one-year mourning period meant he feared that if he continued to stay indoors, the people at court would forget there was still a Lord Xie.

The next day, he got up and personally took Xie Shian to the palace to register.

After the flowerpot incident, the atmosphere between father and son was somewhat awkward. They rode in the same carriage, silent the entire way.

Finally, the carriage stopped at the palace gate.

"Oh, isn't that Lord Xie? What brings you to the palace?" Xie Jingyu's rival, Minister Yuan, approached. "Lord Xie, your complexion is really not good. You should take better care of yourself."

Xie Jingyu's voice was flat. "Thank you for your concern, Minister Yuan."

"Lord Xie, the mourning period is not over. You shouldn't come to the palace gate. If you offend the nobles in the palace, you might be charged with a great disrespect crime." Minister Yuan said in a low voice. "Liu the Imperial Son-in-law and the Marquis of Xuanwu were both punished for great disrespect. Lord Xie, be careful."

These words sounded like concern but were actually mockery.

Xie Jingyu's face was very dark. In the past, he would have sought revenge, but now, he didn't have the energy.

"Minister Yuan's words are too serious." Xie Shian spoke up beside him. "The Yuan family's young master is not good at his studies and didn't pass the imperial examinations. Naturally, Minister Yuan doesn't know that today is the registration day for the Imperial College. My father is sending me into the palace to study with the nobles. Where is the offense in that?"

Minister Yuan's face stiffened.

It was true that his son was not good at his studies, and mentioning this made him feel ashamed, unable to hold his head up.

He had no choice but to leave in embarrassment.

"I'll send you off here." Xie Jingyu said. "Be careful with your words and actions."

He didn't say anything else. He knew this son knew how to handle himself.

chapters.title: Enrolling in the Imperial Academy
chapters.content:
The palace walls towered high.

Xie Shian entered through a small side gate on the east side of the palace entrance. Following a young eunuch, it took him over a quarter of an hour to finally reach the Imperial Academy.

The Imperial Academy was a school established exclusively for the royal princes and princesses. Children of noble and meritorious families could also enroll, while high-ranking officials were only allowed one spot per generation. For example, the Yun family, despite being an aristocratic clan, could only send one child in... Families of lower rank could only gain admission if their children were exceptionally outstanding. As for ordinary commoners, they need not even dream of it...

Xie Shian arrived at the school gate. As far as the eye could see, there were either princes, sons of dukes, or sons of marquises and earls... His own status was the lowest among them.

He stepped inside and was about to find a seat.

A mocking voice suddenly reached his ears.

"Oh, isn't this Young Master Xie?"

He turned toward the voice and saw a richly dressed man approaching him.

Although he hadn't met many royal nobles, the man's attire, demeanor, and tone made it clear he was a prince.

Xie Shian cupped his hands respectfully and said, "Greetings, Your Highness."

The man was the Sixth Prince.

Currently, the first five princes were grown and held important positions in the court, so the highest-ranking person in the Imperial Academy was this Sixth Prince.

"Young Master Xie is impressive. At such a young age, he's already the top scholar in the provincial examination!" the Sixth Prince sneered. "It makes the rest of us look as stupid as pigs!"

The surrounding noble scions looked at Xie Shian differently.

So this was the youngest top scholar of the provincial examination, Xie Shian, the eldest son of the Xie family. Every time they were scolded, their elders would compare them to this Young Master Xie.

Comparisons were indeed infuriating.

Because of this outstanding person in the capital, they had been beaten by their fathers and grandfathers countless times.

In the classroom, there was also a small figure, Chu Hongyu, the young heir of the Prince of Pingxi.

He sat in the front row, glanced at Xie Shian, and felt a pang of jealousy in his heart.

He wasn't jealous of Xie Shian for being the top scholar, but rather jealous that Xie Shian could openly call his mother "Mother."

Hearing the man in front of him speak, Xie Shian guessed he must be the Sixth Prince. Lowering his head, he said, "Being the top scholar in a minor examination means nothing. I have long heard that the Sixth Prince is exceptionally talented, quick-witted, and a paragon among men."

The Sixth Prince picked at his ear. "What do you mean by 'quick-witted' and 'paragon'?"

A young noble beside him spoke up, "It means praising the Sixth Prince for being clever."

"Then just say I'm clever. Why be so pretentious? Isn't this just to show off your own knowledge?" The Sixth Prince lifted his leg and placed his foot on a stool. "Since Young Master Xie is so good at studying, he must be good at polishing shoes too. Come, clean my shoes for me!"

The surrounding nobles cheered him on.

"Isn't the Xie family from a humble background? Young Master Xie must be used to this kind of work."

"His Highness the Sixth Prince is letting you polish his shoes. This is your fortune. Hurry up!"

"Surely Young Master Xie isn't unwilling?"

Xie Shian pressed his lips tightly together.

He knew that attending the Imperial Academy would invite trouble, but he hadn't expected it to happen on the very first day, and in such a humiliating manner.

The Sixth Prince was the highest-ranking person here. If he offended him, it would be difficult to continue staying at the Imperial Academy.

He clenched his fingers, his lips forming a straight line, and slowly bent down.

Just at that moment, a clear voice rang out: "Sixth Royal Brother."

It was the Eighth Prince, who had walked over. Though only ten years old, he had already grown tall, like a young pine tree. He approached the Sixth Prince and said, "Young Master Xie's hands are for holding brushes and writing essays. For trivial tasks like polishing shoes, a servant would suffice."

As soon as he finished speaking, a palace maid behind him stepped forward, took out a handkerchief, and began wiping the non-existent dirt from the Sixth Prince's shoes.

The Sixth Prince huffed.

This Xie boy's birth mother was from the Yun family, and the Eighth Prince's birth mother was also from the Yun family. It was no surprise he was defending Xie Shian.

General Yun had just returned to the capital and was constantly appearing before the Emperor.

This time, he would let it go. Next time, when the Eighth Prince wasn't around, he would see how Xie Shian would be humiliated!

At this moment, the Dean of the Imperial Academy entered the classroom. The room immediately fell silent, and everyone took their seats.

"All the old students already know me. For the new ones, this is probably our first meeting. So let me introduce myself." Dean Wang stroked his beard. "My surname is Wang. You can call me Teacher Wang. From now on, I will be responsible for your academic life here. I don't care if you are a prince, a noble heir, a young marquis, or an earl. Once you enter this door, you have only one identity: my student. If anyone here uses their status to bully others, I will have no choice but to write a memorial and submit it to the Emperor."

The Sixth Prince looked disdainful. This Teacher Wang only knew how to report to the Emperor. He wrote memorials for every little thing; he didn't know how the Emperor could tolerate it.

"Let's not dwell on that." Teacher Wang continued, "Now, I will test the new students' level. I will give a few questions, and you will answer them."

There were more than a dozen new students, and apart from Xie Shian, they were all children of noble families.

The questions Teacher Wang initially asked were simple, and almost everyone could answer them. As the questions became more difficult, fewer and fewer could respond. In the end, only Xie Shian was left to answer Teacher Wang's challenging questions.

Chu Hongyu sat in his seat, feeling somewhat depressed.

He had only memorized the Three Character Classic and the Thousand Character Classic. Apart from these, he knew nothing else.

Others had studied in private schools for three to five years before coming to the Imperial Academy. But he had been sent here by his father when he was only four years old.

Xie Shian was so outstanding, which made him seem really stupid.

He gritted his teeth, opened his book, and while others were still watching the commotion, he began to study seriously.

Teacher Wang was very satisfied with Xie Shian's performance. "Truly deserving of being the top scholar in the provincial examination. You indeed have some real talent. Xie Shian, from now on, you will sit next to the Sixth Prince. Sixth Prince, you should learn more from Xie Shian."

The Sixth Prince's expression darkened. He was a prince, and now he was being told to learn from a commoner scholar. Wouldn't that be a laughingstock?

He huffed and ignored Teacher Wang's words.

Teacher Wang had been teaching the Sixth Prince for three or four years and naturally knew the prince's temperament, unlearned and troublesome. He arranged for Xie Shian to sit next to the Sixth Prince, hoping that the prince might be positively influenced, even if only a little.

After the morning roll call at the Imperial Academy, everyone was dismissed. Formal classes would begin in September.

As soon as Teacher Wang left, a group of people gathered around Xie Shian's desk. Among them were both noble scions and serious scholars. Several young men held books and earnestly discussed problems with Xie Shian. Xie Shian did not hide his knowledge and chatted with these people of much higher status, and both parties enjoyed the conversation.

Through this, Xie Shian got to know several high-status heirs.

Once again, he deeply understood that one must stand in high places to meet those in high places and to reach high places...

Since he had come to the Imperial Academy, he must establish a firm foothold here, stand out, and ensure that the Xie family would no longer be labeled as a humble family...

---

chapters.title: The Yun Family’s Contingency Plan
chapters.content:
Apart from Xie Shian enrolling in the Imperial Academy, there was another major event in the Xie family: Xie Pin was getting married.

More than two months ago, the Emperor issued a decree, bestowing marriage between Prince Anjing and Xie Pin. The wedding was set for September, and the big day was approaching.

During this time, so many unfavorable things had happened to the Xie family. They were counting on this wedding to turn their fortunes around. Therefore, Xie Zhongcheng and Lady Yuan attached great importance to it.

While Yun Chu was busy, a young servant from Xie Zhongcheng’s side delivered the guest list he had personally drafted to her courtyard, Shengju.

Yun Chu took it and glanced at it. Her brows immediately furrowed.

Not only had Xie Zhongcheng included her father’s name on the list, but he had also included the names of more than a dozen second, third, and fourth-rank military officers who were her father’s subordinates.

She took up a brush and crossed out all these names.

The young servant hesitated, not daring to speak. He took the list back, and soon after, Xie Zhongcheng and Lady Yuan arrived together.

"Chu’er," Lady Yuan got straight to the point. "Why did you cross out all these guests' names?"

Yun Chu raised her eyes. "These people have no connection with the Xie family. How could my mother and father-in-law think of inviting them to the wedding banquet?"

Xie Zhongcheng looked as if it were only natural. "These military officers are all friends of your father, General Yun. When your father comes to the Xie family for the wedding, these people can come along to keep him company and have a drink. Otherwise, your father might find his stay at the Xie family boring."

Yun Chu gave a faint smile.

Her father-in-law was really good at finding ways to show off the Xie family’s connections and save face.

She said calmly, "My father is leaving the capital tomorrow. He won’t be attending the wedding banquet. Father-in-law need not worry about this."

"Leaving tomorrow?" Xie Zhongcheng looked astonished. "The wedding is in just a few days. As the maternal grandfather, how can he not stay a few more days to attend his granddaughter’s wedding?"

Hearing this, Lady Yuan gave her husband a hard tug.

Xie Pin was not Yun Chu’s biological daughter at all. She had no blood relation to the Yun family. Why should General Yun stay in the capital any longer for a granddaughter with no blood ties?

Previously, when they didn’t know that Xie Pin was the daughter of Concubine He, it was fine for Yun Chu to give her wholehearted care.

But now...

Of the three children born to Concubine He—

Everyone in the capital knew what Xie Wei had done.

As for Xie An... he had actually placed a flower that symbolized the end of one’s lineage in his own father’s room.

And Xie Pin... who knew what kind of things she would do in the future?

Each of Concubine He’s children was more terrifying than the last. If she were Yun Chu, she wouldn’t dare to raise these children either.

"Chu’er, your father-in-law’s meaning is that since your father has rarely returned to the capital, he hopes that the Yun and Xie families can interact more," Lady Yuan said with a smile, trying to smooth things over. "Your father must be leaving because of official business. We don’t know when he will depart. I will have Jingyu go with you to see him off."

Yun Chu said, "My husband is unwell. It’s better if he doesn’t go. I can go alone to see my father off. He won’t mind."

Lady Yuan could only sigh. "Then so be it."

After leaving Yun Chu’s courtyard, Xie Zhongcheng flicked his sleeve and left. Lady Yuan continued to sigh as she went to Xie Pin’s courtyard.

Xie Pin’s wedding dress was already embroidered. Currently, she was working on the red bridal veil. Having grown up under Concubine He’s care, she had learned some of her skills. The red veil she was embroidering looked especially beautiful.

Seeing Lady Yuan enter, she stood up and asked, "Grandmother, why have you come?"

"I have prepared some personal money for you." Lady Yuan took out a few silver notes from her sleeve. "After you go to Prince Anjing’s residence, there will be many places where you need money. Here are two thousand taels of silver. It’s not much, but it can help you in times of need. Keep it safe."

Xie Pin pursed her lips. Two thousand taels of silver was indeed very little.

But for her, it was a huge sum, as she only had a little over three hundred taels of silver to her name.

She would probably become the poorest princess consort in this dynasty.

"Prince Anjing’s residence is not like our Xie family. There are many rules. After you marry there, you must be cautious in everything," Lady Yuan advised. "You are the principal wife and the mistress of the prince’s residence. You must be a virtuous wife, helping the prince solve his worries. Do not do those..."

"I know!" Xie Pin said impatiently. "The palace matrons have already taught me all this."

Lady Yuan spoke earnestly, "You also know what Xie Wei has done. As for Xie An, in your father’s room... Well, let’s not talk about that. As your grandmother, I don’t ask you to help the Xie family. I only ask that you live peacefully and that everything goes well for you."

Xie Pin tightened her lips. "I will remember."

In just a few days, she would be married to Prince Anjing’s residence. Initially, she had been looking forward to this day, but now that it was truly approaching, her heart was filled with an indescribable sense of confusion and panic.

If she were the only princess consort, everything would be fine. But she was not entering alone, there would also be a concubine accompanying her.

Thinking of this, Xie Pin couldn’t help but sigh.

The next day, before dawn, Yun Chu got up and took a carriage to the city outskirts. Her father, accompanied by three hundred personal guards, was secretly heading to Nanyue.

The three hundred guards had already departed in advance. Yun Silin was saying his farewells to his family at a pavilion outside the city.

The Yun family members were all present: Yun Chu’s mother, Lin Shi; her elder brother, Yun Ze; her sister-in-law, Liu Qianqian; and her nephew, Yun Zhenjiang.

"This time, I am going to Nanyue and probably won’t be back for two years," Yun Silin said to his family. "After I leave, if anything major happens in the Yun family, you must consult with Chu’er more."

Yun Ze nodded. "Father, don’t worry. I understand."

Lin Shi and Liu Qianqian did not question why Yun family matters should be discussed with a married-off daughter. They both seriously nodded in agreement.

"Chu’er..." Yun Silin looked at his daughter. "Marrying you to Xie Jingyu was the best choice under the circumstances at the time. But time has proven that this choice was wrong. Your mother and I have discussed it. We will choose a suitable opportunity to ask the clan elders to intervene and arrange a divorce. Your elder brother and sister-in-law also agree with this. After the divorce, you can return to the Yun family. We will support you for the rest of your life."

Yun Chu felt a warmth in her heart. "Father, I already have a plan for the divorce. You need not worry about this small matter while you are away."

"Matters concerning children are always the most important," Yun Silin raised his hand and rubbed her hair. "You have truly grown up. You are unwilling to share anything with your parents, and you are used to solving everything on your own. I am proud that you have grown up, but it also pains me... Chu’er, rest assured. Your father promises you that what you fear will not happen."

Yun Chu’s eyes stung. She nodded forcefully. "Alright, I will learn to discuss things with my elder brother."

She was afraid that if she continued, she would not be able to hold back her tears. She turned and took a deposit slip from her maid, Tingxue. "Father, there are fifty thousand taels of silver deposited here. It’s the earnings from selling ice this summer. Take this money to the south, buy land, buy people, and plant crops, grain, the more the better."

Yun Silin pondered for a moment and understood Yun Chu’s meaning.

If it really came to that, having grain would be the Yun family’s contingency plan.

Just as he was about to speak, Yun Ze suddenly said, "The Prince of Pingxi has arrived."

Yun Silin immediately tucked the deposit slip into his waist pocket and looked toward the side. Prince of Pingxi, Chu Yi, was riding a horse toward them.

chapters.title: Xie Pin's Grand Wedding Day
chapters.content:
Chu Yi arrived on horseback.

He dismounted in front of them and said to Yun Silin, "I came specially to see the general off. Fortunately, I am not too late."

Yun Silin took Chu Yi aside and said, "Your Highness has eliminated countless bandits, earning the trust of the Emperor and the love of the people. However, this has also aroused the jealousy of the Crown Prince. Have you noticed this yourself?"

Chu Yi replied, "If I were to hide my talents and give up military power just because of the Crown Prince's jealousy, that would be a betrayal to my father, the Emperor, and to the people. I will still do what I must do."

Yun Silin nodded.

He admired Prince Pingxi for this very reason, which was why he was willing to take him to the battlefield for training.

Among the grown princes in the palace, the Crown Prince was the son of the Empress, the Second Prince was exceptionally talented and known for his wisdom, and the Third Prince, Prince Pingxi, was martial and held great prestige in the hearts of the people... At court, there were already faint signs of three factions forming.

If the Yun family were to choose a wise master, they would have to pick one of these three.

Prince Pingxi might...

However, they would need to observe for at least two more years before making a decision.

He spoke, "I will be leaving for Nanyue soon. I don’t know when I will return. If anything happens to the Yun family, I hope Your Highness will take care of it."

Chu Yi readily agreed.

After they had discussed everything, Yun Silin bade farewell to everyone, mounted his horse, and rode south.

Watching him disappear down the road, Chu Yi finally withdrew his gaze. As he turned his head, he caught sight of Yun Chu’s profile.

After she left the hot spring villa that day, he had ordered someone to investigate the affairs of the Xie family’s inner courtyard.

He knew that it was highly inappropriate for him to investigate a woman’s private quarters... But the seed that had sprouted in his heart had already grown into a towering tree, with countless wild vines spreading madly. He could no longer control that hidden emotion; he needed an outlet.

He had always considered himself an upright man. He would not use underhanded means to get what he wanted.

But when his subordinates reported back about the Xie family’s affairs, he was relieved that she had suffered so much; it was as if he now had a reason to do things he had never dared to consider before. But more than that, he felt heartbroken for the five years she had spent in the Xie family... Slowly, he became determined. He didn’t mind using some tactics to help her leave the Xie family...

She and her husband had only shared a bed on their wedding night and never again.

Her husband had taken four concubines, one after another, and fathered a large number of illegitimate children.

Her life in the Xie family had been far from happy.

Yun Ze was about to speak when he noticed that Chu Yi seemed to be staring at Yun Chu.

He looked at Chu Yi and, in those usually cold eyes, saw a hint of something akin to heartache.

His heart jolted in surprise, and he pretended to cough.

But Chu Yi seemed not to hear him; his eyes were fixed on Yun Chu as if glued to her.

"Eldest Brother, are you feeling cold?" Yun Chu asked with concern.

"It’s just that my throat is a little dry," Yun Ze said casually. "Let’s go. We should return to the city."

Lin Shi and Yun Chu helped the pregnant Liu Qianqian into the carriage, while Yun Ze and Chu Yi rode their horses in front of the carriage.

Yun Ze let out a heavy sigh.

Chu Yi asked him, "What troubles you, Minister Yun? Are you worried about General Yun’s safety?"

"With my father leading three hundred elite soldiers, there’s nothing to worry about," Yun Ze thought. Besides, Chu had already written in her letter about every possible danger, person, or event they might encounter on the road. If his father still ran into trouble, it could only mean that the Yun family’s fate was sealed.

He paused before saying, "It’s about Chu’er. These are family matters, so I won’t trouble Your Highness with them."

Upon hearing this, Chu Yi immediately said, "Your father and I are close friends despite the age difference, and you and I practically grew up together. As your friend, I am willing to listen and share your burdens."

Yun Ze’s fingers tightened.

It seemed that Chu Yi had not overthought it. Prince Pingxi’s feelings for Chu’er were indeed...

He spoke softly, "Five years ago, when my parents were choosing a husband for Chu’er, they carefully selected Xie Jingyu, the top scholar of that year. We thought it was a good match, but who could have imagined... Xie Jingyu already had children before the marriage. After Chu’er married into the Xie family, her days were spent managing household affairs and raising the Xie family’s children. The thought of her raising someone else’s children is heartbreaking..."

Chu Yi’s eyes darkened suddenly.

He had a son and a daughter. If Yun Chu became his wife, in the eyes of the Yun family, would she not also be raising someone else’s children?

Yun Ze glanced at him.

His words were clear in their implication.

Even if Chu’er divorced, she would not easily remarry, let alone marry a man who already had children.

He hoped Prince Pingxi understood this.

Chu Yi’s eyes were only dark for a moment before they brightened again.

If Yun Ze could say such things, it meant that Yun Ze had likely seen through his intentions.

Yun Ze had not mentioned that Yun Chu was already married but had instead brought up the children... Did this mean that the biggest obstacle between him and Yun Chu was the children, not her marital status?

If that was the case, did it mean the Yun family was also considering a divorce for Yun Chu?

"Being a parent is the greatest virtue, and being a child is the greatest filial piety. Your sister, as the legitimate wife of the Xie family, is the epitome of goodness and virtue. But the Xie family’s children—" Chu Yi shook his head. "Is the Xie family truly worthy of your sister’s sacrifices, Minister Yun? Some things, when they need to be cut off, should be cut off."

Yun Ze pressed his lips tightly together.

It seemed Prince Pingxi had not taken his words to heart at all.

"I’ve heard that Minister Yun has been restoring ancient texts recently and has encountered some troubles," Chu Yi continued. "Is there anything I can do to help?"

Yun Ze’s voice was indifferent, "This small matter does not require Your Highness’s attention."

After saying this, he kicked his horse and rode ahead.

Chu Yi paid no mind to his attitude. He rode his horse beside the carriage, following all the way to the Yun residence.

When Yun Chu dismounted, he stepped forward, cupped his hands, and said, "The Xie family’s wedding is in a few days. Would it be too presumptuous of me to ask for an invitation?"

Yun Chu thought of the two children and nodded, "Alright, I will have someone deliver it to your palace."

In the blink of an eye, the day of the grand wedding between Prince Anjing and the eldest daughter of the Xie family arrived.

The entire Xie residence was adorned with lanterns and decorations. The servants were filled with joy, and the main hall was bustling with activity. Even Xie Jingyu, who had been ill for a long time, seemed to have recovered.

He was dressed in new clothes, looking spirited and standing at the entrance to greet guests. There was no trace of his month-long illness.

"Congratulations, Minister Xie! Madam Xie!"

"I have prepared a small gift. I hope Minister Xie will accept it!"

"Minister Xie, a joyful occasion makes one look radiant! Later, let’s have a few drinks!"

Some colleagues from the court arrived at the door, each bringing congratulatory gifts and offering compliments one after another. Xie Jingyu’s complexion improved with each word.

Soon, a carriage stopped at the entrance of the Xie residence. Chu Yi, dressed in a black brocade robe, was the first to alight from the carriage. Then, he lifted two children down from it.

The onlookers were all stunned.

"It’s Prince Pingxi!"

"When did Minister Xie become connected to Prince Pingxi?"

"Prince Pingxi attending a wedding should be at Prince Anjing’s residence, not the Xie family’s. It seems their relationship is extraordinary."

"Perhaps it’s out of respect for Madam Xie, since she is the eldest daughter of the Yun family."

Chu Yi, holding his daughter, walked straight up to Xie Jingyu. "Minister Xie, congratulations."

Although Xie Jingyu was somewhat surprised, he still welcomed them in with a smile.

As the most distinguished guest, Prince Pingxi naturally did not continue to greet guests at the entrance but accompanied Xie Jingyu into the residence.

After taking a few steps inside, Chu Yi stopped. "May I trouble Madam Xie to help look after these two children?"

Yun Chu smiled and took the hands of the two children.

---

chapters.title: Prince Pingxi Makes His Move
chapters.content:
The Xie residence’s entrance was bustling with guests. Yun Chu, not wanting to greet any more, left it to Yuan Shi and took the two children to the inner courtyard.

The two little ones were overjoyed, constantly calling out to Yun Chu as "Mother."

Meanwhile, Xie Jingyu accompanied Chu Yi into the banquet hall, where servants served the finest tea.

Chu Yi casually remarked, "I’ve heard that the late Madam Xie passed away, and Minister Xie fell ill from grief. But from what I see, Minister Xie seems to be in good health."

Xie Jingyu respectfully replied, "I was once so ill I couldn’t get out of bed. My wife helped invite a retired imperial physician to diagnose and prescribe medicine for me. After taking the medicine, I recovered significantly."

Chu Yi’s fingers paused.

She... cared so much for this man that she even invited an old imperial physician for him?

A sense of gloom filled his heart. He asked casually, "Which physician was it?"

"It was Physician Qin," Xie Jingyu replied. "Physician Qin’s medical skills are exceptional. I will probably be fully recovered soon."

Chu Yi’s brow furrowed.

He might not know the specifics of all the civil and military officials, but because his two children had been frail since birth, he was well aware of every imperial physician in the Imperial Medical Bureau, what they specialized in, and their surnames. He was also familiar with all the physicians, herbalists, and barefoot doctors in the streets and alleys of the capital. Needless to say, he knew all the retired imperial physicians...

He had never heard of a retired imperial physician named Qin.

He temporarily set aside his doubts and said, "Today is a joyous occasion for the Xie family, the wedding of your eldest daughter. Yet, it seems someone is missing from the Xie family?"

Xie Jingyu’s face stiffened.

The missing person was naturally Xie Shiyou, his unfilial second son.

He didn’t even want to mention that disobedient son on such a happy day.

"How can such a joyous occasion lack someone?" Chu Yi said with a smile. "I have specially brought Xie Shiyou back for Minister Xie."

"What?!"

Xie Jingyu’s face changed drastically, and he abruptly stood up.

This sudden movement drew the attention of several nearby guests, who thought something had happened.

"Why is Minister Xie so agitated?" Chu Yi asked leisurely. "I know the Xie family has been searching for Xie Shiyou’s whereabouts. Coincidentally, my people spotted him, so I thought I would give Minister Xie a great gift."

When he had ordered Cheng Xu to investigate the Xie family’s affairs, he discovered that He Concubine, the one who had caused Xie Jingyu to disregard propriety, had died under mysterious circumstances.

Following this lead, he uncovered a shocking secret.

It turned out that He Concubine was the legitimate granddaughter of Minister He of the Ministry of Revenue, who had been executed for corruption and abuse of power over twenty years ago.

Furthermore, the Xie family’s eldest son, eldest daughter, and second son were likely descendants of the He family. However, he had not yet found concrete evidence.

"Let’s go, Minister Xie. Accompany me to bring Xie Shiyou back home."

Hearing Chu Yi’s words, Xie Jingyu swayed unsteadily.

After the old madame’s death, Xie Shiyou had secretly fled. At that time, the Xie family had been the talk of the town, like a rat crossing the street.

After so many days, the Xie family’s affairs had finally been forgotten... If Shiyou returned now, he would immediately be arrested, and the old madame’s death would be brought up again. If Shiyou’s crimes were confirmed, the Xie family would forever be nailed to the pillar of shame.

"Oh, there’s one more thing." Chu Yi’s voice was heavy. "More than twenty years ago, there was a major corruption case in the Ministry of Revenue that shocked the capital. Minister Xie, as a staff member of the Ministry of Revenue, must have heard of it, right?"

Xie Jingyu was still reeling from the news about Xie Shiyou when he heard another shocking piece of information.

"Rumor has it that descendants of the He family have recently come to the capital." Chu Yi fixed his gaze on Xie Jingyu. "Has Minister Xie seen any of the He family?"

Xie Jingyu felt a wave of dizziness and nearly fell off his chair.

"No, I haven’t," he gasped after a long pause. "This official does not know. Your Highness, what do you mean?"

"When I’ve said this much, Minister Xie still pretends to be ignorant in front of me." Chu Yi smiled. "Concubine He’s real surname is He. Am I correct?"

Xie Jingyu felt a surge of nausea, followed by a violent cough. He covered his mouth with his hand and felt a warmth in his palm. When he looked, it was a mouthful of black blood.

Clearly, he had felt much better that morning, but now he felt completely drained, as if he might faint at any moment.

But he knew he couldn’t faint.

"Y-Your Highness!" Xie Jingyu struggled to speak. "This official... this official..."

He wanted to say something, but he didn’t know what to say.

Since Prince Pingxi had come to him with this, it meant that all the evidence was already in place. Any explanation he gave would be futile.

Wait!

A sudden flash of insight struck him.

Prince Pingxi had come to discuss this matter during the Xie family’s joyous occasion, rather than bringing officials to investigate. This meant there was still room for negotiation.

He saw a glimmer of hope and immediately said, "Your Highness, if you have any orders, just say the word. This official is willing to serve you with my life!"

Chu Yi twirled his thumb, pausing for a long moment before speaking. "Minister Xie has been in mourning for a while now. I’m sure the late madame has felt your filial piety. I have some matters that require Minister Xie’s attention. Please make preparations."

Xie Jingyu was taken aback.

Since ancient times, it had been said that filial piety was the foundation of all virtues. When parents passed away, one was to observe a three-year mourning period; for grandparents, it was one year. This was known as "ding you" (observing mourning).

During the mourning period, officials were not allowed to attend court. Many talented individuals had their careers delayed because of this. He had been worried that after his one-year mourning period, the court would no longer have a place for him.

He never expected Prince Pingxi to ask him to return to work early.

Prince Pingxi was a royal prince. For him to allow an official to end mourning early to attend to duties was known as "duo qing" (breaking mourning for official duties). This was a special treatment reserved for officials of high rank and great trust from the Emperor. How had he, Xie Jingyu, earned such treatment...

However, Prince Pingxi had a hold over the Xie family and wanted him to work for him. By allowing him to end mourning early, he was also cultivating a trusted subordinate.

He, Xie Jingyu, was after all the top scholar of his year, a man of great talent. He had simply not been given the opportunity to shine.

Now that the court was subtly divided into three factions, what if the Crown Prince’s faction was the strongest? If he followed Prince Pingxi, he would certainly help Prince Pingxi ascend to the throne.

"I am willing to serve Your Highness with my life and follow you to the death!" Xie Jingyu declared.

Chu Yi nodded, a hint of mockery flashing in his eyes.

He would arrange a lucrative position for Xie Jingyu, a lucrative position in the Ministry of Revenue, one that involved handling large sums of money, at least hundreds of thousands of taels of silver a day.

He didn’t believe Xie Jingyu could resist such temptation.

The Yun family, from top to bottom, was known for their integrity. If they found out that their son-in-law had embezzled government silver, they would have an even clearer understanding that the two families were not on the same path. This would only accelerate Yun Chu’s divorce from Xie Jingyu...

Chu Yi was about to speak about Xie Shiyou.

Cheng Xu hurried over and whispered in his ear, "Your Highness, the Yun family has found their way to Li Hua Alley."

Li Hua Alley was where Xie Shiyou was temporarily being held.

His men were extremely efficient. For the Yun family to have found Li Hua Alley so quickly could only mean that the Yun family had been keeping tabs on Xie Shiyou all along.

After Xie Shiyou fled the Xie family, he had lived under a bridge and eaten swill. Since the Yun family had been secretly watching him but had not extended a helping hand, what did this imply?

It implied that the Yun family no longer considered the Xie family as relatives by marriage.

Chu Yi smiled slightly. "Release Xie Shiyou."

He wanted to see what the Yun family was planning. He didn’t mind lending a hand.

chapters.title: The Command of De Fei
chapters.content:
Soon, the auspicious hour arrived.

The wedding procession of Prince Anjing arrived at the Xie residence.

Xie Pin, supported by the matchmaker, walked out of her boudoir in a daze, reached the gate of the Xie residence, and was helped into the bridal sedan.

After entering the sedan, she lifted the red veil and peered through the gap in the curtain at the Xie family. She saw her grandfather and grandmother, her father and mother, Xie Shian, as well as the concubines and other siblings of the Xie family... It had only been four years since she was acknowledged and returned to the Xie family, yet she had already regarded this place as her home. She never expected to leave so soon.

Her heart was filled with melancholy and reluctance, but even more so, she yearned for her future life.

The sedan was lifted, moving further and further away from the Xie residence.

Xie Pin thought the sedan would go directly to the prince's mansion, but unexpectedly, after turning a corner on the street, it stopped at the gate of the Shi residence.

Prince Anjing personally entered the Shi family's gate and led the concubine, Miss Shi, into another bridal sedan.

The two sedans, one after the other, passed through the bustling streets, drawing much discussion among the commoners.

"Prince Anjing is truly fortunate to marry two women in one day. Come, let's make a bet. Who do you think Prince Anjing will spend the wedding night with?"

"Of course, it's Miss Xie, the principal wife. It's only natural for the wedding night to be with the principal wife."

"Not at all, not at all. The Shi family's status is much higher than the Xie family's. Prince Anjing will still need to rely on the Shi family's influence in the future. He will definitely give the Shi family enough face."

"You all say the funniest things. Prince Anjing marries two women in one day, yet the combined dowry of both is not as much as that of the Crown Princess or Princess Gongxi, not even a tenth."

Looking from the street, it was true. One was a principal wife, the other a concubine, yet the combined dowry of the two women was less than thirty-two palanquins.

Moreover, it seemed to be all household items, with nothing truly valuable.

"The Xie family is from a humble background. It's understandable they can't provide a dowry, but the Shi family..."

"Don't you know? The current mistress of the Shi family married in later. This Miss Shi is a stepdaughter. Which stepmother would prepare a dowry for a stepdaughter?"

"Prince Anjing is a royal prince. When the Emperor bestowed the title, he was rewarded with countless gold and silver treasures. Why would he care about his wife's dowry?"

"Prince Anjing, with such a noble status, married the daughter of a mere fifth-rank family. This shows that Prince Anjing truly admires Miss Xie and is a man of responsibility."

...

Xie Pin, sitting inside the bridal sedan, let out a sigh of relief.

She had no dowry, and neither did Concubine Shi. So she didn't have to feel inferior to Concubine Shi.

After about a quarter of an hour, the sedan stopped. The curtain was lifted, and the matchmaker helped her out of the sedan. She stepped over the threshold and entered the Prince Anjing's mansion.

In a daze, she performed the wedding rituals, her ears filled with various auspicious words, and then she was sent into the bridal chamber.

She sat in the joyous bridal chamber, not knowing how long she had been sitting. The distant bustling sounds gradually faded, and the night grew darker. The maids beside her yawned one after another, and even she herself couldn't sit still.

She lifted the red veil: "Go and see if the Prince is still drinking in the front courtyard."

The maid nodded and left. After a short while, she returned: "Miss, the Prince..."

Xie Pin coldly interrupted her: "What Miss? I am the Princess Consort now."

"Yes, Princess Consort." The maid spoke, "This servant asked around. The matrons in the mansion said the Prince went to Concubine Shi's residence."

Xie Pin yanked off the red veil, her face turning an extreme shade of livid.

She was the principal wife, the Princess Consort. The Prince did not come to fulfill the rituals with her but went to the concubine's place first. This was a slap in her face.

But she also knew that she had married before her coming-of-age ceremony. To avoid giving people a reason to talk, the Prince would definitely not come to her on the wedding night.

She took several deep breaths before suppressing her anger, then ordered the maid to help her wash up and go to bed.

The next morning, before dawn, the matrons of the prince's mansion came to wake her up. She had to go to the palace to pay respects to the Empress and De Fei.

Xie Pin had not slept well all night, her complexion was terrible. She applied a lot of powder to cover the exhaustion under her eyes and followed the matron to the front courtyard. Her husband, Prince Anjing, was practicing swordplay.

This was the first time Xie Pin had seen Prince Anjing wielding a sword, and she was momentarily captivated.

After Prince Anjing finished, she quickly took the handkerchief from the maid's hand and stepped forward to wipe the sweat for Prince Anjing: "Your Highness, you must be tired."

Prince Anjing glanced at her, took a step back, and coldly avoided her touch.

Then, he strode past her. She turned around and saw Concubine Shi approaching.

Prince Anjing walked to Concubine Shi's side, and the two stood facing each other, looking like a perfect couple. She, the legitimate Princess Consort, felt rather ridiculous in comparison.

She spoke: "Your Highness, it's getting late. We should enter the palace."

Prince Anjing nodded: "Concubine Shi will come along."

Xie Pin's fingers stiffened. She forced a smile: "For a concubine to enter the palace... it might not be appropriate."

"This is the command of this Prince's mother, De Fei." Prince Anjing glanced at her: "What, does the Princess Consort have any objections?"

Xie Pin's smile also froze.

De Fei must hate her to the core, deliberately summoning a concubine on the first day of the wedding.

From this day forward, everyone would know that she, Xie Pin, the daughter of the Xie family, was not respected by her husband nor liked by her mother-in-law. She had lost both face and dignity.

Prince Anjing coldly humphed and strode forward.

He regretted it to the extreme. He regretted not resisting the temptation that day and doing such a thing with this woman at Qing'an Temple...

He, a royal prince, was forced to marry a daughter from a fifth-rank commoner family as his principal wife, becoming the biggest joke in the entire capital.

Why should he give this woman any face? Why should he give her the respect due to a Princess Consort? Even if he didn't like Concubine Shi, he would still pretend to be affectionate with her just to spite Xie Pin...

"Princess Consort." Concubine Shi walked to Xie Pin's side and softly said, "De Fei and my late mother had some friendship. That's why she summoned me."

She was afraid that the Princess Consort and the Prince would grow apart, so she came to explain.

But Xie Pin coldly laughed: "Is Concubine Shi here to brag about your mother's close relationship with De Fei and try to suppress me, the Princess Consort?"

"No, of course not!" Concubine Shi quickly said, "What I meant was..."

"Enough, don't say any more."

Xie Pin impatiently curled her lip and turned to follow Prince Anjing's steps.

Concubine Shi bit her lip tightly and slowly followed the two. The carriage headed towards the imperial palace.

By the time they reached the palace gate and followed the eunuchs to the Kunning Palace where the Empress resided, the sky had just begun to brighten.

The three of them paid their respects to the Empress. The Empress rewarded Xie Pin with a jade ruyi and gave Concubine Shi a jade bracelet.

Xie Pin's face was filled with genuine gratitude as she thanked the Empress, finally showing the first smile since her marriage.

But when they arrived at De Fei's residence, she couldn't smile anymore. De Fei gave her only a golden hairpin, but turned and rewarded Concubine Shi with several bolts of fine brocade and a set of exquisite hair ornaments.

De Fei didn't even glance at her. She took Concubine Shi's hand: "This palace and your mother were close friends. The year this palace entered the palace to serve His Majesty, your mother married your father. Who could have imagined that your mother would pass away so young... Alas, it's just that making you a concubine is truly a waste of your talents..."

"I am not aggrieved." Concubine Shi hastily said, "The Princess Consort and I are like sisters. Being able to serve the Prince together with the Princess Consort is my fortune."

She intentionally mentioned the Princess Consort, hoping that De Fei would speak more with the Princess Consort.

But to Xie Pin's ears, these words were extremely grating.

---

chapters.title: The Hot Spring Villa Welcomes Guests
chapters.content:
De Fei coldly glanced at Xie Pin.

She had not ordered Xie Pin to be driven out, which was her magnanimity as a palace concubine, but it did not mean she accepted Xie Pin as her daughter-in-law.

She chatted warmly with Concubine Shi, but it did not mean she liked Concubine Shi.

These two women, one had schemed her way to the position of Princess Consort, and the other was a reluctant choice. It would be strange if she liked either of them.

The Xie family claimed to be from a humble background and had no dowry, which was acceptable.

The Shi family was even more ridiculous. That Madam Shi, fearing she would outshine the principal wife, had prepared a dowry as meager as the Xie family's.

She gave face to Concubine Shi only to force the Shi family to bring out the dowry that originally belonged to Concubine Shi.

"An open hot spring villa has been established in the suburbs of the capital. In a few days, you will accompany this palace to the villa to soak in the hot spring pools." De Fei smiled and said, "People say that the hot spring is extremely beneficial for women's health. You should soak more often and conceive a child for Lao Si as soon as possible."

Concubine Shi was in a dilemma, unsure whether to agree or not.

Xie Pin's teeth were almost ground to pieces.

She, the principal wife, had not conceived a child yet. How dare De Fei allow a mere concubine to become pregnant!

But she did not dare express her inner dissatisfaction and could only force a smile.

When De Fei took Concubine Shi to the hot spring villa, the villa had already become well-known to most people in the capital.

"People say there's a hot spring villa in the suburbs called 'Chu Yun Zhi Shang.' It's said to be much larger than the imperial hot spring pools."

"If it's larger than the imperial hot spring pools, why hasn't it been offered as tribute to His Majesty?"

"That hot spring is a bit far from the capital. If it were offered as tribute to His Majesty, he would rarely be able to visit. Moreover, I've heard that the person behind this hot spring villa is Prince Pingxi. His Majesty, as a father, wouldn't compete with his son for property."

"The royal family opened a hot spring villa, which is for the noble families to enjoy. How could commoners like us have a share? We can only watch the excitement."

"You're wrong there. My cousin works as a laborer at the villa. He told me long ago that the hot spring at Chu Yun Zhi Shang is particularly large, so it's divided into two separate gardens. One is exclusively for noble families, and the other garden has a large open-air hot spring pool. Us commoners can enjoy it for just a few coins."

"Really? Can commoners soak in hot springs?"

"Of course, it's true. If you don't believe me, let's go take a look together."

...

The idea of dividing it into two villas was proposed by Yun Chu.

The wealthy could enjoy the hot springs, and ordinary people with some spare money naturally wanted to experience it as well.

For the wealthy, exclusive pools and courtyards were built with strong privacy and higher prices.

For ordinary people, there was a large open-air pool, separated only by gender. Although the price was cheap, the large number of ordinary people made it a considerable income every day.

After the ice shop closed, the Chu Yun Zhi Shang hot spring villa opened.

Under the collaboration of Manager Cheng and Chen Defu, the hot spring villa made a name for itself in the capital on the very first day of business.

The individual courtyards required advance reservations, and they were already booked until the end of the year, with deposits exceeding ten thousand taels of silver.

The ordinary pools were cheap. Even in the dead of winter, it only cost 200 copper coins per person. As it was early autumn, the price was naturally lower, 80 coins allowed one to enter and experience soaking in a hot spring. Therefore, from morning till night, the entrance of the hot spring villa was bustling with a continuous stream of visitors.

Although the two villas were separated by only a wall, both sides of the wall were planted with large areas of peach blossoms, and the main gates opened in opposite directions, so they did not affect each other.

Tingshuang brought the account books from the first half-month of business to the Xie residence and carefully reported the situation at the villa during this period.

Yun Chu listened and nodded. With Manager Cheng's decisive actions and Old Chen's meticulous attention to detail, everything at the hot spring villa was going well. Of course, the main reason was that the person behind the villa was Prince Pingxi. With Prince Pingxi, whose name made countless bandits tremble in fear, no one dared to cause any trouble.

"Madam, something happened the other day." Tingshuang said, "Consort Yuan, by the grace of Her Majesty the Empress, left the palace and specially took people to the hot spring villa. When she passed by your small courtyard, she wanted to go in and take a look. Manager Cheng stopped her, and Consort Yuan slapped Manager Cheng across the face. Then, she entered your small courtyard's pool and started soaking in the hot spring..."

Yun Chu was not at all surprised by this.

Her small courtyard was different from the others. The entrance was filled with rare flowers and plants, and the pool was inlaid with various colored stones.

Originally, the courtyard had been filled with crape myrtles, but since she did not like them, Prince Pingxi had ordered them to be replaced with orchids and jasmine.

Such a unique courtyard naturally attracted Consort Yuan's attention.

Tingfeng was shocked: "Does Consort Yuan not know that the person behind the villa is Prince Pingxi? How dare she barge into a courtyard that clearly does not receive guests?"

"Consort Yuan thought this courtyard was prepared by His Highness for Concubine Yin. Consort Yuan considers herself more noble than Concubine Yin and is the birth mother of the Sixth Prince. Why would she care about Prince Pingxi?" Tingshuang said, "When Consort Yuan was soaking in the hot spring, Manager Cheng invited Prince Pingxi to the villa. Prince Pingxi arrived with two matrons. The two matrons completely ignored Consort Yuan's dignity and pulled her out of the pool..."

Tingxue covered her mouth: "Prince Pingxi's audacity is too great..."

Even Yun Chu was startled.

Although Consort Yuan was no longer a favored concubine, she was still one of the four consorts and the Emperor's woman, and she had given birth to a princess and a prince. Prince Pingxi's actions not only disrespected Consort Yuan but also trampled on the Emperor's dignity.

However, many days had passed, and she had not heard of any incidents in the imperial harem. It seemed that Consort Yuan had not made a big fuss about it, or perhaps it should be said that the Emperor, between Consort Yuan and Prince Pingxi, had chosen Prince Pingxi, and the matter had been suppressed.

Yun Chu changed the subject: "Tingshuang, take these fifty thousand taels of silver to Old Chen and have him command someone to build a large seafaring ship."

Tingshuang was surprised: "Madam, you intend to...?"

"When the ship is built, I plan to do some overseas business."

She could not place all her hopes of making money solely on the hot spring villa. If something unexpected happened, everything would be lost.

She remembered that in her previous life, some merchants had gone overseas and brought back many strange and rare goods to sell in the capital, each earning a fortune.

Foreign novelties were always the most popular goods in the capital. Merchants without ships could only purchase goods from traveling merchants, which cut their profits in half. It was better to build her own ship, import goods herself, and then transport them across the country.

Tingshuang nodded and took the order to handle it.

Yun Chu took stock of her savings. Selling ice alone had earned her 230,000 taels of silver. Building the hot spring villa had cost nearly 20,000 taels. She had given 50,000 taels to her father, allocated 50,000 taels for building the ship, and still had 110,000 taels left. This was a huge sum for any family.

She tapped the abacus and said, "Tingshuang, see if there are any quiet and elegant two or three-courtyard small houses for sale in the capital. Buy one before winter and hire skilled craftsmen to renovate it."

Once the matters with the Xie family were settled, she would need a place to live.

Although returning to the Yun family was an option, her brother and sister-in-law would not mind, over time, it might lead to unnecessary troubles.

Tingshuang noted everything down.

As they were speaking, a servant came to report that the eldest miss had returned.

chapters.title: The Hunting Invitation
chapters.content:
Yun Chu sat in the flower hall, lifting her gaze to look at Xie Pin, who walked in through the door.

After marriage, it was customary to return home for a three-day visit, but Xie Pin had not gone back. It didn’t take much thought to realize that Anjing Wang must have refused to accompany her, and Xie Pin, fearing gossip that she was not favored by her husband, had found an excuse to stay away.

Now, more than half a month had passed since Xie Pin’s marriage, and she appeared much more composed than before her wedding.

"Greetings, Wangfei."

Yun Chu stood up and performed a courtesy.

"Mother, please rise at once," Xie Pin hurried forward a few steps to help Yun Chu up. "I became Wangfei all thanks to you. If you still bow to me, how can I bear it?"

She spoke these words, but deep inside, a secret satisfaction bloomed.

Look at her, the legitimate eldest daughter of a first-rank general, and now even her own birth mother had to bow to her. It was proof enough of how noble her status had become.

She might be at a disadvantage before De Fei and Anjing Wang, but the Empress still gave her face. As for others, they were too busy flattering her to ever intentionally humiliate her.

Yun Chu, of course, sensed this hidden emotion.

"Pin’er looks well. It seems you are doing fine in the Wangfu," Yun Chu said with a faint smile. "Shi Ce Fei is a little older than you. It’s only natural for the Wangye to summon her to his bed. You must remember not to be jealous or make a scene."

She had rescued Du Ling’s younger sister, Du Ying, from the Anjing Wangfu, but she hadn’t expected Shi Jia’s eldest daughter to become a Ce Fei.

In her past life, this Shi family eldest daughter had been married off by the Shi family matriarch to a sixty-year-old man as his fourth wife. The old man had died just three months after the marriage, and his many children had immediately driven Shi Xiaojie out. The Shi family, ashamed of her, had severed all ties.

For most pampered young ladies, such humiliation would have been unbearable, and they might have chosen death. But Shi Xiaojie had sold the pitifully small dowry the Shi family had thrown out, reportedly for only three taels of silver, and rented a shabby house, where she began to make a living with odd jobs...

Later, Shi Xiaojie opened a teahouse, and her business thrived. Since Yun Chu enjoyed tea, she had specially instructed Tingxue to buy tea from Shi Xiaojie’s shop every few days, which was how she had heard about Shi Xiaojie’s story.

If, in this life, her schemes caused Shi Xiaojie to be implicated and die because of Anjing Wang, she would never find peace.

The only possible way out was this: after Anjing Wang’s downfall, more than a dozen concubines in his harem were released. Since most were from respectable families and had been forcibly taken, if Shi Ce Fei could be reduced to a concubine, she might have a chance to survive.

Thinking of this, Yun Chu continued, "Anjing Wang is of age but has no children. De Fei will certainly urge Shi Ce Fei to conceive as soon as possible. De Fei is not targeting you, so you must not hold a grudge. Do you understand?"

Xie Pin tightened her lips.

Mother was truly too clever. Without even meeting De Fei, she already understood De Fei’s plans.

A few days before the grand wedding, De Fei had sent palace matrons every day to deliver various medicines to Shi Ce Fei, claiming they would help her conceive a son immediately.

She was the legitimate Wangfei of Anjing Wang. She absolutely could not allow anyone to bear the Wangye’s child before her.

She lowered her eyelids and said, "Mother doesn’t know yet, but Shi Ce Fei has already been demoted to a concubine. She wrote disrespectful words about De Fei in her room, and the Wangye disapproved..."

Yun Chu’s fingers paused.

She had intended to provoke Xie Pin into taking action, but it seemed Xie Pin had already been unable to restrain herself. The wedding had only just taken place, and Shi Ce Fei had already fallen victim to her schemes.

There was no need for her to waste her breath then.

Seeing that Yun Chu remained silent, Xie Pin felt a flicker of unease. She quickly changed the subject: "Mother, I came back this time to share some good news. Every autumn, His Majesty arranges a royal hunt. This year, it’s scheduled for the 21st of September. The Wangfu is allowed three attendees, so I brought the extra invitation for you."

Yun Chu took the invitation and glanced at it. Indeed, it was for the palace’s annual royal hunt.

In her past life, the Fourth Prince, Anjing Wang, had met his end during this very hunt. From that moment on, the Anjing Wangfu ceased to exist.

She had thought Xie Pin might manage to be a proper Wangfei for a while, but she hadn’t expected the hunt to come so soon. The title of Anjing Wangfei was far more short-lived than she had imagined...

She smiled and said, "I won’t attend the hunt. You can give this invitation to An’ge."

Just then, Xie Shian entered through the door and said, "Mother, His Majesty has specially ordered all scholars from the Imperial College to accompany the hunt. I don’t need an invitation."

In the past, he had always needed his mother’s introductions to enter high society circles. But now, he was different. He could integrate himself among the noble families on his own. Even if those people looked down on him, he had won the favor of the Imperial College’s teachers. After school each day, they even gave him private lessons. For the upcoming provincial examinations, he was determined to win first place and make those who underestimated him take notice.

He paused before adding, "Families of first and second-rank officials are allowed to bring one female relative. Grandmother will likely attend, so since Eldest Sister has the invitation, why doesn’t Mother take it and go to keep Grandmother company?"

Yun Chu tugged at her lip.

She often returned to the Yun family and could see her mother anytime. There was no need to go to the hunting grounds just to talk.

She knew that these two siblings simply wanted to show her that their status had changed; that they could now take the lead in inviting her to places she couldn’t go before.

Before she could speak, Tingfeng rushed in: "Madam, someone from the palace has arrived. It’s the Empress who has sent an imperial decree for you."

Xie Shian and Xie Pin exchanged a glance before following Yun Chu to the front courtyard.

The messenger was a young eunuch, who respectfully addressed Yun Chu: "Madam Xie, by the decree of Her Majesty the Empress, you are invited to attend the royal hunt at Yan Mountain on the morning of the 21st of September, accompanied by the imperial procession. Please make preparations."

Yun Chu was somewhat surprised.

The Yun family had produced a palace concubine, but they were not close to any of the other concubines in the palace, including the Empress. Why would the Empress personally invite her to the hunt?

Still, the Empress’s decree could not be refused. No matter how many questions she had, she could only accept it respectfully.

Xie Shian’s fingers tightened.

He had assumed that his mother would not have the qualifications to attend the hunt and would need to rely on his sister’s invitation to gain entry.

But he never expected that the Empress would send a special decree, personally inviting his mother. This was an immense honor.

Xie Pin felt even more bitter.

She had become Wangfei thanks to her mother and had wanted to use her own status to invite her mother to the hunt.

But her mother didn’t need her at all.

She lowered her head, staring at the invitation in her hand. The more she looked at it, the more ridiculous it seemed. She threw it into Xie Shian’s arms: "You can give it to whichever classmate you want as a favor."

If Father were healthier, she could have given it to him. But as it was, it would just benefit an outsider.

Xie Shian nodded. During his time at Huai De Academy, he had met many people, including some young masters from official families. This was a good opportunity to strengthen those connections. Weren’t these the very networks he would need when he entered officialdom in the future?

---

chapters.title: He Xu Returns to the Capital
chapters.content:
Xie Shian took the invitation and went to visit his former classmates.

The carriage was blocked on the road, so he got out and walked. After a few steps, he spotted a familiar figure on the street.

His pupils contracted, and he quickly chased after the figure.

But the figure slipped through an alley and disappeared into some unknown shop, vanishing from sight.

Xie Shian looked up and found himself in front of a gambling den.

His expression darkened.

If he wasn’t mistaken, the figure he had just seen was He Xu, who had disappeared several months ago.

Although it was only a side profile, he was certain it was his biological maternal uncle, whose real name was He Xu.

The capital was investigating the He family’s affairs. He Xu appearing in the capital was extremely dangerous.

His biological mother had been forced to her death because of this, yet He Xu was still living so carefreely. If he were discovered, the consequences would be unthinkable...

Xie Shian made an immediate decision and entered the gambling den. Inside, the noise was deafening, and the place was packed with people. He searched the entire place but found no trace of He Xu.

He no longer had the mind to deliver the invitation to his classmates. He hurried back to the Xie residence.

He went to the study to find Xie Jingyu, but the servants said Xie Jingyu had not yet returned.

He knew that since his eldest sister had become Wangfei, his father had been ordered by the court to "end his mourning period early" and had been given a lucrative position.

Rumor had it that it was a coveted position in the Ministry of Revenue, where he was in charge of counting the treasury’s silver every day.

By nightfall, Xie Jingyu finally returned.

His health was already poor, and the continuous days of hard work had left him limping and hunched over. His left leg dragged along the ground as he walked, a far cry from the elegant demeanor of the former top scholar.

Yet his face glowed with energy, as if he were radiant.

Xie Shian quickly went to support his father, helping him sit in the study’s chair before pouring a cup of tea for him.

Xie Jingyu did not drink the tea immediately. Instead, he pulled a stack of silver notes from his sleeve, at least five or six thousand taels’ worth.

Xie Shian’s face showed disbelief: "Father, where did this money come from?"

After the old madam’s funeral, the Xie family had been nearly bankrupt. Otherwise, they wouldn’t have struggled to prepare a proper dowry for his eldest sister.

"I’ve been re-examining and reorganizing the Ministry of Revenue’s accounts for the past five years," Xie Jingyu said, his voice carrying a hidden excitement. "It turns out the previous accountants were utterly incompetent. Some entries were overstated, some understated. After recalculating, there was a surplus of 7,100 taels. I only took 5,000, and the remaining 2,100 was recorded in the public accounts."

Xie Shian frowned: "Father, you’ve only just taken over this position. Doing this now may not be wise."

Wouldn’t it be safer to wait until he had firmly established himself, until fewer people were watching him?

"You don’t understand."

Xie Jingyu shook his head.

He had obtained this lucrative position through the Prince of Pingxi’s connections. He had to produce results to earn the Prince of Pingxi’s trust.

From the 5,000 taels, he set aside half in his study and placed the other half in a box. Once the amount accumulated to a suitable figure, he would present the box to the Prince of Pingxi as a token of his loyalty.

Xie Shian opened his mouth to argue further but suddenly remembered something more important. He changed the subject: "Father, I think I saw He Xu on the street today."

"Really?" Xie Jingyu stood up abruptly. "Wasn’t he in debt for over 10,000 taels and fled the capital to escape his creditors?"

Xie Shian said in a low voice, "I saw him enter a gambling den, but I couldn’t find him. I’m not sure if I was mistaken."

How could He Xu, who owed so much money, dare to return to the capital, let alone enter a gambling den? Would the gambling den even let him in?

Perhaps he had been wrong.

"Whether you were mistaken or not, we cannot take this lightly," Xie Jingyu said, tapping his fingers on the table. "I will arrange for a few men to stake out the gambling den. If he appears, they will take him to a secluded place... Only the dead can keep secrets."

Xie Shian lowered his eyelids.

His biological mother had been driven to her death by his own father’s hands. His maternal uncle seemed to matter little in comparison.

But once he achieved success, once he held high office, once he restored the He family’s name, he would certainly establish eternal tablets for his mother and uncle, so that their descendants could honor them for generations...

Just as Xie Jingyu had arranged for men to go to the gambling den, Yun Chu’s people had already taken He Xu from the gambling den to a small courtyard where he was temporarily staying.

As soon as he entered the courtyard, He Xu saw Chen Defu sitting there drinking tea. He said, his face full of guilt, "Elder Chen, I was just out for a stroll. I didn’t go gambling..."

Back then, he had been nearly killed after being castrated, and it was Elder Chen who had saved him.

It was Elder Chen who had arranged for people to escort him back to his hometown in Ji Province.

He had grown tired of staying in Ji Province and wanted to return to the capital for some fun. It was Elder Chen who had given him travel expenses and arranged this comfortable residence for him.

He had only arrived the day before yesterday. Originally, he had planned to go to the Xie family to ask his sister, He Lingyuan, for some money to loosen her purse strings, but he hadn’t found her. So he had wandered into the gambling den. He was afraid that Elder Chen would be angry and abandon him, and then he would be finished.

"He Xu, do you know how close you came to losing your life?" Chen Defu said coldly. "I went through great trouble to save you because I wanted you to live, not to throw your life away so carelessly."

He Xu replied nonchalantly, "I still owe the gambling den so much silver. They won’t kill me; at most, I’ll get a beating."
