Chen Defu shook his head. "The one who wants you dead is Xie Shian, the eldest young master of the Xie family."

"What? Xie Shian?" He Xu frowned. "How could he possibly want to kill me? Elder Chen, you must be mistaken."

After all, he was An’ge’s maternal uncle. Blood was thicker than water.

"You were raised by my own hands, so I won’t hide the truth from you," Chen Defu said, looking at him. "You and Concubine He of the Xie family are full-blooded siblings, aren’t you?"

He Xu’s eyes tightened. "How do you know that?"

"I also know that Concubine He is the biological mother of Xie Shian, Xie Shian’s younger brother, and Xie Pin. I know even more; that Concubine He was the legitimate daughter of the He family." Chen Defu’s voice was low. "The Xie family has offended someone powerful. That person is investigating the He family’s affairs, preparing to deliver a fatal blow to the Xie family... Therefore, Concubine He, as a key witness, was forced to her death by Xie Jingyu and Xie Shian working together... They have been searching for you. As soon as you returned to the capital, you were spotted. The next person to die will be you!"

"No, that’s impossible!" He Xu’s face changed dramatically. "My sister was tough. She couldn’t have died. You’re lying to me!"

"Ah—" Chen Defu sighed deeply. "If you don’t believe me, then wait and see for yourself. I’ve said all I can."

He patted He Xu’s shoulder and walked out.

At the entrance of the small courtyard, he turned to the two guards in the shadows and said, "Watch him closely. Do not let him die."

After keeping an eye on He Xu for several months, the time to use him was almost here. He just didn’t know if the Xie family could bear the weight of the special gift Madam Yun had prepared for them.

chapters.title: Departure for the Hunting Grounds
chapters.content:
In the blink of an eye, it was September 21st.

Before dawn, Yun Chu got up, washed, dressed, and packed her spare clothes. Taking Qiu Tong with her, she boarded a carriage bound for the palace gates.

Xie Shian did not accompany her. Instead, he went to the Imperial College to meet his classmates and travel with them.

By the time Yun Chu arrived at the palace gates, many people had already gathered, high-ranking officials of the first and second ranks, along with their families, all set to join the hunting expedition at Yan Mountain.

"Chu Chu." A voice sounded by her ear.

Yun Chu turned to see Du Ling, her face lighting up with a smile. "Ling Ling, you look so dashing today."

Du Ling chuckled. "Last year, I fell ill during the hunt. This year, I’ve made up my mind to stand out. But you; why are you wearing such a long skirt? I was hoping to compete with you."

"Spare me," Yun Chu raised her hands in surrender. "The journey to Yan Mountain is exhausting enough. Where would I find the energy to compete with you?"

She had only been allowed to come because of the Empress’s decree. The Empress must have something to say to her.

The Empress was no simple woman. She had managed to protect the Crown Prince in the Eastern Palace for over twenty years. Even when the Second Prince’s influence had grown overwhelming, the Crown Prince’s position remained unshaken. As Empress, she must have extraordinary means.

Yun Chu had been pondering, if the Empress intended to win over the Yun family, how should she refuse?

With so much on her mind, she had no energy left for horseback riding, archery, or hunting.

As they spoke, the palace gates opened. The imperial procession emerged in grand fashion, led by the Emperor, followed by the Empress and the Crown Prince, then several concubines and many imperial princes. Only after the royal family had taken their place at the front did the officials and their families follow in order of rank.

The procession quickly swelled to what looked like two or three thousand people.

As a fifth-rank lady, Yun Chu had the lowest status and naturally brought up the rear. Du Ling, wanting to keep her company, linked arms with her. "I’ll ride in your carriage. It’s a three-hour journey, and I’m already tired. We can chat along the way."

Yun Chu nodded. Three hours was half a day, indeed, traveling alone would be dull.

Du Ling quickly boarded the carriage and lifted the curtain, only to find two small children sitting obediently inside. She blinked in surprise. "Chu Chu, did the Empress’s decree say you had to bring children?"

Yun Chu shook her head. "No."

Du Ling pressed her temples. She didn’t understand, if the Empress hadn’t ordered it, why was Chu Chu bringing bastards along to the hunting grounds?

That scoundrel Xie Jingyu kept taking concubines, one after another, and fathering children left and right. Yet Chu Chu still promoted his illegitimate children...

But these two bastards were unusually good-looking, far beyond her expectations for illegitimate children. Unable to resist, she reached out and pinched the boy’s cheek.

"Ah—"

Chu Hongyu cried out in displeasure.

But that didn’t matter.

What mattered was, why were there other people in his mother’s carriage?

That unreliable servant, A Mao; had he gotten the wrong information?

Yun Chu, standing outside the carriage, was puzzled by Du Ling’s question when she suddenly heard a familiar voice.

She quickly climbed into the carriage and saw the two well-behaved children inside.

"Mother... Aunt Yun!"

Chu Hongyu realized there was a stranger present and stopped himself just in time, restraining the urge to pounce on Yun Chu.

Du Ling was stunned. "Aunt? Chu Chu, who are they—"

Yun Chu gently pushed Du Ling into the carriage. Only after the curtain fell did she explain, "This is the young heir of Pingxi, and this is the young lady."

"No wonder they looked familiar..." Du Ling had a sudden realization. She had only seen the children from afar at banquets, and since children changed so much day by day, she hadn’t recognized them.

"Ah, so it’s the young heir and the young lady." Du Ling smiled. "Shouldn’t you two be in the imperial procession? How did you end up in the Xie family’s carriage? Did you get on the wrong one?"

Chu Hongyu tilted his head. "Madam, you know this is the Xie family’s carriage. Then why are *you* here?"

Du Ling found his mannerisms too adorable. Laughing, she replied, "Because I’m close friends with Madam Xie. We agreed to share a carriage."

"I’m also close friends with Madam Xie." The little boy lifted his chin. "I even went to the Kunning Palace and had the Empress issue a decree for Madam Xie to join the hunt."

Yun Chu was surprised. "Because of *you*, the Empress sent me a decree?"

The little boy nodded proudly. "I said Madam Xie crushed my cricket. I wanted to collect my debt, so the Empress agreed."

The hunting trip would last a full five days. He and Changsheng could spend five whole days with their mother. Such an opportunity was too rare to miss.

Yun Chu: ...

This little rascal could have told her sooner. She had been under the impression that the Empress wanted to win over the Yun family and had spent all this time worrying about it...

But now that she understood, she could stop fretting over the Empress and relax on the way to Yan Mountain.

She reached out and pulled the silent little girl, Chu Changsheng, into her arms, softly saying, "The journey is long. Lean on Auntie and rest for a while."

The little girl nodded, wrapped her arms around Yun Chu’s neck, and contentedly nestled against her chest.

Chu Hongyu’s eyes turned green with jealousy.

But he knew his sister was frail. It had taken great effort to convince his father to let her leave the house. He wouldn’t compete with her over such a small matter.

Du Ling had a son and daughter of her own. Seeing the boy’s expression, she knew what he was thinking. Smiling, she scooped him up and placed him on her lap. "Young heir, you can lean on me and rest. By the time you wake up, we’ll have arrived."

"No, I don’t want to!"

Chu Hongyu had barely touched Du Ling’s leg before scrambling away with all his might.

He refused to be held by any woman other than his mother.

Clinging to Yun Chu’s arm, he pouted, "Aunt Yun, when we get there, will you hold me for a while too? Please?"

Yun Chu ruffled his hair. "Of course."

Du Ling, exasperated, said, "Young heir, do I have thorns on me or something?"

Chu Hongyu did his best to remain polite. "Madam, we’re not familiar, so I won’t trouble you."

Du Ling nudged Yun Chu’s arm. "When did you and these two get so close?"

Yun Chu couldn’t quite say.

When *had* they gotten so close?

Their first meeting had been unpleasant, but somehow, her heart had become inexplicably tied to these two children, and she could no longer let go.

She looked down at the children. "This is my close friend, Madam Ji, née Du. You can call her Aunt Du."

Chu Hongyu immediately sweetly called out, "Aunt Du! My sister can’t talk, so I’ll say it for her too, Aunt Du!"

"Then I won’t be polite and refuse." Du Ling’s heart melted. "I didn’t bring anything special, but this bracelet is for the young lady, and this jade pendant is for the young heir. Consider them a greeting gift."

Chu Hongyu glanced at Yun Chu. Seeing her nod, he reached out to accept. "Thank you, Aunt Du."

Yun Chu took out a small bundle and removed two pendants she had designed herself. They were made from the raw jade the Prince of Pingxi had given her before.

The red jade pendants each bore one of their names, engraved with auspicious clouds and flourishing flowers; designs she had drawn herself and commissioned a craftsman to carve.

The children were overjoyed when they received the pendants. Chu Hongyu examined his from every angle, unable to look away. Suddenly, his fingers stilled. Tilting his head, he asked, "Aunt Yun, didn’t you make one for Father too?"

Yun Chu: ...

---

chapters.title: A Preposterous Possibility
chapters.content:
Yun Chu pressed her forehead.

She had made three identical pendants. If she had made one for the Prince of Pingxi as well, what would that have looked like?

But such things couldn’t be explained to a four-year-old child.

She pulled out another bundle and smiled. "I used the remaining jade to make a set of jewelry for Changsheng and a jade ornament for you."

"Wow, I love it!" Chu Hongyu’s face lit up with delight. He had already forgotten about his father. "I’ll hang this jade ornament on the sword Grandfather Emperor gave me. It’ll look amazing."

The little girl twirled her jewelry, dancing with joy.

Yun Chu spoke gently, "Changsheng, let me help you put it on to try."

It was a set of bejeweled hairpieces with gold and jade, suitable for a girl who had just come of age. Since Changsheng was still young, Yun Chu only pinned two floral hairpins in her hair.

Chu Hongyu clapped. "So pretty! Sister looks so pretty."

Du Ling studied them and said, "Chu Chu, I remember when you came of age, you wore a similar set of bejeweled hairpieces. The young lady looks so much like you... Especially her eyes, they’re *exactly* alike. The more I look, the more I feel you and the young lady resemble each other. The nose, the mouth, the shape of your faces..."

Yun Chu’s fingers froze.

Her mother and elder sister-in-law had once remarked that she and Changsheng looked alike.

Now Du Ling was saying the same.

Not long ago, at the hot spring villa, she had accidentally eaten wild mushrooms and fallen unconscious. The Prince of Pingxi had mentioned that Changsheng had also suffered a serious accident with wild mushrooms as a child.

Four years ago, in the snow, she had given birth to twins.

That same year, the Prince of Pingxi had gained a son and a daughter.

An incredible thought suddenly struck Yun Chu.

Could it be...?

It was too absurd...

Her hands trembled uncontrollably.

She closed her eyes and took several deep breaths, but the blood rushing in her chest refused to calm.

" Aunt Yun, what’s wrong? Are you unwell?"

Chu Hongyu’s voice was filled with concern.

She opened her eyes and saw her own face reflected in the child’s large, worried eyes. In his world, it seemed there was only her...

She forced a smile. "I heard your father say you and Changsheng were born in winter. When is your birthday? Tell me in advance so I can prepare gifts."

"I don’t know." Chu Hongyu blinked. "I don’t want any gifts. I just want Aunt Yun to be with me that day."

Yun Chu looked at him. "Then when we arrive, ask your father which day you were born, alright?"

Chu Hongyu nodded vigorously.

It was already autumn. By the coldest time of winter, it would be his and Changsheng’s fifth birthday. With Aunt Yun there, it would be a very special day.

The children, being so young, soon fell asleep in the swaying carriage.

One slept in Yun Chu’s arms, the other on Du Ling’s lap.

Du Ling spoke softly, "Chu Chu, are you and the Prince of Pingxi’s household this close? Is this the Yun family’s choice?"

Yun Chu replied, "I’m a married woman. My actions don’t represent the Yun family."

"But will the Empress see it that way?" Du Ling asked. "The young heir specifically went to the palace to request the Empress’s decree to invite you. The two children even came to your carriage. The Empress is bound to notice. She’ll assume the Yun family has sided with the Prince of Pingxi."

Yun Chu looked at her. "And what about the Du family, the Ji family? Which side have they chosen?"

Du Ling sighed. "The Du and Ji families don’t wish to involve themselves in the struggle for the throne. But no matter who we refuse, the other side will assume we’ve joined their opponent. Inadvertently, we offend every prince. My father’s stance is to remain loyal to whichever prince the Emperor chooses as Crown Prince. Whoever becomes Crown Prince, the Ji and Du families will support."

Yun Chu shook her head.

In her past life, when she died, the Crown Prince’s power had been weak. The Empress had barely managed to keep him in place, and it was only a matter of time before he was replaced. When the Crown Prince fell, the Du family would likely fall with him...

As someone who had been reborn, her previous life had been too short. She only knew which princes had failed, but not who had ultimately ascended the throne.

Choosing a side was a gamble with fate for her as well.

One wrong move, and all would be lost.

"Why are we even talking about this?" Du Ling changed the subject. "This isn’t something we women should worry about. Help me see, how can I make my hairpiece look even better?"

Yun Chu had to admire her friend’s carefree nature. She laughed. "It’s already perfect."

"When I’m with you, the most beautiful woman in the capital, how can I not pay attention to my appearance? I can’t let you outshine me." Du Ling adjusted her hair. "Oh, right, Ying’s marriage has been arranged."

Du Ying’s future husband was the son of a third-rank Left Deputy Censor of the Censorship Court, a very good family background.

Yun Chu thought for a moment but couldn’t recall this family’s fate in her past life. Still, it was certainly better than becoming the Princess Consort of Anjing.

The two chatted idly, covering all sorts of topics, until they finally arrived at Yan Mountain.

This was imperial land. Every autumn, the court gathered here for the hunt. The mountain had long been enclosed, and dangerous beasts like tigers and leopards had been driven out. Only herbivores and small game like rabbits and pheasants remained.

The servants began setting up camp, while the nobles prepared for the hunt.

Yun Chu silently stood at the edge of the crowd. She couldn’t understand how these people still had so much energy. After half a day of jostling in the carriage, her body felt like it was falling apart. How could they still have the strength to hunt...?

The Emperor, mounted on a tall horse, declared, "There’s less than an hour until sunset. We’ll set a time limit of one incense stick. Whoever hunts the most game will receive a reward from me."

The princes, high officials, and the young masters of noble families all cheered in response, creating a lively atmosphere.

Yun Chu spotted the Prince of Anjing among those following the Emperor. Dressed in riding attire, he looked spirited and energetic. Xie Pin’s eyes seemed glued to him.

She also saw the Prince of Pingxi. Among the imperial princes, he stood out. While the other princes were scholars, the Crown Prince was highly talented, the Second Prince was renowned for his wisdom, the Fourth Prince was still slight of build, and the others were even younger, the Prince of Pingxi was tall and straight, robust without being burly, imposing without being bulky. It was clear he was a man of martial arts...

As she watched, the man on the horse suddenly turned his gaze toward her.

She started; she had unconsciously been staring at the Prince of Pingxi for quite a while.

She quickly forced a smile and pointed to the side, indicating to the Prince of Pingxi that the two children had been taken away by a nurse.

The Prince of Pingxi’s lips curved into a smile in response.

"Third Brother?" The Prince of Gongxi looked at him, unable to help but ask, "I think this is the first time I’ve seen Third Brother smile like this."

The Third Prince was always cold and aloof. Of course, he *did* smile sometimes; but it was either a cold smirk or a faint, detached smile, never reaching his eyes.

But now, this smile was genuine, radiating from within. His brows and eyes were filled with joy.

chapters.title: Concubine Yin’s Probe
chapters.content:
On Yan Mountain, steeds galloped.

The Emperor, accompanied by the Empress, the princes, meritorious nobles, young masters, and others, began the first hunt.

Some noble ladies interested in hunting also rode along swiftly on horseback. Left in the camp were only a few palace concubines and women like Yun Chu, who felt a bit weary.

Yun Chu sat under a tree, watching from afar as two children ate snacks attended by palace maids.

At this moment, a matron approached her.

"Madam Xie, Her Grace Concubine Yin invites you for tea."

Yun Chu’s fingers paused for a moment.

She roughly guessed why Concubine Yin wanted to speak with her. She had collaborated with the Prince of Pingxi to open a hot spring estate. It was reasonable for Concubine Yin to ask a few questions about it.

She followed the matron to the imperial tents.

Under the swift efforts of hundreds of palace maids and eunuchs, dozens of imperial tents had been set up. This setup was no less impressive than a temporary palace.

Several older palace concubines had not gone hunting and were resting in their tents.

When Yun Chu entered Concubine Yin’s tent, she saw Concubine Yin speaking with a girl around sixteen or seventeen.

The girl had delicate eyebrows, a round face, and was very charming. Whatever they were discussing had made the girl’s face flush crimson.

"Miss Fang, come here." Concubine Yin smiled, removing a bracelet from her wrist. "This is my gift to you for our first meeting. Keep it well."

Miss Fang seemed a bit flustered and dared not accept it.

Concubine Yin directly placed it on her wrist.

Last time, she had chosen Miss Tan for the Third Prince, but unfortunately, that young scoundrel Yu’er had ruined it.

This time, before the Emperor bestowed a marriage, she absolutely would not let another unmarried girl interact with the two children...

After Miss Fang expressed her gratitude and left, Yun Chu stepped forward and curtsied. "This concubine greets Her Grace Concubine Yin."

"Madam Xie, please sit." Concubine Yin smiled. "This is the first time we’ve formally met, isn’t it?"

Yun Chu sat down, only perching on the edge of the seat, and lowered her head. "Yes."

"I heard from the Third Prince that the hot spring estate above Chu Yun is under your name, Madam Xie." Concubine Yin took a sip of tea and casually said, "I had someone look into it. It turns out you acquired that estate from a merchant for a few thousand taels of silver. How about this: I’ll offer twenty thousand taels, and you can transfer the estate to the Third Prince’s name."

Yun Chu was taken aback. She truly hadn’t expected Concubine Yin to want to buy her estate.

Just because she had taken the initiative to collaborate with the Prince of Pingxi didn’t mean she had only that one collaborator.

She was only stunned for a moment before smiling. "Thanks to Her Majesty the Empress’s invitation, I have the honor to join the hunt at Yan Mountain. I was just thinking about what gift to prepare for Her Majesty. I wonder if Her Grace Concubine Yin could offer some advice?"

Concubine Yin had been wearing an expression of strategic confidence, but upon hearing Yun Chu’s words, she almost dropped the cup in her hand.

She understood what Madam Xie meant: if she insisted on buying the estate, then this woman before her wouldn’t mind collaborating with the Empress and the Crown Prince.

If it truly came to that, then the Third Prince’s slight connection with the Yun family would be gone.

"The Empress enjoys fragrances." Concubine Yin smoothly shifted to a new topic. "I’ve heard that your mother, Madam Yun, is skilled in blending perfumes. The Empress particularly likes the orchid fragrance she creates."

Yun Chu smiled. "Thank you for the guidance, Your Grace."

As they were speaking, the tent’s curtain was lifted. Before anyone could be seen, a voice rang out: "Imperial Grandmother!"

Immediately after, Chu Hongyu rushed in like a cannonball and crashed into Concubine Yin’s arms.

"Oh, my dear!" Concubine Yin looked at the child in her arms with affection. "I’ve prepared a pony for you. Would you like to try hunting?"

Chu Hongyu’s eyes lit up. "Really?"

Concubine Yin nodded. "You can, but Changsheng cannot. Don’t tire her out."

Even without her saying so, Chu Hongyu knew he couldn’t take his sister horseback riding.

The little guy’s eyes rolled as he looked at Yun Chu. "Madam Xie is the legitimate eldest daughter of the Yun family. General Yun is so impressive on the battlefield. I’m sure Madam Xie is just as skilled. How about we have a little contest?"

Yun Chu: "..."

This kid really knew how to put on an act.

Fortunately, he knew how to disguise their overly intimate relationship in public.

She stood up. "How could I refuse the Young Master’s invitation? Please, lead the way."

Chu Hongyu puffed out his little chest and strode forward. Yun Chu bid farewell to Concubine Yin before leaving the tent.

Concubine Yin’s smile gradually faded.

Outside, Chu Hongyu saw the white pony brought by the guards and was overjoyed. He quickly had someone help him mount the horse.

His father was a military man, and he had loved these things since he was little. He could ride on a horse’s back at three and was already a good rider at four.

He said to the guards beside him, "You all stay behind. Madam Xie, I’ll go ahead."

Yun Chu hadn’t planned to hunt and hadn’t brought a horse. She had to borrow one from someone else, mounted it, and caught up with the pony ahead.

Chu Hongyu rode faster and faster, but his pony was too small. No matter how fast it went, it was slow. Soon, Yun Chu caught up, along with a group of guards.

He huffed, "I told you not to follow me! All of you, stay back!"

Yun Chu spoke up. "With me here, the Young Master will be safe. You can fall back a bit. It’s fine."

The guards exchanged glances before slowing down and following at a distance.

Once he was sure the guards couldn’t hear them, the little guy sweetly called out, "Mother!"

Yun Chu deliberately kept a straight face. "Don’t call me that."

"I’ll call you that when no one’s around." Chu Hongyu grinned. "My goal is to catch two foxes and make two scarves. One for Mother, and one for Changsheng."

Hearing this, Yun Chu couldn’t help but laugh.

This kid had just learned to ride a horse. Archery while riding was a high-difficulty skill he couldn’t possibly manage. He was just boasting.

She said, "I won’t need the scarf. Look over there, so many flowers. Let’s go pick some. We can make a flower crown for Changsheng."

The two dismounted and walked hand in hand to the sea of flowers.

These were wildflowers of unknown names, red, purple, white, and blue in various colors.

The little guy happily picked flowers while Yun Chu focused on weaving the flower crown. Suddenly, she heard voices speaking.

"Young Master Xie, you’re just riding a horse without shooting any arrows. Don’t tell me you can’t even shoot? Ha ha ha!"

The Sixth Prince sat on a large horse, looking back at Xie Shian behind him with a face full of mockery.

He led the way, and a group of spoiled young masters followed suit with their taunts.

"Young Master Xie is so good at his studies, but he can’t even shoot an arrow. How stupid."

"Tsk tsk, if you can’t shoot, what are you doing at a hunting ground? You’re just here to embarrass yourself."

"If you can’t hunt, get off the horse. Get down, get down!"

Previously, at the Imperial Academy, these people had to be cautious because of the teachers. Now, with no one else around, they all let loose, surrounding Xie Shian and mocking him endlessly.

---

chapters.title: Delivering a Weapon in the Dead of Night
chapters.content:
Xie Shian sat on the horse, gripping the reins tightly.

He had spent his childhood studying, only studying. No one had taught him to ride or shoot, and he hadn’t learned on his own.

After confirming he would attend the hunt, he had specially gone to the market to pick a good horse. He had asked his father to hire a teacher to teach him archery.

But time was too short. In just over ten days, he had only learned to ride. Archery was too difficult; it required more time to master the technique.

He had long anticipated that this group would make things difficult for him.

Expected troubles were naturally easier to handle. He loosened the reins and dismounted.

"Young Master Xie, just follow behind us and pick up the prey for us, ha ha ha!"

The Sixth Prince laughed loudly and whipped Xie Shian’s horse, startling it into a run. The others burst into laughter as well.

The group rode off, and Xie Shian pressed his lips together, chasing after them on foot.

"Mother, is he your eldest son?" Chu Hongyu crouched in the flowers and asked. "He’s being bullied. Why don’t you help him?"

Yun Chu smiled.

Xie Shian was not like other twelve-year-old boys. He knew exactly what he wanted and would stop at nothing to achieve it.

Now it was the Sixth Prince humiliating him, but once he stood firm, the Sixth Prince would be the one to suffer a major setback.

However, Xie Shian probably wouldn’t get that chance.

Yun Chu and Chu Hongyu picked many flowers and made two flower crowns before riding back.

The hunting party had also returned. Without a doubt, the Prince of Pingxi had taken first place, having hunted more than a dozen prey, including a live rabbit.

The Emperor was delighted and awarded the prize to the Prince of Pingxi on the spot.

The other princes all came forward to offer their congratulations.

The atmosphere was friendly and harmonious.

Night slowly fell, and campfires were lit. Everyone had dinner by the fire.

Yun Chu and Lin were preparing to enter Consort Yun’s tent when Xie Pin walked over with a smile. "Grandmother, Mother, I’d like to pay my respects to Her Grace Consort Yun as well."

Lin’s expression turned indifferent.

The divorce between Chu and Xie Jinyu was already a done deal. It was just that Chu had said she would find a good opportunity, so they hadn’t taken action yet.

These illegitimate children of the Xie family would have no further connection to Chu in the future. There was no need to indulge them.

"You are now the Princess Consort of Anning, a member of De Consort’s household. It’s not appropriate for you to pay respects to Consort Yun at this time." Lin said coolly. "If outsiders see this, they might think De Consort and Consort Yun are on the same side, which would unnecessarily invite suspicion from Her Majesty the Empress."

Xie Pin’s face stiffened. "I-I didn’t consider that. My apologies."

De Consort didn’t take her seriously at all, and now she had to avoid suspicion with Consort Yun. She felt her future was bleak.

Lin took Yun Chu directly into Consort Yun’s tent.

Consort Yun was a general’s daughter. Years ago, she and Yun Chu’s father, Yun Silin, had trained in martial arts together under the old general. Riding and archery were no problem for her. However, since the Empress enjoyed hunting, Consort Yun had given up this hobby. Even at Yan Mountain, she had not joined the Emperor in the hunting field.

Before Lin and Yun Chu could bow, Consort Yun quickly supported them and pulled them to sit. "It’s just the three of us in the tent. No need for formalities."

She paused before saying, "My elder brother wrote to me, saying that Chu had a bad dream where our entire Yun family was executed?"

Lin nodded. "Many things from Chu’s dream have come true in reality."

Originally, she hadn’t known about the dream, as the men of the Yun family believed such matters were not necessary to share with women.

It was Chu’s father who suddenly mentioned the divorce from the Xie family. After persistent questioning, she found out about that dream...

"Elder Brother said that in Chu’s dream, the Eighth Prince died..." Consort Yun’s heart trembled. "Chu, when you first said to ask me to agree to let the Eighth Prince go to his fief early, was it because of this dream?"

Yun Chu nodded, then shook her head. "I originally thought that if we escaped the vortex of the struggle for the throne, the Yun family might have a chance to survive. But after discussing with Grandfather, Father, and Elder Brother, I realized that once the Yun family reached this position, it would never be possible to remain uninvolved. So I have to ask, Aunt, have you ever considered letting the Eighth Prince take that position?"

Consort Yun was so shocked her pupils contracted. She quickly looked toward the tent’s entrance.

"Autumn Tong is outside. It’s fine." Yun Chu said. "If Aunt has such thoughts, then the Yun family is willing to fight for it."

Consort Yun’s face showed a bitter smile. "The Yun family does have the strength to say such things, but... the Eighth Prince’s temperament is not suited for that position. Even if he ascended, he wouldn’t be able to hold it steadily. Why go through such suffering?"

Lin understood the Eighth Prince well. He was too pure and kind.

Royal descendants usually developed scheming minds by the age of five or six, but the Eighth Prince, at ten years old, was still as pure as could be.

She spoke, "Then listen to Chu. You should apply for the Eighth Prince to be enfeoffed and sent to his fief as soon as possible, to leave the capital, this place of strife and discord."

Consort Yun’s eyelashes trembled, and she nodded in agreement.

The Eighth Prince was ten now. He would have to be at least twelve to be enfeoffed. She still had at least two years... She needed to plan carefully.

After leaving Consort Yun’s tent, Yun Chu and Lin returned to their own camps.

They were not members of the royal family, so their tents were in another area.

As soon as Yun Chu entered her tent and was about to freshen up, Autumn Tong lifted the curtain and entered. "Madam, the Prince of Pingxi requests your presence outside for a discussion."

It was already the end of the Xu hour (around 9 PM). Most people were exhausted and had already rested. The area around the camp was very quiet.

Yun Chu didn’t know why the Prince of Pingxi had come to see her so late.

But if there was something important to discuss, this was indeed the best time, as they wouldn’t be seen by others.

She changed into a set of dark clothes and exited the tent. A servant named Chengxu, who attended Chu Yi, was waiting at the tent’s entrance. Upon seeing her, he respectfully said, "Madam Xie, please follow me."

He walked ahead with his head lowered, constantly complaining in his mind.

Their prince had always been a gentleman. Since he had followed the prince, he had never seen the prince arrange a private meeting with a woman.

Even if there was an extremely important matter to discuss, it shouldn’t be at such a late hour, and it shouldn’t be in such a remote place... If he didn’t trust the prince’s character, he might have suspected the prince of having improper intentions.

Yun Chu followed Chengxu to a lake in the mountains.

The grass and trees here were lush, reaching knee height. The lake’s surface reflected the moonlight and sparse stars. A torch was inserted nearby, making a crackling sound as it burned.

Chengxu lowered his head and retreated. Autumn Tong stood guard not far away.

Only Yun Chu and Chu Yi remained.

"Greetings, Your Highness."

Chu Yi turned around. "No need for formalities."

"Last time, General Yun asked me to find a weapon for you. I searched high and low but couldn’t find a suitable weapon for a woman. So, I had one made." He handed over what he was holding. "Take a look. Do you like it?"

"Thank you for your trouble, Your Highness."

Yun Chu truly hadn’t expected him to bring her a weapon.

She took the item. It was an exquisite short sword, about the length of a woman’s forearm, small enough to be hidden in a sleeve.

She drew the sword. The sharp blade gleamed with a cold light under the moonlight.

She tested it and found the short sword very comfortable in her hand. She plucked a strand of her hair and swung the sword, easily cutting the hair.

"I love it! Thank you, Your Highness!"

Yun Chu genuinely liked the well-suited weapon and couldn’t help but try a few more swings.

"Miss Yun, this short sword has another special feature."

"What special feature?"

Yun Chu was so focused on examining the weapon that she didn’t notice the change in his form of address.

chapters.title: Improper Conduct
chapters.content:
Chu Yi’s gaze fell on Yun Chu’s face.

The night was pitch black, yet her face seemed to glow in the darkness, her two eyes like black gemstones, impossible to look away from.

Actually, the weapon could have been delivered at any time. If he truly couldn’t spare the time, he could have sent a servant to the Xie residence.

But he had deliberately chosen this hour, this place, and asked her to come in the dead of night.

His intentions were no longer hidden.

But he had to hide them well.

"Look here, on the right side of the short sword, is there a protruding round dot?"

Under the moonlight, Yun Chu indeed saw the small dot. It was a tiny red jade stone, and it seemed pressable.

She looked up. "Your Highness, what happens if I press it?"

Chu Yi clearly saw his own reflection in her eyes.

This feeling pleased him.

A faint smile unconsciously curled his lips.

He took two steps toward Yun Chu, then stood beside her, both of them facing the lake.

He reached out and placed his hand on the sword’s hilt.

As the man’s scorching palm approached, Yun Chu couldn’t help but startle.

She suddenly realized; they were standing far too close.

This was improper.

Before she could react, the man’s low, husky voice sounded in her ear: "Press it like this."

As he spoke, his hot breath fell on Yun Chu’s cheek. Her breath hitched, and she pressed down with her thumb. With a *whoosh*, the tip of the short sword suddenly shot out a silver dart, about the length of a little finger.

The short sword instantly plunged into the water, and soon, a dead fish floated to the surface.

Yun Chu was stunned. "How many times can it be pressed?"

Chu Yi replied, "Three times."

As soon as he spoke, his breath brushed against her ear, making her entire body uncomfortable.

She quickly took a few steps to the side, found an angle, and tried it. The short sword’s tip immediately fired a second dart, embedding itself deep into the trunk of a nearby tree.

Yun Chu walked over and tried to pull the dart out, but it had sunk in too deep; two-thirds of it was buried, and she couldn’t budge it at all.

"I’ve had a box of these darts made. In a few days, I’ll have them delivered to the Yun residence." Chu Yi walked over, pulled the dart from the tree trunk, then slowly reinstalled it before handing it back to her. "I hope you’ll never have to use them."

Yun Chu took it, and once again couldn’t help but express her gratitude. "Thank you, Your Highness."

She came from a martial family and had seen countless weapons since childhood, but this was the first time she had ever seen such an exquisitely crafted short sword.

Normally, a short sword was used for self-defense in close combat. But Prince Pingxi had hidden a clever mechanism inside; besides close combat, it could also be used for ranged attacks. The element of surprise made it easy to gain the upper hand in a confrontation.

"Does Your Highness perhaps need something?"

She felt a pang of regret. Last time, she should have kept some of that raw jade. Maybe she could have had something made to give him.

Chu Yi coughed lightly. "If Miss Yun truly wishes to thank me, then over the next few days, I ask that you take care of the two children. If I’m not mistaken, Yu Ge’er and Changsheng will come to your tent tonight."

Yun Chu wasn’t surprised at all.

That little Yu Ge’er had the empress invite her to Yan Mountain, he must want to cling to her every day.

It was only a few days, anyway. And something bad was about to happen. Staying with her would at least offer them some protection.

She was about to nod in agreement.

Suddenly, Cheng Xu and Qiutong rushed over from the distance.

"Your Highness, there are assassins!"

"Madam, this servant will escort you back to the tent!"

Yun Chu’s heart sank.

She hadn’t expected that the incident from her past life would happen on the very first night of the hunt.

"Cheng Xu, you escort Madam Xie."

Chu Yi left his most capable guard behind, then swiftly rushed toward the assassins.

Cheng Xu and Qiutong protected Yun Chu as they quickly returned to the tent.

The tent was already in chaos. Many noble ladies and young misses were pale with fear. The court’s high-ranking officials had gathered around the royal family, with a ring of Imperial Guards on the outer perimeter.

Yun Chu saw the two children huddled beside Consort Yin, guarded by a wet nurse, and finally relaxed.

"Chu’er, where did you go just now?" Lin Shi grabbed Yun Chu’s hand. "You scared me to death. I thought you’d been captured by the assassins."

"I felt stifled inside the tent, so I went out for some air." Yun Chu replied. "I’m sorry, Mother. I made you worry."

The crowd waited in the night, terrified, for about half an hour before the guards who had gone to chase the assassins finally returned in waves.

Leading them was Prince Pingxi, Chu Yi.

His horse stopped in front of the crowd. He dismounted and approached the emperor. "Your Majesty, this subject has captured three assassins alive. Bring them forward!"

The guards behind him dragged three tightly bound black-clad assassins and threw them to the ground.

"Brazen assassins, daring to attempt the life of His Majesty!" The usually wise and dignified empress flew into a rage. She picked up a teacup and smashed it against one of the assassins’ heads. "Speak! Who sent you?"

If not for a quick-witted young eunuch who had heard the commotion in time, the emperor might have died at Yan Mountain.

Though his life was spared, his arm had been cut by an assassin. The sight of the emperor’s blood was an omen of national misfortune, which was why the empress was so furious.

The assassins refused to speak, biting their tongues to silence.

Prince Gongxi walked forward and searched the assassins, pulling out a token from one of them. He presented it with both hands. "Your Majesty, please look."

As soon as the emperor saw the token, his expression changed drastically. "Isn’t this Prince Anjing’s token? Where is he? Where is he now?"

"Your Majesty, Prince Anjing also went with Prince Pingxi to chase the assassins just now." Consort De said in disbelief. "How could Prince Anjing’s token end up in the hands of an assassin? Something must have happened to him! Your Majesty, please send someone to find Prince Anjing!"

"Is that so?" Prince Gongxi spoke up. "After the hunt ended, I haven’t seen Prince Anjing at all. Sister-in-law, do you know where Prince Anjing went?"

Xie Pin took a moment to realize that Prince Gongxi was addressing her as "sister-in-law."

She hurriedly stepped forward from the crowd and, without thinking, said, "After the hunt, His Highness left the tent."

She had only found out from her maids that His Highness had left in a hurry. She had no idea where he went or what he was doing. She was a terrible princess consort.

She slightly lifted her head and met Consort De’s furious gaze.

It was only then that she belatedly realized; she had said the wrong thing.

Consort De had said that Prince Anjing had gone to chase the assassins, but she had said that he had left long ago...

Prince Gongxi cupped his hands toward the highest figure present. "Your Majesty, the most urgent matter now is to find Prince Anjing immediately."

The crown prince, his face grim, said, "Your Majesty, please allow this subject to personally interrogate these assassins."

The emperor’s expression was unreadable.

Only the empress knew that the emperor was furious to the extreme.

Ever since the emperor had ascended the throne decades ago, he had never encountered an assassination attempt. If he hadn’t been injured, it might have been fine, but now that blood had been drawn, this matter could not be taken lightly.

Chu Yi led his men in a thorough search of Yan Mountain for Prince Anjing.

Meanwhile, the crown prince and Prince Gongxi began interrogating the three captured assassins in full view of the crowd.

One of the assassins bit off his own tongue. If Prince Gongxi hadn’t reacted quickly, the other two would have also taken their own lives.

"You have committed a capital offense and deserve death, but not so easily."

The crown prince clapped his hands, and a eunuch from the Eastern Palace stepped forward, awaiting orders.

---

chapters.title: The Crown Prince Interrogates the Assassins
chapters.content:
The night was pitch black.

The cold moonlight shone on everyone’s faces.

By now, it was past midnight, yet most of those present had not the slightest hint of sleepiness. Only the half-grown children had fallen asleep in the arms of the servants.

The two assassins were bound to a long bench by the crown prince’s order, their faces turned upward.

The crown prince rolled up his sleeves and took a piece of paper, as thin as a cicada’s wing, from a basin of water on the ground. The soaked paper dripped water as he placed it directly over one of the assassins’ faces.

The surrounding officials and noblewomen did not yet understand what was happening.

But Prince Gongxi had already figured it out. He frowned in disapproval. "Your Highness, the Crown Prince, our dynasty rules with benevolence. This method is inappropriate..."

"This is an attempt on His Majesty’s life. When dealing with such vicious and evil men, there is no need to speak of benevolence." The crown prince said, "Second brother, come assist me."

Prince Gongxi had no choice but to step forward and, together with the crown prince, place the soaked paper over the faces of the two assassins.

At first, the two assassins didn’t understand what was happening. They even felt that the water on their faces was cool and refreshing. But soon, they began to suffer.

Their noses seemed blocked. No matter how hard they tried to breathe, only a tiny bit of air could get through, doing nothing to relieve the suffocating sensation.

"The prince here promises you both: whoever confesses first will be granted a quick death." The crown prince spoke slowly. "The one who remains stubborn... will enjoy this torture to the fullest."

Only then did the onlookers understand what was happening.

It turned out they were using paper and water to slowly suffocate the men. The process would take at least half an hour, truly a fate worse than death, where one could neither live nor die.

Many people whispered among themselves.

"His Highness’s method is clever. It will surely make the assassins talk."

"His Highness has always been known for his benevolence. How would he know such interrogation techniques?"

"This method may not draw blood, but it is extremely cruel..."

Standing in the crowd, Yun Chu thought of how, in her past life, the crown prince had frequently been targeted. It seemed to be because the crown prince’s usual behavior did not match the image people had of him.

The crown prince’s benevolence was a perfect image carefully crafted by the empress. But the crown prince himself was just an ordinary man, prone to mistakes, capable of unorthodox actions, slowly deviating from the prosperous path the empress had paved for him...

Even though she had died early, she could guess that the crown prince must have failed in the end.

Therefore, she had never considered having the Yun family support the crown prince...

"I confess! I confess!"

Under the gentle yet cruel torture, one of the assassins finally couldn’t bear it any longer and shouted hoarsely.

The crown prince’s face broke into a smile. He personally removed the paper from the assassin’s face.

"That token was given to me by General Mingwei. He told us to use the token as a secret signal to meet up and strike at the right opportunity!"

The crown prince frowned. Among the many military generals in the court, he only knew the names of the first and second-rank ones. This was the first time he had heard of General Mingwei.

Before he could speak, the outer guards suddenly stirred. Immediately afterward, a man in his forties was escorted forward.

"Are you General Mingwei?" The crown prince smiled. "Would you like to experience this for yourself?"

As soon as he finished speaking, the man prostrated himself on the ground, weeping bitterly. "Your Majesty... This subject was coerced! The prince has my elderly mother and children. This subject had no choice but to obey Prince Anjing’s orders. Otherwise, my family would be ruined..."

"You’re talking nonsense! Spouting lies!" Before he could finish, Consort De lifted her foot and kicked him over. She knelt down and said, "Your Majesty, Prince Anjing would never order such a treasonous act! He may be reckless, but regicide? Even if he had ten times the courage, he wouldn’t dare! Your Majesty, please investigate thoroughly and clear Prince Anjing’s name!"

The crown prince also knelt. "Your Majesty, last time when this subject was gravely ill, all evidence pointed to Prince Anjing. This time, the assassination attempt also implicates him..."

"Last time’s incident was already investigated by Your Majesty. It was a setup to frame Prince Anjing!" Consort De quickly interjected. "This time must also be General Mingwei colluding with someone behind the scenes to frame my son. He must be lying. Interrogate him properly, and the truth will come out!"

Prince Gongxi raised his eyes and looked at General Mingwei, who was kneeling on the ground.

General Mingwei slowly lifted his head and met Prince Gongxi’s gaze. His throat trembled involuntarily.

Suddenly, he stood up, his voice wild. "Yes, it was I who framed Prince Anjing! This matter has nothing to do with His Highness, nor with my family. It was I alone who plotted this rebellion and assassination. I am guilty, and I deserve to die! Your Majesty, this subject wishes to atone with his life!"

Before anyone could react, he drew a sword from a guard’s waist and thrust it into his own throat. Blood spurted out as he fell to the ground, dead.

Consort De was so frightened that her face turned ashen. She then shrieked, "Someone! Call the imperial physician! Save him! He cannot die!"

If he died, Prince Anjing’s guilt would be confirmed.

The empress coldly stated, "Consort De, the truth will be known once Prince Anjing is found."

Consort De’s heart twisted with a growing sense of foreboding.

Soon, Chu Yi galloped over on his horse. "Reporting to Your Majesty, this subject has searched all of Yan Mountain but found no trace of Prince Anjing. The men sent down the mountain have learned that villagers saw a young man fleeing west under the escort of dozens of people. After showing the villagers Prince Anjing’s portrait, they confirmed it was him."

"No, impossible!" Consort De crawled on her knees to the emperor’s feet. "Your Majesty, Prince Anjing is innocent. He would never do such a thing..."

The emperor, who had been silent all this time, suddenly stood up and kicked Consort De aside with his foot.

Xie Pin, standing nearby, was so shocked that she froze.

In her mind, Consort De had always been an untouchable figure, so noble, so arrogant in her presence. Yet now, she was sprawled on the ground, more insignificant than dust.

A malicious thought crossed Xie Pin’s mind: *Serves her right for being so arrogant. Now she’s getting her comeuppance.*

But she also knew that if Prince Anjing was proven guilty of the assassination attempt, her own fate would be no better than Consort De’s.

"Prepare the carriage. Return to the palace!" The emperor suppressed his anger, rose to his feet, and after a pause, said, "Old Three, you will remain at Yan Mountain. Turn every stone to find the man!"

Chu Yi accepted the order. "Yes, Your Majesty!"

"Old Two, take your men to Prince Anjing’s residence and search thoroughly." The emperor said in a deep voice, "If that unfilial son has long harbored patricidal intentions, there must be evidence!"

Prince Gongxi lowered his head to conceal the calculations in his eyes. "Yes, Your Majesty!"

The autumn hunting trip ended at the first watch of September 22nd.

The emperor returned to the palace, with the officials, noblewomen, and young ladies following behind the imperial procession. They didn’t arrive back in the capital until nearly dawn.

Yun Chu and Xie Shian returned to the Xie residence together.

As soon as they entered, Xie Jingyu came forward. "I heard there was an assassination attempt at Yan Mountain. What happened?"

"All evidence points to Prince Anjing." Xie Shian’s face was gloomy. "If he had acted sooner, it might have been fine, but he chose to arrange the assassination a month after Elder Sister’s marriage... If his guilt is confirmed, Elder Sister will likely... and our Xie family will also be affected."
